Alright ladies and gents, listen up. As someone with over 350 hours on record, I'm gonna give you the low down of this online game.
TLDR; the rolling system sucks, full of bugs, development cards suck, don't download or buy...yet.
So firstly, I must say that I am an avid Settlers of Catan player. I own every expansion available in the United States and play some form of the game at least once every couple of weeks. I've been playing for 17 years. I love the board game and have recently taken to trying variants such as Poverty is No Shame.
Secondly, I have so many hours because I always wanted to play more when I was growing up and now that I finally can play as much as I want...let's just say I've made up for lost time. Despite how many hours I have, I do not recommend this game in its current form. Why?
Cons:
1) The rolling system is trash. I've had games where more 12s were rolled than 6s, and games where not a single 5 was rolled the entire game. I understand probability (I have a Bachelor's Degree in Psychology) and I understand that true randomness means that the probability does not always line up with reality. That said, this game's randomness is often unbearable. Ie, sometimes 7 is the most common number rolled, meaning the game gets locked up for several rounds and no one produces anything. I've literally decided to stop putting the 7 on other players so that someone could produce something worth taking (talking 17+ sevens in a single game). I've had many other people comment about how they hate the rolling system too. It's something that can be fixed by using event cards, but you can't choose that option in matchmaking with human players, and I'm not interested in playing with AIs.
2) Bugs. Bugs everywhere. Like mating season for mosquitos on steroids. Sometimes a player is kicked for seemingly no reason. Sometimes a player is shown to be vacant but actually still there. Sometimes the game just locks up and you can't do anything about it. A token will often become way bigger than the others when the inventor card is played. Sometimes I'll go quite a while without matching to anyone (and we pay good money for good internet). You can read the other reviews to get more on this, obviously. Some people can't even play the game.
3) Development cards. Don't even get me started. I played a game today where another player played 3 Inventors in 2 turns, each of those turns being within 3 rounds. Excessive? Yes. So much. The problem with this is that your odds of winning come more down to the luck of the draw and less down to your own strategy. I believe the board game has a decent balance of the two, but this online game is just...well, you pretty much have to win some and lose some in my experience. I've had game where I got 3 or 4 alchemists and I've had games where I had level 4 showing on the commodity flipper and didn't get a single development card the whole game. It's way too unpredictable, which reduces your ability to strategize greatly.
4) It isn't exactly free. From what i can tell, the base game is, but none of the Avatar enhancements and none of the expansions are. It isn't expensive and I didn't mind paying whatever I paid for it (10$? 15$?), but it's trashy of the developers to mislead you.
5) The only current options are 3 or 4 player games. I'd like the option to play with up to 6 people and I'd especially like the option to play on the 5 and 6 player board with any amount of players. This isn't a big con, but it goes on the list nonetheless.
Now that I've laid out the immense flaws of the game, I'll give you the pros.
1) The chat function is nice and functional. Most people don't chat, but it's nice that it's there. Also, it has a whisper feature so that you can talk to just one opponent instead of all of them if you'd like - a nice touch.
2) The game is visually all that I want. Yes, the graphics look kind of mid 2000s esk, but the real game isn't exactly the dog and pony show.
3) It gives you all information at any point - scores, longest continuous road of each player, how many development cards they have, how many knights they have, etc. This is something that I wish could be easily integrated into a real game, but it just can't be.
4) The trading system works well. It  wasn't intuitive to me when I learned it, but it is really functional. You can do wild card trades so that you can just offer a wheat and see what people will give you (or vice versa). It tells you what your trade rate is for each resource and commodity, and it's a logical set up.
Summary:
Don't buy this game. The cons outweigh the pros right now and even if you're an avid Settlers fan like me, you'll be disappointed sooner or later with it. I think it has a lot of potential if the developers fix the problems I've mentioned above, but it definitely isn't worth it right now.

Back to the Future is my favourite science fiction trilogy, and after eagerly traversing all 5 episodes of this game, I must say it makes an inspiring and amusing sequel. Although not much effort was made to fill the environments with many citizens, as it would have been expected for a more realistic recreation of each era, the main characters, including new ones, are remarkably well polished in personality. The original ones were given the same personality and vibrance as in the films, in fact. In addition, Marty McFly feels just the way he's meant to be from the very beginning: a cool-yet-sloppy teenager. And even though he was played by a different voice actor, his voice sounds extremely similar to Michael J Fox's from a few decades ago.
The gameplay is quite similar to the Monkey Island series'. Attempting to slash the frustration of getting stuck, we are given a hint system that provides clues on demand without spoiling it immediately. These are entirely optional, so in general, it is a plus. Those who are used to the old sk00l point-and-click adventures may not need this anyway. The UI could have been made slightly better by adjusting the character movement by keyboard, which sometimes did not behave as expected. I also got myself into a strange bug in chapter 5, in which Marty may get into a place he's not expected to go to. Not saying where, but a reload doesn't hurt much here.
The story was both fascinating and touching in many parts. As Marty and Doc visit past and present instants of time, they find their own reality suddenly changing, often to the worse. It's like visiting the corrupted Hill Valley from Part 2, except that all alternate timelines are different, and they must figure out new ways to get back in time and save their reality. All this while helping past selves, avoiding running into other past selves, persuading alternative selves and making your opinion become heard on what spices to put on a week-old cabbage soup. Indeed.
I had relatively quick game sessions in this game, and now there isn't much reason to replay it. I guess these kind of games must come to an end, unless they make alternate endings like in The Walking Dead. I'm not sure whether I would have liked that in BttF, though. To conclude, I guess I'll go for 7.4/10. I would certainly send a friend back in time. *Back in Time song*

Here's few of the very many words one can use to describe this game: immersive, satisfying, and rewarding. It is immersive because of the graphics, the sound design, and all of these cool mechanics that make me feel like a true soldier. But most importantly, the community. The community to this game is sooo awesome! Aside from the few people that every multiplayer game has (I think you know what I'm talking about), the community does an equal, if not more, important role in showing you the ropes of the game and making you feel like you're in the heat of battle. This game has satisfied me, particularly because I have been subconsiously searching for this game most of my PC gaming "life" by playing games like Planetside 2, War Thunder, H1Z1 Just Survive (particularly because the DayZ experience in this game), and, if I daresay, even Battlefield. It is very rewarding because you spend at least the first 5-8 hours trying to figure out controls, get kills, and generally figure out the game's mechanics and physics. But please don' let this discourage you, because the feeling you get on your first kill is one of the most exciting moments I've ever had in a multiplayer PvP game!  Even if, and that is a big IF, you get bored of King of the Hill or Sector Control or any other "standard" game mode, there's still a wide range of unique and equally engaging modded servers. Again, the community serves as the backbone to this game. There are so many gameplay choices in this game that are exlusive to Arma's server list, a prime example being DayZ (which gave birth to a whole era of permadeath survival games). With this said, I can easily reccomend this game to two distinct groups of people: one being the serious gamer who is willing to spend time to learn a game and get a long time of fun, and the person who likes a large variation and value with just one purchase (albeit serveral mod downloads).

Overall, it was a very enjoyable experience. If you like Lovecraft and anything inspired by his work, it's pretty likely that you'll like this game. Do yourself a favor, if you want to be scared, don't watch too much gameplay beforehand. And definitely don't do what I did, and read the way the monsters behave in the game, because that kind of made them a lot less scary for me. Outlast is a game that handled the enemies a lot better, as far as the need to run and hide from them. But these monsters are still pretty creepy when you look at them. Even so, the game is good at building up tension and making you feel helpless. The puzzles are good, not too hard, not too easy. Oh, and play with headphones on and lights off. Instantly turns up the scare factor! It's not the most amazing game I've ever played, not even the most amazing horror game I've ever played, but it is definitely worth 8 hours of your time.

This game's artstyle is gorgeous, the music is amazing and the worldbuilding is superb. It is truly a work of art and every screen is a sight to behold.
So why do I not recommend it? Well, Pyre suffers from one fatal flaw that kills it: The core gameplay loop just isn't fun.
The core gameplay of this game is as follows: You read through a long (albeit enjoyable) story sequence where the characters play off each other and interact, taking few if any decisions. Then, you look to the sky is what looks like it should be a minigame but is actually a linear world map without mapping out the world. You arrive at the new area and take a mechanical choice between one of a few minor rewards, then you interact with your party some more and finally get to actually play what is essentially a very pretty game of soccer. The game markets itself as a party-based RPG, but in actuality it's a sports game. You must take a ball with one of your 3 characters and get it to the opponent's Pyre. The person holding the bal is defenceless. Every character that doens't hold the ball has an instakill radius around them, a ranged attack, a leap and a sprint. The matches themselves are quite easy and odn't have a lot of complexity to them. If the opponent has the ball, try to banish them, if you have the ball avoid opponents and get it to their Pyre. The customization options for the characters are quite limited and frankly unsatisfying to unlock. Furthermore, the matches are very short.
In short, this game's core loop is 15 minutes of mostly linear story followed by 5 minutes of not-great gameplay. Comparisons to Bastion and Transistor are inevitable. This game is clearly the inferior of the 3. That said, it is gorgeous.

Supergiant games has done it once again. To start off, this game is heavily story driven and alternates between the gameplay and the story, so if you're not into a mix of sports-like gameplay paired with a visual novel, then perhaps this game may not grab your attention.
Jumping right into the pros and cons as far as I have seen in my few hours of gameplay and light comparisons to Bastion and Transistor:
Pros:
1. The characters are very memorable. It's highly inclusive of you, the Reader, in the game, which is quite different from the way Transistor executed the character stories.
2. The gameplay portions are very unique and addicting, simply described as sports game mechanics with a twist. In addition, mixing team composition can make a huge difference in certain battles due to their individual perks and abilities.
3. The art is absolutely captivating and beautiful (as usual). It captures the feeling of each landscape perfectly and is just downright perfect background material.
4. The story still progresses even if you lose. For some this can be seen as a con, but for me it adds some element to replay value, which I will get into later.
5. There are different decisions you can make throughout the game, mostly limited to one or two, but they can affect character stats and how much purchasing power you have.
Cons:
1. The gameplay CAN get repetitive. Especially if you choose a certain composition and roll with it for many fights, it loses all aspects of the challenge. But a possible solution to this is to turn up difficulty.
2. The decisions still have some flaws. With the very few routes you can take to progress, most of them don't heavily hold any consequences and some can result in events that are mildly infuriating. SPOILERS:
3. While there is Versus mode, there is no online multiplayer mode. The developer themself addressed this:
Basically, Supergiant Games' focus has always been the story and it makes sense that they didn't go the online multiplayer route, but it still would have been a fantastic addition to the game to go head to head with a variety of different skilled players online.
After playing through the campaign and trying out the versus mode with a friend, the gameplay and controls are solid in both. The campagin really gives the Reader (you) a sense of haste and worry towards the end of the game
, which makes it feel much more real and immersive. Overall, I highly recommend this game! As with the differences between Bastion and Transistor, Pyre is a fitting addition as a unique standalone game to this Supergiant trio.
As mentioned before, there definitely is replay value that Pyre can offer, let it be attempting to win all Rites, or losing all Rites, or just seeing what could happen when taking other options that are limited. You begin to realize towards the end of the game that there are several different ways for the game to be played and your bigger decisions you made along the way add up to very different endings. Furthermore, the addition of Versus is an interesting aspect to developing player skills to test new combinations and strategies which was highly enjoyable for myself and my opponent.
Overall, Pyre is an absolute must-have, 10/10!

A simple puzzle game, Hook is quite fun, but make no mistake that it is short and simple - there's 50 puzzles, but the first 25 or so are simple tutorialising. I 100% completed the game in under an hour while watching a movie, and probably 20 minutes of that was spent on the last 7 or 8 puzzles. That said, for $1 I can't really fault the length of the game.
The mechanics are simple and intuitive, and tutorialised quite well, but there's only really one type of puzzle, meaning that the gameplay does stagnate a bit towards the end. By the last 3 levels I felt that it was getting slightly tedious, and that the gameplay was becoming more "stare at some lines" than actually puzzling, as most of the difficulty in the final levels was induced by the lines constantly swapping over each other.
The puzzle design isn't fantastic, but it's at least decent - the gameplay mechanics mean that none of the puzzles are unintuitive or seemingly unsolvable, enough time spent looking at it and following paths through will eventually reveal the solution, and successfully clearing half the lines off the screen at once is very satisfying.
All-in-all, a decent puzzle game that you probably won't be disappointed with considering the low price point, but nothing particularly special, either.

TL;DR: Minimalistic and nice but short, casual puzzle game about untangling hooks.
Rarely does a puzzle game start so leisurely. The first couple of levels of
are
to fail, their sole purpose being to demonstrate core mechanics. After all, a single hook cannot be tangled with itself.
In
bunch of abstract hooks are piled in an elaborate manner to present a puzzle. Your mission is to pick out all hooks one or few at a time without them getting stuck to each other in the process. Pressing a button, connected to a hook by a line, activates the hook to be removed. If it's not obstructed, you are one step closer to success.
is well designed. Success is usually not too difficult but it still feels satisfying as you solve a puzzle. All new features are introduced naturally by incredible simple and easy puzzles instead of bulky tutorials or manuals.
A couple of special features spice up the puzzles: there are rotating switches that control which hooks get activated; plus there are "antennae" that transfer the "hook activation signal" like teleporters. These add up to increasingly complicated puzzles.
Most puzzles admit no mistakes. Later on, once the puzzles get larger and more complicated, three mistakes are allowed. The difficulty curve is generally super. Music fits the game well, being a pleasant ambiance mixed with occasional sound of nature, e.g. a bird tweet or a stream.
Perhaps the only thing that the game really falls on is its length: the 50 levels can be beaten in a mere hour. Then again one hour of entertainment for one euro (or equivalent) is pretty adequate to me.

Is a machine possessing your consciousness you? Is it even human? Rarely a horror game can be this thought provoking, Frictional Games has done well again.
I have played Frictional Games games ever since Amnesia The Dark Descent. I really enjoyed Amnesia The Dark Descent, but wasn't able to enjoy Amnesia A Machine For Pigs just as much, and I'm currently playing Penumbra Overture too. I was afraid that the same thing would happen with SOMA, but it didn't.
Just like Amnesia and Penumbra series, you rely heavily on stealth, utilizing every means possible to ensure you do so. Frictional Games did well in creating tension through unsettling visual and background music, which in turn makes the players tense which adds to the tension itself. Simply put, the game uses the players' own fear to fuel their own fear.
There are many variations of enemies in this game, even more than Amnesia and Penumbra series, each with their own powers and weaknesses, patterns and behaviours. And I loved it. I enjoyed every second of thinking "how do I get past it?" Having to find out how each of them behaves, and actually getting past each of them, is also a part of the tension.
Verdict: A must buy for those who enjoy true horror games
Frictional Games, through this game, has AGAIN raised the bar for every other horror games. This game is what horror games should be. This game is why horror games should be separated from cheap trashes full of jumpscare.

A nice little turn based tactical squad shooter. Gameplay is in the title, you're counter terrorists breaching an area and clearing it out.
It gets a little more complicated than that of course, who goes in first, what weapon they're equipped with, how long you look at an area, you plan it out hit "Breach" and watch it all go to plan. Or all go to hell if you didn't take into account a possible sniper.
It's not as good as Frozen Synapse, but FS is on a whole other level compared to most games and a lot of people find find FS a bit
cereberal. For those who want the challenge of planning but don't want to start counting miliseconds and take every single possible combination into account, Breach And Clear is for you. It's thoughtful enough to be a challenge, with a clean UI, reasonable customisation, a nice learning curve, and enough maps to keep you busy for a while.
You unlock weapons with stars, you get stars from clearing maps on each difficulty. 4 stars for a good clear on Easy, on Normal, on Hard, on Insane, on... Elite? Either way, when you see firearms that need 400 stars to unlock it isn't as bad as it looks as when you clear a map on Hard, it automatically registers as cleared on Easy and Normal as well. 12 stars for once through.
Your units level up and you can apply their stats wherever you want, there's six classes to choose from, four in a squad, and yes you can run four of the same type. Should you? Well that depends on your playstyle. Four Direct Action units with different weapons can be one hell of a rush. Literally, lots of sprinting and shotguns in that style. Those damnable snipers never saw it coming.
Max level of 30, turn perma death on and you'll hit 30 by the time you're through your third country (7 countries, 5 areas each, three game modes (Clear, Defuse, Escape), that's 105 different runs you can make before it gets repetitive, 120 with DLC), which gives you plenty of time to start on another squad or three.
Each class is balanced, Direct Action and Intelligence are fun as rushers and ninjas/scouts respectively, Medic's make sure no-one goes down, Breachers have a thing for grenades, Weapons Sgt can suppress, and Fireteam Leader's give everyone bonus everything, but none of them are clear winners. It depends more on playstyle than game stats.
Reasonable amount of guns. I'd have preferred more, and more variety, as well as grenade launchers, rocket launchers, etc, but it's not bad.
It's definitely a port, there's a little too much clicking when equipping mods to weapons, but it's laid out nicely so there's that.
Seven squad types, eight with DLC, each of them give bonus points to certain stats so again there's no clear winner. Simply go with the one that fits your playstyle or which you find the prettiest of them all.
If you don't like the idea of a tactical turn based squad shooter, then this is going to suck. For those who do enjoy the genre or would like a nice entry point to it, Breach And Clear is it. And afterwards if you feel like more of a challenge, Frozen Synapse it is; because chess was just too easy.
9/10, worth full price, DLC worthwhile.

I think I've found a new favorite sidescroller; it isn't all that often that one of those comes around where I don't roll my eyes and leave it after the first half hour.
Pros:
- Story. The story strays into the cliche at times, but otherwise is wonderfully crafted and engaging
- Voice acting. This is something plenty games, especially sidescrollers, lack. The voice acting is spot on
- Depth. The game has plenty locations to explore and plenty treasures to find, keeping the player interested and roaming
- Accuracy. This is something I didn't expect, but the game tosses out old terms and quotes from the Greek poets and        Homer with astonishing regularity. This really helps the world connect back to the ancient Greek roots, unlike plenty other that wore the "Ancient Greek" label.
- Varied Gameplay. Instead of being same-old, shoot-this kill-that, the game actively switches it up between puzzles, races, platforming challenges, and kill-them-all brawls interspersed with the occassional boss fight or conversation with an NPC. This helps it stay fresh for longer and is a welcome addition
- Music. While it may not be to everyone's tastes, the music is hauntingly beautiful if somewhat repetitive after a time
- Balance. This sort of game always has trouble balancing between frustratingly dificult and too easy. Apotheon manages it. There were definitely moments of sheer panic where I felt like I was being crushed, but these never crossed the line into an annoyingly hard fight.
- Replayability. The first run through, without seeking out side quests or the like, on the easiest settings, takes about 12 hours. Have fun. I persume it will take another 12 on the next difficulty, and a lot more than that on Olympian.
Cons:
- Controls. Yes, let's talk about the one major failing that this game has; the controls. They aren't all that bad, but suffer on two points: Firstly, platforming is a bit of a nuisance. The game makes you stick to any climbable surface you touch, theoretically making platform puzzles easier but also slowing you down at inopportune moments. Furthermore, archery and thrown weapons are the slightest bit inaccurate and hard to master early on.
- Tutorial. The first mission is in essence a tutorial mission. It gives you all the basics, but no more, leaving you to puzzle out the rest on your own. Where do I get more crafting recipes? Wait, my weapons can break? Can I repair them? These questions and more are left to the player to decipher. On the one hand, this can be enjoyable if the player enjoys the challenge and the thrill of discovering something new. On the other, people who want to jump straight in may suffer a few mishaps - I myself ended up fighting a boss with only one spear as my other weapons had worn down.
Despite the slightly sticky controls and the imperfect tutorial, this game is still excellent. If you enjoy sidescrollers, story-driven adventure games, or Greek mythology, this game is a perfect fit and I anticipate having a lot of fun with it.

This game is very entertaining! - at least at first. I am only 44 days (of in-game time) in, so I may not give the most experienced review. I am glued to the game and my day evaporated in a flash because I was so entertained and kept busy with all the maintenance and expedition updates. I love how the game is controller-friendly, an the customization of your family and pet is great.
However, I feel that the random encounters are limited. It's always the same few things, either someone wants to fight, or trade and join your bunker. Perhaps more interesting things will happen in the future, but I really think the game needs more interesting things to happen.
Perhaps more interaction with the locations you visit. Such as a choice of areas of a big factory to search (bossess office, factory floor, supply room, etc), a chance of traps and other dangers depending on the room and a random time limitation that forces you to choose all or less of those rooms. For instance your character sees a gang of cannibals coming and feels they only have time to check one room, if you choose two or more you may have to fight your way out.
Also I don't think areas you've visited should have their items replenish so fast. It makes things WAY too easy. Why not have NPCs take over a building at random too, and have them defend their items?
All in all this game is well-worth the price and I look forward to the coming updates. I pray modding is made-easy in the future as this game offers an incredible opportunity for expansion. It's even better than I thought it would be.

Considered by many to be the best horror game ever made and the horror game that made the genre what it is today, I have to say I was a little disappointed.
I'll start with what makes the game good:
The atmosphere is probably the best thing about the game. The music and environments and just different ambient sounds create the perfect atmosphere for the game. It is probably the biggest contributer to the scare factor of the game.
Now my issues with the game:
Firstly, the story is actually really good. It is disturbing and interesting. My issue with it is that, the game doesn't explain what is going on and to truly understand the whole story, you are forced to read diary entries and notes scattered throughout the game and even then, they are cryptic at times.
Secondly, the gameplay. The sanity meter, I feel, detracts from the overall experience. I know that it sort of makes sense but it just gets annoying most of the time since not paying attention to it just ends up in your screen going all wobbly. I also don't need to be told when I'm feeling scared.
Lastly, the monsters themselves just aren't that scary. I was more scared in the parts before the monsters arrived when I didn't know if they would be around the next corner or the one after that. This just built up tension and was the most effective at being scary. When the monster's actually arrived however, the game just became a stealth game where you just couldn't fight back.
Even though this review has been mostly negatives, I would still recommend the game if you are looking for a decent horror game. It is worth getting when it is on sale and is worth putting in some time even if it is just to try out the horror game genre.

I originally played this game back in 2012/2013 (It was one of those years). I decided to reinstall and play it again for Halloween 2017. Let me just say, this is by far the best horror game I have played in my time. The castle you explore is very spooky and will make you hesitant to progress on. The sound effects are very well made. The creatures you encounter among your journey are disturbing, and surely will send chills down your spine. The game does a great job at story telling by providing notes and flashbacks giving us insight to the events that have occurred between the characters. The sanity system is a great feature which will make you plan your steps carefully, otherwise you will find yourself in a very bad state of mind making the game even more terrifying. Throughout the game you will search for oil to add to that trusty lantern you hold, and tinderboxes to ignite the light sources you find around the environment. The puzzles are satisfying and can be tricky at first, but don't worry you can always check a guide if you get stuck. You can finish the game in about 6-8 hours (First playthrough in mind, no speedrunning). The game has 3 endings, which for some may encourage you to play through the game again. Custom Stories is a great addition, adding new content and more hours of gameplay for those who seek even more horror. I highly recommend this game to anyone who is brave enough to play it.

Ok, i am going to try to make this as explanitory as possible, for anyone thinking about buying this game.  Iwill start with listing the pros cons and some of the mixed parts of this game.
Pros!
Graphics, even on medium, are absolutely amazing, from the drinking to eating to biting to running the dinosaur's animations are Beautiful, as are the siple but efective blowing grass, swaying branches and foliage decoration.
The sound effects, all of the Dinosaur's calls seem to fit perfectly with the creature and the ambient sound effects that surround you and how distance affects how Dinosaur's calls sound to you are simply superb.
The general displays such as how you select dinosaurs, how the menus look and feel are so smooth and function extremely well.
Cons...
As amazing as this game is, it does have its flaws, as do all games.
The way of installing and uninstalling mods can seem very back and forth involving subscribing, enabling then restarting for the mod to make things work, then having to reverse everything to play normally, can consume a lot of time when traversing through multiple different mods.
The speed of filling up food and drink is extremely time consuing as you have to stand there holding the E button down for over 2 minutes to fill up your water, which can make it almost impossible to refuel anywhere where there is at least 1 hostile player.
Mixed:
The dev team have repeatedly shown how devoted they are to this game, and I do not understand how people still hold grudges against them, there have been multiple times where they have been rather unpleasant but in every situation where I have seen this happen, they have thoroughly apologised for their actions, and do thank their community more often than you think, whether they respond to faq quickly, and patch issues in the game as fast as they can.
The community, I put this in mixed as there are those few players who hold grudges, such as on the NightShine DM server, the DeathMatch part is often overlooked, and as soon as somene kills they have 5 overprotective spinos and acros pouncing on them over and over and over no matter what you do. On the other end of the spectrum, most of the community is helpful, devoted and ready to give a hand when required, from making almost any type of guide t answering simple questions, s many of the people in this community are ready to help!
I hope this Review has helped you understand this game, or helped you decide whether to get this game or not, If you love dinosaurs and want to be one in progression, and work your way up, sandbox, and choose whatever you want to be and mess around with no risks, (except for getting lost!) or survival (which I've never played xD ) and you have a little patience fr the small issues here and there, then I fully reccomend this game to you!!

There's a lot of things wrong with this game. The two biggest ones are the fact that your enemy AI is insanely perceptive at any difficulty and directly because of that, playing as a sniper quickly diminishes since they'll quickly try to overrun you. I don't know if that's a design choice, but it definitely doesn't allow much room for fun.
There are a few moments where you can maintain stealth, but eventually you'll be found out whether it's killing someone too close to another person or just them discovering another body, but once that happens, the AI will bumrush your position and you'll end up in close quarters combat. There's no way to displace because the AI will know where you are forever the moment you are discovered.
On the other hand, sniping is incredibly deep and rewarding. Your breathing pattern (which changes depending on how much you've moved), wind strength and direction, bullet drop and some other things I probably missed all are taken into factor with each shot, making every bullet valuable.
Traps are also fun to set up. Knowing your enemy is just going to storm you once you've blown your cover, you can place traps across the field, bottlenecking, ambushing and creating death corridors for them.
Sniper Elite V2 is a fun game, but if you really want to appreciate it, you have to invest more hours than an average playthrough time. If you didn't get this for free when Rebellion offered it as a promotion, don't ever get it. It's fun, but it just didn't stick with me.

I don't normally buy early release games, but I seen this game on youtube, and it looked like a really fun game to simply mess around in.
I decided to pick it up it kept my amusement for 2-3 hours easily. There isn't a whole lot you can do, but certainly enough to keep you amused for awhile. And I guess there is mod support as well, once you do get bored of everything that comes with the game by default. There are different "Scenarios" (which I haven't played them all yet) or you could just free roam across different landscapes. (Again I haven't played every map yet). There are several different cars or trucks by default, including semi trucks and trailers. Trailers are fully functional, with physical properties as well. You can couple them/decouple them, open their doors, etc.
You can play with different environment setting, like gravity. Ever tried going off-roading on Jupiter?
The physics (which I think needs some work) is still pretty impressive. Just about every part of a real car is actually part of your car, and has physical properties. It is fun driving intentionally into a brick wall as fast as possible to watch your car crumble into a pancake.
Another thing that I found interesting is, you can also "grab" just about any part of your car. I've spent about 30 minutes alone just flinging my car around to see what happens, or stripping the car down to bare bones (and somehow still driving it).
One thing I was really surprised (since it is early access) about is support for steering wheels. I have a Logitech G29 steering wheel with pedals (including clutch pedal). I didn't had to configure anything, and the game figured out that I had a steering wheel (which I find much more easier to use than mouse + keyboard). The game also registers feedback to the steering wheel, so driving older cars without power steering = a lot of steering resistance, pretty realistic in that sense. However, I noticed that some vehicles had no feedback whatsoever. I don't have the H shifter so I don't if the game supports that yet.
If there was one thing I would like to see in this game, is multiplayer support. I can see myself messing around in this game with a friend or two for hours. Setting up races, or challenges, or destruction derby!
If I were to criticize one thing, it is the camera control. The camera control could do some improvement. Feels unintuitive, and the camera likes to return to odd positions.
The game isn't very well optimized, I normally play games in 4K resolution, but in this game I was getting low FPS at 4k res. Going down to 1080P resolved the FPS issues for me. This is not a huge issue really, just something I noticed when I first started.
Overall this game is really fun to mess around, and it definitely has some potential. I can't wait to see a more polished version and updates.

Survarium - "STALKER's spiritual successor".
I've been playing on and off for~ a year(?) now, ever since late closed alpha and it definitely has improved a lot.
There's a lot of things I like about the game like level design, how the weapons feel and the atmosphere.
Currently, the game only has PVP in it, but sometime this year (Q3-4), the 'Freeplay' mode will be added to the game.
PVP has 3 modes at the moment:
-Team Deathmatch
-A gamemode where you collect containers of files(?) scattered around the map, and bring them to your base
-A conquest type gamemode where you capture research devices and protect them, so the enemy can't capture them
The way you acquire items in the game is made pretty well in my opinion.
You find random items (useable items like medkits or weapons and armor) after every match you play
OR
You can complete missions which increase your rank in faction so you can buy the items from the in-game shop.
There are 4 factions in the game
-Scavengers
-Black Market
-Fringe Settlers
-Renaissance Army
You can be a member of a single faction only, unless you leave for a different faction. Your progress will not reset for the faction you left.
Overall, I think the game is pretty alright, it has cons like premium currency but that's the F2P model.
Just give it some time and remember it isn't STALKER 2.
My score out of 10 for the game is 7/10.

Not for everyone, and not a STALKER 2
I just installed steam version (and now the game runs for me better than ever - 60fps ftw), but I've played since the closed beta (v0.16b - that's from back in december 2013) with countles (200+) hours on record.
Most complaints I see people have about the game itself (and not the technical issues) come from this - it's not a STALKER game, and it definitivly feels different than most, if not all, other multiplayer shooters.
Movement is different, gunplay is different.
It has couple of skill trees - it's supposed to feel sluggish untill you level up properly, and even then it feels (to me, at least) more realistic than a lot of other shooters in terms of movement.
It only has PvP, but PvE is coming even though it might seem like a carrot on a stick for a lot of alpha/closed beta/open beta testers (they never promised anything, but PvE was planned for the 4th quartal of 2014).
There should be much more stuff added in every sphere of the game, and it's far from done, so be aware that my approval is more of a "positive expectations" than a proper "this game is 10/10" recomendation, but I will certanly play more of it, unless it becomes a pay 2 win game.
Some might say that it seems to be the case even now, but that's just on paper - in reality I feel that it really isn't p2w yet - I feel that you can get superior weapons from in-game currency than from real money, and even if you have an enemy with supperior weapon, it feels to me like you'll be able to hold your own with a touch of skill or luck.
I do not believe in buying games untill they're done - I haven't spent a single € on this game, and I never felt that the somebody was better then me because he/she payed for it. It always came down to skill - as soon as I got in the zone with any of my guns, I quickly became one of the top 2-3 players in a match, win or loose, and that's even with tier 2 guns in a tier 12 match.
Skill trees for gunplay, movement (implemented), survival - traps and such, healing, and anomaly traversing (not yet implemented), 15 levels of gear, interesting maps, great immersion... what's there not to like (except for bugs, glitches, optimisation and the game not being finished)?
Still a great co-op game !

One of the deepest video games I've ever experienced, and that's not just because it takes place on the ocean floor.

There are very few horror stories that I just don't want to end, and SOMA is definitely one of them. A must play for gamers, non-gamers, horror lovers, horror haters alike. Every one should play this game.

I'm not sure if it's just for Windows 8 users, but I definitely had some trouble running this game as-is. I did finally manage to get it working (by hitting the home key right as DOSBox began and then going back into the game), but I ran into lag and sound issues.
If anyone is experiencing any sort of problems with any Doom I or II games on Steam, the best way to fix it is to download ZDOOM (a newer engine that runs Doom just like it was played originally, but with higher resolution and more options) and copy all the files into the directory where "dosbox.exe" is. To get to the game's folder easier, you can just right click it from the Steam games list, click properties, and then find "Browse local files...". Delete the original dosbox.exe file, and then rename zdoom.exe to dosbox.exe, so Steam will recognize it and automatically run it for you every time. This will make sure it runs your Doom .wads on every computer without trouble. If this helped you, please give this review a thumbs up to help spread the word. Thanks! :) Anyways, that aside, onto the review:
I'll make it short and sweet. Doom is one of the best first person shooter video games to this day. Wayyyy way back in the early 90s, id Software revolutionized the FPS genre with Wolfenstein 3D, and then ultimately cemented it into gaming as we know it with the release of the first Doom. It plays very well, even to this day (although you may have to adjust some controls for maximum precision and more comfort). You'll have fun running through each level, blasting zombies and imps to pieces with anything from a pistol to a shotgun, all the way to a chaingun or a BFG. Don't look the acronym up, kids. And those aren't all the weapons the game has, either. I won't spoil it for you, though. There are loads of enemies to do battle with, and all the levels are extremely complex. There will be doors opening behind you, keycards that you need to find in order to get to the next room, secret hidden hallways, etc. The music is perfect in all its MIDI glory. The modding community has always been faithful. Check out Brutal Doom if you want to know what I'm talking about. I mainly bought the entire Classic Complete pack just to have the WADs legally. That's right, lawyers and PC haters. Not all of us just sit around pirating games all day. If we really love it, we'll buy it. Anyways, with these WADs, you can copy them directly from your Steam folder and use them on other source ports for features such as playing multiplayer on modern servers, upgrading the graphics/resolution, and, of course, modding. There are also methods of creating your very own WADs, which is one thing that's made Doom such a popular game. It has stood the test of time for 2 decades, and I see it going for even more than that. It's a classic. Just like Super Mario Bros., Sonic The Hedgehog, and The Legend of Zelda. Definitely pick this one up. I have no complaints for this version of the game, other than what I said about it possibly not working for everyone's machines when first downloaded. But follow my guide up there, and you'll have it fixed in minutes. It's really easy, even for those not tech savvy.

Funnily enough, a few weeks before learning about Apotheon for the first time, I had a similar idea for a Metroidvania-style game stylized to look like ancient artwork, only Egyptian-style instead of Greek. Not terribly relevant, just noting what got me enthused to play Apotheon in the first place.
The basic premise of Apotheon is that Zeus has grown tired of mankind's continuous degeneration, and has decided to call do-over and wipe the Earth clean of mortalkind, and decrees that the gods of Olympus will withdraw their favor. Crops won' grow, sun won't shine, the forests are empty of game, etc. After fending off some desperate raiders in the opening tutorial, Hera bids you to travel to Olympus and take back what the gods have deprived your people of by force. One thing leads to another and you find yourself going head to head with Zeus himself in the climactic battle.
Apotheon's being drawing point is definitely its artstyle. The entire game is made to look like Greek pottery art come to life, and it gives the game an identity all is own that serves the tone of the game perfectly. Gameplay wise there isn't much to talk about, pretty typical Metroidvania fare, and in the end I only have three major complaints:
1. Weapon degradation has never improved a game. I imagine it was mostly added to force players to try out the different weapons in the game (there's a lot of them), but all it did was make me focus on using the worst weapons in my arsenal just so they'd break and get off the list. Breakable shields is more understandable, but generally speaking iron is slightly more sturdy than carboard and tinfoil.
2. The game tends to take more than it gives, which made me resort to farming on more than a few occasions. Farming is for survival games and MMOs. Otherwise it just indicates poor resource distribution.
3. The Caduceus of Hermes, while a fun exploration tool, also reveals a number of clumsy level borders, as the developers never intended those areas to be accessed. Many of these are one-way trips and can lead to falling out of the map entirely. I get the feeling the Caduceus was added to the game partway through development and the rest of the game wasn't built with it in mind.
All in all these are only mild niggles in what is otherwise a beautiful and engaging Metroidvania title. Definitely give it a go.

This game might be fun if it weren't completely and utterly broken. I don't use those terms lightly either. This may be, hands down, the most fundamentally broken game in my Steam library (about 350 games and counting). I don't care if you get it for 90% off. It's not worth a penny.
I loved the Guild 1 and I knew the Guild II had a reputation of being janky (rough around the edges). From a technical standpoint it lived up to that reputation. I get a black screen when loading even though I can space bar through it to get to the main menu. The game stutters on my PC. Mouse clicks don't register and there's the normal clipping and other graphical issues that I'd expect.
What I didn't expect was the economic model to be broken. For a game where that's the majority of the game, that's kind of a fatal flaw. Here's a case in point. I have started as a smith on two separate maps. I must buy raw materials from the market and create finished goods. The problem is that the finished goods get cheaper and cheaper but the raw materials almost never replenish - and if they do it's at a cost higher than the finished goods.
When you have a smithy you can only start by building 2 items. That's it. Everything you make takes iron. When iron starts costing 50+g per bar, you can't make money. There are a couple of mines scattered around the map. Guess what? They never sell any iron. Same goes for charcoal. Wood isn't quite as bad but ultimately it's the same thing. So once you make one or two batches of goods you can't make any more. I fast forwarded through TWO YEARS of gametime and the iron went from 50g to 48g. This isn't going to help.
At that point it's literally game over. Since everything takes money - this is an economic simulator after all - this is the end of the game unless you want to sit there and listen to the background music. To use a phrase from the olden days, this game is a coaster. I figured I was doing something wrong so I asked on the forum. Guess what? It was confirmed the game is simply that broken.
This is the equivalent of a space flight game where they forgot to put engines in the spaceships. Or a game like Civilization where building a new unit takes 1,000 turns instead of 6 or 8. There's a mod out there that supposedly fixes this. I may download it and if it fixes this issue I might actually get to play the game I purchased. But when the game is broken in that obvious of a manner then there's no way to ever recommend it no matter how much a user-made mod fixes things.
EDIT - Tried the megamod. Same results. No goods in the market. Uninstalled. What a waste of potential.

This game is absolutely amazing. It has the perfect balance of horror and puzzle solving. Everything about this game is fun and interesting. One tip is to play slowly. It is much easier to immerse yourself in the story and the horror if you don't rush through the game. The lore is supremely supplemented by finding notes and memoirs of the protagonist, the antagonist, and more.
I have found this game to be a bit weaker on subsequent playthroughs because you can solve puzzles much more quickly, but the horror elements of the game are such that repeat playthroughs can still be quite scary and different. This game does not go for the cheap thrills of jumpscares, but sustained, tense horror that continues well after the initial scare with chase scenes, and plenty of hiding and using the environment to your advantage.
* Minor mechanics spoiler ahead. *
My main criticism of the game would be the hard transitions from horror to puzzle sections. I can understand that you should get breaks to relax a little bit and solve some puzzles, but knowing almost every puzzle section is completely devoid of enemies makes them break immersion a little bit. I also think that your sanity drains far too quickly. I have played through this game probably 9 or 10 times, and even when I absolutely FLY past most of the game that I already know how to solve or effectively/quickly pass up enemy encounters, I find that the effects of low sanity can be a bit of a detriment to gameplay. However, this does make sense, as immersing yourself in the castle can be quite unsettling for you and your character, so sanity is always on the brink of being lost.
* End minor spoilers. *
Despite my criticisms, this is still my favorite horror game of ALL TIME, by far. Every person I have shown or recommended it to has thought the same. I am not into number-rating systems, but if I were forced to give one, 10/10, in every department.
Buy it for yourself, and your friends. You will get more than your money's worth of entertainment in the main story, user-made custom stories, and some replay value.

This game's artstyle is gorgeous, the music is amazing and the worldbuilding is superb. It is truly a work of art and every screen is a sight to behold.
So why do I not recommend it? Well, Pyre suffers from one fatal flaw that kills it: The core gameplay loop just isn't fun.
The core gameplay of this game is as follows: You read through a long (albeit enjoyable) story sequence where the characters play off each other and interact, taking few if any decisions. Then, you look to the sky is what looks like it should be a minigame but is actually a linear world map without mapping out the world. You arrive at the new area and take a mechanical choice between one of a few minor rewards, then you interact with your party some more and finally get to actually play what is essentially a very pretty game of soccer. The game markets itself as a party-based RPG, but in actuality it's a sports game. You must take a ball with one of your 3 characters and get it to the opponent's Pyre. The person holding the bal is defenceless. Every character that doens't hold the ball has an instakill radius around them, a ranged attack, a leap and a sprint. The matches themselves are quite easy and odn't have a lot of complexity to them. If the opponent has the ball, try to banish them, if you have the ball avoid opponents and get it to their Pyre. The customization options for the characters are quite limited and frankly unsatisfying to unlock. Furthermore, the matches are very short.
In short, this game's core loop is 15 minutes of mostly linear story followed by 5 minutes of not-great gameplay. Comparisons to Bastion and Transistor are inevitable. This game is clearly the inferior of the 3. That said, it is gorgeous.

Supergiant games has done it once again. To start off, this game is heavily story driven and alternates between the gameplay and the story, so if you're not into a mix of sports-like gameplay paired with a visual novel, then perhaps this game may not grab your attention.
Jumping right into the pros and cons as far as I have seen in my few hours of gameplay and light comparisons to Bastion and Transistor:
Pros:
1. The characters are very memorable. It's highly inclusive of you, the Reader, in the game, which is quite different from the way Transistor executed the character stories.
2. The gameplay portions are very unique and addicting, simply described as sports game mechanics with a twist. In addition, mixing team composition can make a huge difference in certain battles due to their individual perks and abilities.
3. The art is absolutely captivating and beautiful (as usual). It captures the feeling of each landscape perfectly and is just downright perfect background material.
4. The story still progresses even if you lose. For some this can be seen as a con, but for me it adds some element to replay value, which I will get into later.
5. There are different decisions you can make throughout the game, mostly limited to one or two, but they can affect character stats and how much purchasing power you have.
Cons:
1. The gameplay CAN get repetitive. Especially if you choose a certain composition and roll with it for many fights, it loses all aspects of the challenge. But a possible solution to this is to turn up difficulty.
2. The decisions still have some flaws. With the very few routes you can take to progress, most of them don't heavily hold any consequences and some can result in events that are mildly infuriating. SPOILERS:
3. While there is Versus mode, there is no online multiplayer mode. The developer themself addressed this:
Basically, Supergiant Games' focus has always been the story and it makes sense that they didn't go the online multiplayer route, but it still would have been a fantastic addition to the game to go head to head with a variety of different skilled players online.
After playing through the campaign and trying out the versus mode with a friend, the gameplay and controls are solid in both. The campagin really gives the Reader (you) a sense of haste and worry towards the end of the game
, which makes it feel much more real and immersive. Overall, I highly recommend this game! As with the differences between Bastion and Transistor, Pyre is a fitting addition as a unique standalone game to this Supergiant trio.
As mentioned before, there definitely is replay value that Pyre can offer, let it be attempting to win all Rites, or losing all Rites, or just seeing what could happen when taking other options that are limited. You begin to realize towards the end of the game that there are several different ways for the game to be played and your bigger decisions you made along the way add up to very different endings. Furthermore, the addition of Versus is an interesting aspect to developing player skills to test new combinations and strategies which was highly enjoyable for myself and my opponent.
Overall, Pyre is an absolute must-have, 10/10!

A great concept that was unfortunately horribly executed by a largely incompetent development team and greedy company. Sadly the game will likely sink to its bare number of players long before the first character pack comes out, and by then it'll be too late to bother.
+ Atmosphere is fantastic

= Combat is brutal and
the mechanics actually work

- Peer-to-peer connections. Absolutely unforgivable in a game that so strongly focuses on precise timing, position, and prediction.
- Matchmaking is pretty much useless, as it results in stacked matches, endless searching, and random dumps.
- Community features are very basic and largely useless. Parties are broken up if matchmaking fails, after a match you get dumped to the map (and removed from party) if there isn't enough players to continue.
- Certain mechanics are rediculously broken. Guardbreaks are super easy to spam, not so easy to counter. Revenge builds build full revenge within a couple of blows, and players can pop Revenge to double their health, damage, and don't use stamina while it's up.
- The community is obsessed with "fair fights" but stupidly queues for matches that encourage anything but.
- Steel gain is painfully slow, and prices of unlockables are sky high.

I don't normally buy early release games, but I seen this game on youtube, and it looked like a really fun game to simply mess around in.
I decided to pick it up it kept my amusement for 2-3 hours easily. There isn't a whole lot you can do, but certainly enough to keep you amused for awhile. And I guess there is mod support as well, once you do get bored of everything that comes with the game by default. There are different "Scenarios" (which I haven't played them all yet) or you could just free roam across different landscapes. (Again I haven't played every map yet). There are several different cars or trucks by default, including semi trucks and trailers. Trailers are fully functional, with physical properties as well. You can couple them/decouple them, open their doors, etc.
You can play with different environment setting, like gravity. Ever tried going off-roading on Jupiter?
The physics (which I think needs some work) is still pretty impressive. Just about every part of a real car is actually part of your car, and has physical properties. It is fun driving intentionally into a brick wall as fast as possible to watch your car crumble into a pancake.
Another thing that I found interesting is, you can also "grab" just about any part of your car. I've spent about 30 minutes alone just flinging my car around to see what happens, or stripping the car down to bare bones (and somehow still driving it).
One thing I was really surprised (since it is early access) about is support for steering wheels. I have a Logitech G29 steering wheel with pedals (including clutch pedal). I didn't had to configure anything, and the game figured out that I had a steering wheel (which I find much more easier to use than mouse + keyboard). The game also registers feedback to the steering wheel, so driving older cars without power steering = a lot of steering resistance, pretty realistic in that sense. However, I noticed that some vehicles had no feedback whatsoever. I don't have the H shifter so I don't if the game supports that yet.
If there was one thing I would like to see in this game, is multiplayer support. I can see myself messing around in this game with a friend or two for hours. Setting up races, or challenges, or destruction derby!
If I were to criticize one thing, it is the camera control. The camera control could do some improvement. Feels unintuitive, and the camera likes to return to odd positions.
The game isn't very well optimized, I normally play games in 4K resolution, but in this game I was getting low FPS at 4k res. Going down to 1080P resolved the FPS issues for me. This is not a huge issue really, just something I noticed when I first started.
Overall this game is really fun to mess around, and it definitely has some potential. I can't wait to see a more polished version and updates.

What else is there to say about Doom? If you haven't played it you should.
Doom is the forefather of all modern first-person shooters. Its controls are tight, its level design remains some of the best ever achieved in the industry, its music is legendary, and the shotgun blast remains iconic in the world of shooters.
The story is simple, but standard for 1993 games. It begins in the Hangar of the Phobos moon base as the Doomguy fights his way through the forces of hell before arriving on the lost Deimos base. He has to fight his way through even tough challenges here and take down the vile Cyberdemon before descending into Hell itself.
The first nine levels of Doom were released as shareware in 1993. It set a benchmark that future games would dream of reaching. It also had one of the first modding scenes in PC gaming.
Speaking of mods, one of the downsides to Doom, especially the Steam version, is that the controls and settings haven't aged all that well. Thus, I'd recommend using a launcher. I personally use GZDoom, which you can find
.
There are other mods that add to the already awesome and timeless gameplay of Doom, specifically the
. This mod adds additional shooting gameplay and a whole lot more blood to the game.
If you are a gamer. Specifically a shooter gamer, you absolurely cannot do much better than Doom.

Apparently, from what I hear from other fellow "reviewers", this is one of those Telltale games before the heavy-hitters like "The Walking Dead" and "The Wolf Among Us", and as such, you would expect certain nuances of this game, contextual to its development, compared to the general expectations these days.
Having said that, I'm not a big graphics man, and I generally don't expect too much when it comes to these point-and-click adventure games. But it's Back to the Future! Made by Telltale! And has Doc's original actor (Christopher Lloyd, from what I recall)! So what's not to love? Unless you're not a BTTF fan, or just hate the game in general.
The premise of the game is to explore Doc's disappearance, requiring you to go back in time and find him in some time in the past. From there, the plot kind of goes in some strange but enjoyable turn of events, thus propelling your role to fix up time paradoxes and whatnot, so the future normalises itself.
So plot-wise, the game seems to make sense mostly. Characters aren't too detailed, but you can make sense of what they're like, which is important in some parts of the episodes. But the plot starts to get interesting from Episode 3 onwards,
.
Controls can get a bit weird with the camera panning around sometimes, so you might find the down button moves you left, and some others unusual orientation of movements.
Now, I played the "Wallace and Gromit" games
, and what I mainly don't like in these episodes is the
.
In "Wallace and Gromit", you'd just right click to bring up your items and pick something out. Here, you have to click on the item icon, pick your item, and if you need to pick out another item, you have to do the process again. Sure, you're never really using objects mostly, but it is always nice to hotkey these things.
Additionally, some items
and kind of just loiter around your item space. I guess red herrings are interesting, but if you're stuck in a certain part of the game, you might think these items are useful, but the're not. So be aware of that, but at least they disappear (mostly) in the next episode.
Also, walking speeds are a bit slow. I found that holding Shift makes you "run", which is just a sped-up animation of Marty with a slight speed increase. In certain areas, you will actually run, and even so, if you phase out of an area, you have to re-hold the Shift key again to "run". A bit of a pain, but it's manageable.
The puzzles are interesting to solve, like that guitar battle with Leech, the SoupMo guy,
.
In some instances, you'll be likely to be in a situation where you're wondering
. Here, hints can come in handy. I've only ever had to use the hints once (mostly due to my adamance of finding the solution myself), but sometimes it can really get to you and make you kinda rage at the game, because you don't know what to do next.
And some instances, you'll actually solve the puzzle using sheer coincidence, where your actions just happpen to fall together into a solution that works out. But mostly, you'll have to recall certain information and use objects to help you coordinate the environment to your will and get things done.
In terms of play time, each episode took around 2-3 hours each, which equates to about 10-15 hours to finish the series. So if you're a casual player with a few hours to spare, I guess this is one avenue to spend your
on. See what I did there, eh? But $24.99 is a little steep for only 15 hours, I suppose. You might want to wait until this is on special (I got it in a Humble Bundle) or something.
But in short, I'd give this a 7/10. Not too bad, but still a bit rough around the edges.

I have been playing this game for quite some time now. I have enjoyed almost every moment of it. Not saying there were flaws that frustrated me, but what game doesn't cause some sort of frustration?
This game is Early Access, so of course there are going to be many bugs/missing mechanics. But that is to be expected with all Early Access games. If you can handle it, I would recommend this game to you.
Game Modes
Sandbox - Not entirely fun, but I suppose it can be if you allow it. I do enjoy the deathmatch servers, a great way to release a little tension, just don't look at global chat if you decide you want to massacre everyone. Sandbox can be great for new players to get a feel for the game. To learn the maps, mechanics etc.
Progression - This can be a lot of fun, if you allow it to be. Most call it a 'sitting in a bush AFK simulator'. It doesn't have to be. If you are constantly aware of your surroundings and explore silently, its enjoyable. I will not say I have never sat in a bush, but that was my choice. Give it a chance, you might surprise yourself.
Survival - The newest game mode and not anywhere near completion. Even so, I do find it a lot of fun. There are only two playable creatures right now, Rex and Carno. There are AI who will either run from you or try to kill you. In the future you will grow from a juvenile into an adult, once you complete this, you will be given a token and buy your next dinosaur. I am sure there will be more to this in the future, so I will not describe this game mode until I know more about it.
If I were to say the worst thing that I have experienced with this game. Wasn't the game itself, more of the community that plays it. Now not all of the community is horrible, I have met many great people.
Developers are more or less targeted by the toxic part of the community, try to take their comments with a grain of salt. Nothing should be taken seriously and should impact anyone's thoughts on purchasing this game. I am not saying this to be a 'brown nose.' It is just something I have observed throughout my time in this community. Yes, the devs can be harsh at times, but again if you read what people write, you would be too.
Right now, if you enjoy playing a dinosaur, I feel this is the game for you. Try it out and give it a chance. You will just have to be patient and watch where this game is going to take you. If you want to know more about it, I would join their official discord.

This game is mediocre at best.
There's a lot of counselors and plenty of Jasons to choose from, which is nice. The in-game currency is limited, you can either buy perks for counselors or kill methods for Jason. That's it.
The maps are big & you can talk with people based on proximity, though you can't choose options to be opted in games only with English speaking players or players above 13 - I've come across many Chinese/Japanese/Russian/children players, not understanding what they're saying & limiting our communication hindering our team effort or just screaming into their microphone. Thank god for the mute button. I don't really like the fact that Jason can speak with the counselors either. I always thought that was a stupid feature.
The team-killing in this game is disgusting. You get trolls who team with Jason, kill their teammates, or rage quit because they don't want to face a certain Jason or they didn't get to play as Jason this match. There is no soft-ban or cooldown on match searches even after this. Not even a report feature.
There's an abundance of bugs. Sometimes playing as Jason, the knives bug out & you can't pick them up. Sometimes as counselors, drawers get stuck & you can't open them. Jason is invincible in his combat stance + blocking. Doesn't take damage from shotgun, flare gun, bear traps or any weapons at all. Sometimes when hosting, the game gives me a black screen & I literally have to restart my computer because I can't get to my task manager or force close the game. The most recent and most time consuming bug, I lost all of my progress by signing in. I had 104 hours of gameplay. I had every counselor/Jason unlocked. Every Jason kill unlocked. 15+ epic perks. I was level 50+ so I had quite a bit of counselor clothing. This was unacceptable for the time took to develop this game and the amount of money this game costs. Though I was able to get in contact with a developer quickly by messaging them in their discord where they were hanging out. Apparently there was some kind of data overload (I was told) and caused some player’s profiles to bug out. I was given my levels back, plus a few extra, and enough CP (in game currency) to re-purchase perks so I was around the area I was before my profile got deleted.
I dislike the fact that Jason spawn is random. I play with friends often, many of whom have their spawn preference set to counselor, and mine to Jason, & they get to play Jason more than I do. What the f*ck kind of spawning system is that? If I want to play Jason, I have to go to private match & select myself as Jason, that is if my game doesn’t give me a black screen for hosting, making me restart my computer.
The teleportation Jason can conduct seems out of place and weird. It would be different if there was accompanying mist that suddenly appears and Jason appears through the mist, obscuring the actual spawn of Jason, but having him appear from thin air with no music to have him suddenly grab you is obnoxious.
On top of the unfortunate way the devs seem to manage themselves, I hardly see responses to bugs (even game breaking bugs), minimal patching/updates to the game (besides the stupid Barney Jason nobody asked for), and the permanent game-banning taking place. If you're interested in the banning situation in the game, watch this video (though not everything is accurate in the video, it gives a good idea what to expect when playing the game). -
The profits: They raised over $800,000 on kickstarter, not to mention backerkit, and have sold over 200,000 game copies (
). That's about $9-$10 million. For that amount of money you would expect more than a buggy alpha version of a hide-and-seek game. (I haven't taken into account the sales on console.)
I backed this game on kickstarter for the minimal amount I could to get the base game, Savini Jason, and the counselor DLC clothing with the game. I hope with bug updates/balancing, the game will get better.
As of now, the biggest flaw I have with the game is the community. The community is disgustingly cancerous. If you plan on playing solely with friends, it’s not a bad investment, though there is no single-player mode available yet. I believe that is to come late this summer, so the game isn’t even ‘complete’, yet there is no ‘early access’ tag on the game in the store, just a big IOU in place of promised content.

The reliance on the RNG to be on your side is very high. Prepare to start over quite a few times through circumstances you can't avoid.
You need to be lucky enough to find the right material in the right amounts, while hoping that nothing bad happens to anyone.
Rain can be very unpredicatble. Some times you can wait days and only receive enough to fill 20 or 30 water even with an upgraded filter. This can leave you unable to leave your shelter to continue to collect other items leading to a spiral of defeat.
Sometimes you get random people that join you beyond your starting family of 4. These people will do absolutely nothing but consume resources for at least 20-30 minutes of real time. After an eternity of waiting on them to eat and drink their bloody fill, they'll finally go on expeditions. Once you run out of gas masks, and if they get radiation sickness, then you have 2 options. Use the pills or let them die. If you kick them out of the shelter before they die, they get angry and ruin your buildings.
You can get attacked by bandits and at the point of this writing, you cannot do anything except hide from them.
You can build Hiding Spots. It can be difficult to find enough hinges for every person you have.
All the items you need to be more efficient come at workbench level 3 and 4 and it can be quite tough to get to that point.
In this, you're relying on a lot of RNG, and not all that much strategy.

This is a difficult game to review, because good or bad really depends on what side of the fence you're playing on. Steam really needs an option other than reccommended or not, buy because you'll play as counselors far more often, I had to go with not reccommended. When you're playing as Jason, the game is actually a lot of fun. If you're playing as a counselor, however (and actually trying to survive) not so much.
This game is incompetently unbalanced in Jason's favor. It's quite clear where all the developers thought and effort went when designing it. Jason has plenty of ways to find and catch counselors while counselors have nothing at all to give them any sort of advantage.
There are two ways for a counselor to survive, (three if you count killing Jason but the circumstances required for that are nearly impossible).
1. By finding gas, a car battery and keys for the car and driving the car away. The locations of these are randomized, so they could be anywhere. The car handles for crud, however, and if you hit anything at all, (including Jason) it will crash and it will take you a few seconds to get the car started again. However, Jason will usually know when the car is moving so all he needs to do is teleport in front of the car and you'll likely hit him.
2. By finding the phone box fuse, phone box and using the phone to call the cops. A five minute timer will come up and once the police arrive you can go to the location that they spawned and escape. However, not only is the location of the fuse randomized, so is the phone itself, and unlike Jason's map, the phone is NOT marked on the counselor's map. So even if a counselor DOES stumble upon the phone box fuse, they most likely won't know where to take it unless someone else knows where it is. Which brings me to my next point.
The idea behind the gameplay of the counselors was clearly teamwork. You were meant to work together to find everything, which would be fine, however, there were issues even with this.
First and foremost... There's no text chat in the game. So if you have no mic (or in my case, the mic isn't working with this game for whatever reason) you're out of luck. If you should stumble across the fuse, you can't ask someone else where the phone is.
Second, until you and the other counselors find walkie-talkies, you can only communicate with counselors that are nearby so even if you CAN talk to other counselors, if you're alone or the counselors nearby to you can't help you, you're out of luck unless both you and the one that can help you have a walkie-talkie.
Third, dead players cannot communicate with living ones. This might seem obvious, but it creates a huge problem. If a counselor dies, he can't tell those still living "I had the phone box fuse." or whatever he might have had on him. Meanwhile, the other counselors are still looking for that vital item in the usual locations because they don't even know to look for it elsewhere, having no idea that it's laying in the middle of the wilderness somewhere near that player's corpse.
Unlike the beta, counselors do NOT begin with a map. Counselors have to find their map (which are also randomly placed). Until you do, you're basically wandering blind. This is not true of Jason, he DOES have a map to begin with, and his map is more detailed. He knows where the phone box and electrical boxes are. Counselors do not, even if they DO have a map.
And lastly, counselors have no option to quit the game without sacrificing their XP, even if they've died. If you die, you have to sit back and spectate the rest of the game (unless in the unlikely event that you get resurrected as Tommy Jarvis). So if you die early on, you could very well be sitting and watching instead of actually playing for the next 20 minutes, unless you want to lose experience gained in the game.
To sum up, Jason is given nothing but advantages while counselors are given nothing at all. If the communication issues between counselors were resolved, it would go a long way toward fixing these problems

What nuance does the force have?
That’s the question Obsidian asked themselves. Is there a Machiavellian equivalent in the Star Wars Universe?
Do good things mean good for all or can dark actions beget positive outcome?
These questions would have been answered, had Obsidian been given the time. But now we’re left with a story that does little to overturn the dichotomy of the force. The vestigial limb of this idea is Kreia.
Kreia is difficult. As the game is today, you almost need precognition to guess what she wants from you. Doing good will often get you chastised by her, but do bad will get you chide remarks — both ending in influence lost.
The only tell-sign that you’re down the right path is to say, “You’re right.” or “I’ll consider your teachings.” If by some happenstance you don’t see that option then you’ve really screwed up. But that doesn’t make her any less of a nuanced character. If anything she becomes more human by being difficult to please. But does it make for a better game?
That’s how I’d query all the characters of KOTOR 2.
.
So why do I recommend this?
The characters do belong there — they have history with the universe. They breath their beliefs and exhale world-building that needn’t be expounded.
Every character is more than they seem but stay human. Kreia is desperate. She is trying to impart knowledge that will make you grow. From her perspective, you’re an impetuous child who holds too much power but has so much responsibility.
Nuance can be found in the dialogue, too.
The writer has a secret they’re trying to tell you but they can only speak in enigmatic messages spread across multiple dialogues.
And you’re the other. You’re the monster in the closet for this writer.

I've just played about an hour and a half of this game and I couldn't stop smiling the entire time.
