TL;DR: A good game from Supergiant Games, definitely recommend playing it. But beware, there is much to read and if you don't like the core gameplay (the rites) then this game will disappoint you.
Gorgeous and breathtaking art aside, this games core mechanic, the Rites, is a really fun kind of soccer, almost reminiscent of Mario Strikers: Charged, but also vastly different in style. The different characters have different abilities with weaknesses and strengths, making it crucial to choose the right team against the opponents you are facing.
Main goal is to push a ball in the enemies fire (the pyre) and extinguish it, either by tossing yourself with the ball in there (easier, but with drawbacks for the next round) or just tossing the ball (more difficult, because easily interruptable, but no drawbacks).
The enemy however, having the same abilities as you, won't make it easy on you and every Rite plays different.
There is more, the story is also quite intriguing, slowly opening up to the player as he goes his way. The characters all have their own quirks and almost all of them are likable in their own way. However, the game gains another component after aprox. 4 hours of playtime, opening it up more, but also falling into repetition gameplay-wise. Midgame you experience the same procedure again and again, always interrupted by different story bits, but still, it is a loop and the story does not really move at this point.
Unfortunately I am quite sure the many "choices" you can make throughout the game (don't want to spoil anything) will not amount to as many endings as it wnats you to believe, because the sheer number of possible outcomes cannot be programmed into this little game.
All in all, the beautiful art, the unique gameplay and the possibilities unfolding as I play make this game pretty good. This certainly gets a high recommendation, everyone should try this, but also beware, there is much text and a lot of repeting gameplay mechanics midgame, making it a game that is NOT for everyone. Not Supergiants best game, especially story-wise, but very enjoyable nonetheless (for me at least).

His oldest daughter and youngest son are currently on the political ladder as the masses continue to believe he earned the title through hard work and not through cold revenge for his wife's imprisonment. Hook is a series of logic puzzles which take about an hour to an hour and a half to work through. It's short, but well priced. Its ideal use is probably downloaded from the google app store and played while you're waiting for your flight, because it reminds me of some short puzzle book you pick up at an airport book store - except it isn't $1,500.
Minimalist is probably the right word because it gets to the point of what you are there for without a needless amount of useless and annoying user interface.  Controls for the switches are easy and intuitive and the game gives you easy walkthrough levels to learn how things are going to work when it starts to get complicated. Progress is saved after you unlock the next level in case you buy this game two hours after you should have been in bed and realize that might have been a mistake.
Some of the higher level puzzles look daunting but, honestly, all of them are doable as long as you commit yourself to sitting down and thinking about things before you do something stupid. Failed attempts restart the level but, even then, they realised this might be frustrating at high levels and give you basically "three lives" before a restart. It's super sweet.
Between its plesant experience and price, I do recommend this game highly.

Let me begin by saying that this game is alright. There isn't anything seriously bad about it, but there isn't much that is great either.
I bought this game during a sale for less than $5.00 and I don't think I would have paid more for it.
It's fun little game, but it feels just a step above a java game that you could play on your browser. It's pretty addicting just like some of those simple games are as well.
I haven't played a game like this before, but I hear that there are similar ones with more depth.
--WHO THIS GAME IS FOR--
Someone who is just interested in some casual tactical gaming. Pleased enough with moderate strategy gaming.
The Good:
++Levels aren't dreadfully long (about 6 minutes) but there are 7 countries to visit, each with 5 levels to play in. Also 3 game modes (Terrorist Hunt, Bomb Defusal, and Escape Plan) using same maps, This may not seem like alot but it manages to have just enough variety
++There are a lot of options with costomization and I've found myself really thinking about my purchases for guns.
--However, there is a problem with costomization that I will get into later
++Option to play with Permanent death of squad members to earn extra XP (You get a replacement if one dies but you have to rank them back up) You keep the dead members expensive weapon equipment, which is good.
++Upgrading skills for your soldiers is pretty solid with the variety of options (Responce, Accuracy, Health, Speed, Evation and an Skill that goes with the soldier's role; Like Squad Leader gets leadership skill you can upgrade). Not too easy to upgrade but not too hard.
++I like that you can assign roles to your 4 person squad (Leader, Medic, Breach, ect) and that they get perks unlocked as you level up.
The Bad:
I'm going to begine with the costomization options
++There are MANY different guns (some same price and same specs though)
On the guns you can pack them with Optics, Lasers, Grips, Flashlights, Supressors, Gas System, and Triggers
The problem is that There are only a handful of attatchments in each category and it's easy to max out on the Optics, Lasers, Grips, Flashlights. There are no tactical thinking involved in these options because they only improve accuracy and have no negatives, so you don't weigh your options. -It's pretty mindless
--The good thing is that Suppressors, Gas Systems,  and Triggers provide certain pros and cons that make you consider what perks you want and the expense of something.
There are vests and other things but to buy that are important, but there are many items like clothing, goggles and facepaint that provide NO perks.
++The Main Menu is slow and kinda laggy and brings a bad first impression when you put your mouse over a button and it takes 3 seconds for it to light up. The response when you select it is absolutely normal. But makes the game seem cheap.
++The strategy is pretty basic. I've only felt trapped and in trouble a few times. The gameplay is mostly all about keeping your guys near cover and know how to split up your guys (which isn't challenging)
If you 4 star all the maps as you progress Like I do and not jump ahead two counties (with harder soldiers) it doesn't stay very challenging. (I went two counties ahead and within two moves I was surounded and lost a guy right when he got shot at) -RIP Brett Breachers
++I'm playing the levels in Germany, (which is the 4th country) and the environment is pretty static. Only a few levels actually had 1-3 of the soldiers walking around in real time as you plan out your strategy.
THE UGLY
++The ugly part isn't in the gameplay. It is with selecting items in the market and selecting the items when you choose a new gun or add attatchments.
+The interface with the Market and costomization is terrible.
+When I purchase a new gun I have to make sure to detatch everything on the previous gun, and there isn't any fast/easy way to do it (Such as putting a small 'x' in the corner). I have to select the icon individually for Lasers, Optics, Grips ect. THEN select to 'unequip' this gets very Tedious when there are 7 attachment types.
+The interface only shows you the picture of what items are attached to your gun with no name of them or what their specs are.
+You have to go to unequip it and then mouse over it to view its specs.
+Another problem is that it doesn't tell you the name of what gun your soldier is equiped with. You have to memorize its shape and look in the market so you can compare it to a new weapon.
+When you want to compare weapons in the market you can't do it side by side. You have to click the gun, then scoll down/up the list to view the next one. That is teious as well.
CONCLUSION:
I give the game a 6.5/10 -Would not pay $15.00, wait for a sale of less than $7 if you aren't sure about this. Addicting to play but almost too simple to call it a strategy game.
+It needs improvements to make the game more interesting and needs its interface to be changed.
+Would be interesting to add multiplayer of terrorists vs Spec Ops. Where each team has to make their moves and then it plays out.
+Another request would be to add new scenarios (This might be later in the maps, IDK yet) with a less static environment and enemies. Like Helicopter, or enemies driving in the stronghold with vehicles.

I keep looking in the distance for gunmen in windows of derelict buildings and roof tops.
The crux of enjoyment for me is taking out fellow snipers 100+ metres away. This alone is hugely enjoyable: from lining up your shot, choosing whether to take a body shot or a more risky head-shot(instant kill).
You star in a detailed war zone where you have multiple adversaries in varied scenes. This is different to your average shooter. The rewards are for accurate shooting, long distance shooting, head shots, shooting through 2 people with 1 shot, even shooting someone through the nuts(the slow-mo kill-cam is extraordinarily detailed). The game is more enjoyable when played with patience; although there are some non-sniper scenes(usually in buildings) where you choose a rapid fire gun to take out the enemy. For every mission you choose your rifle, machine gun, pistol and grenades/dynamite etc.
If you ever enjoy those long distance shots in fps games then this will be a perfect alternative to the thousand of mindless shooters out there.
Overall: a superb shooter with detailed graphics and addictive gameplay.

It's a port from mobile. The enemy AI is kind of a joke and you have no way to tell your guys to hold fire. They spray lead at everything in their view instead of waiting to get in to a superior position. This often leads to them taking unnecessary damage and is tactically idiotic.
Example: 4 tango with backs to entry point. Your team enters and opens fire as soon as they enter while moving to cover. They kill all 4 tangos but take damage in the exchange of gunfire. Had they held fire till in cover, they would be far less likey to take damage while maintaining their advantage of surprise and position.
Game lacks "go codes" like Door Kickers does so well. In the planning stage, there is no time representation so you can't see how many seconds it will take to move someone to a position. No hold position/delay for X time command. No shoot at this target till threat is removed, then continue with plan. You can't pick which targets to shoot at so no way to prioritize targets. Therefore you can't tell your guys to focus the sniper standing in the open vs the shotguner in heavy cover who happends to be a bit closer.
Another glaring problem is that every gun unlocked after the CTAR has not been an upgrade. Currently at 472 stars. Laughing at how many stars are required to unlock the later shotguns. Game is getting far too boring and repetitive to ever reach 1400 let alone the 2100 for the last rifle.
From the Devs "The higher star guns are more for 'prestige' than anything else. They were added as    a prize for fans who wanted something out of the ordinary, so they are camouflaged or Platinum/Gold versions of earlier guns."
Prestige in a single player game? Umm OK.
No way to tell what is required to reach 4 stars on any given map. Every map and scenario has different requirements, but game fails to tell you what you are aiming for.  Use an item on one map, ok. Use the same item on another and lose a star but won't tell you are being deducted. Did I get 3 stars on my last try because I didn't make time or due to using an item? No Fn idea. Huge fail IMO.
Not enough variety of weapons. One assault rifle after another. Outside of the of the P90, game lacks submachine guns like a variant of the MP5, MP7A1 or UMP. Guess this is due to the squads being military and not law enforcement. These are guns I would expect to find in the arsenal of a game that focuses on CQB regadless of the operators.
Game is more arcade'ish than tactically sound. Glad I picked this up at 75% off.

A step up from Amnesia (which was fantastic) in scope and ambition. Soma explores the concept of consciousness and what it means to be human and alive, but also brings in some neuroscience concepts you don't often hear about with regards to the mind and body. This isn't primarily a pure shock/horror type of game, rather you can think of it as a stealth and puzzle game set in a sci-fi horror universe. It has its creepy and scary moments, but thats just a side effect of the story, rather than the focus. I'd highly recommend this to anyone who's interested in a thought provoking experience with a rich universe, even if you're not into horror games.
Do yourself a favor and buy it.

Apotheon is an ancient greek action platformer. I dont like the art style, but i guess it fits the ancient greek theme. You can see it yourself in the trailer, if its a plus to you thats fine.
Gameplay consists of going on various quests involving following arrows through the overworld to find mini dungeons scattered about that often have a boss in them and lots of purposeless corridors. Most of these quests never really had any explanation as to why I needed to do them, for example in the "Hades" area players must cross 4 rivers before fighting the areas boss. When you cross these rivers you come out back exactly where you started. It seem the only reason I had to do it was to add to the gameplay, not the story. However, many of these quests were very interesting and fun. This isn't nessicarily a fault. The problems come in with the platforming and combat.
Platforming is quite obnoxious, it almost feels like im lagging but I dont think i am. Its very hard to move just a small amount or land on a small platform. Most areas are designed with "Z" shaped platforms, so youll often try to jump up onto one and lagging into the crook, because the jump didnt respond well. Also unresponsive is trying to down jump through a platform. This is very annoying when trying to run away. When you receive a big hit sometimes you go flying unpredictably. Also if your like me your used to roll jumping everywhere. Nope in this game you get to jump roll instead, thats a bit strange. There arent really that many parts in this game that require precise platforming anyways but its still annoying, especially on the final boss.
Combat system is very simple but there are a ton of guards its much better to just run past most of them. When you do have to fight, despite the game insisting otherwise, you can just button mash with most weapons. Range weapons even have automatic aiming which is pretty OP. You can also make a ton of healing items using the crafting system. Even when you do die you aren't set back much by it.
Theres this weird issue while trying to switch weapons while in combat where you cant do it while attacking. I would expect the game to finish the attack and then switch. When your weapon breaks this gets really annoying and makes it hard to use the more advanced potions at all.The UI also has weird overlapping issues very often.
If your going to play it play it for an ancient greek story the gameplay is subpar.
P.S. If your going to play it anyways you should note that the last difficulty is locked until you beat the game once but theres a bug you can do to skip to the final boss and get the acheivement for beating that difficulty without beating the whole game again.

I've had a surprising amount of fun playing this game. The action is there. The music is great. It's flashy. It's arcady. It's nothing more or less than what it claims to be. It's definitely early access at the moment and there just isn't a whole ton on content in it but for $5 how can anyone be too upset. I'll give a quick pro and con list here just for anyone curious of the current state.
Pros:
-Graphics are pretty good. The lasers are bright and flashy. The paint on the ships is cool.
-Get that sense of mayhem. There are big ships shooting big lasers everywhere and then all around are little ships so it's really kind of crazy.
-The controls are tight and simple. I have used both keyboard and mouse as well as an Xbox controller. Worked great.
-Music is wonderful.
-Split screen coop. A rare addition to modern games especially on PC.
-Active developer. He answers questions on the forums and has already implemented some requested things.
Cons:
-Explosions are a little weak. The sound. The look. The feel. Just not much there at the moment.
-Can be a little hard to tell what ships are good guys and bad guys. Maybe that's just me.
-Although the controls are good and tight it can feel like you are flying a camera around a level editor sometimes. It doesn't hurt the game but some may find it a little strange.
-Repetetive. It's a $5 arcade game so I can't say I expect a big story or a bunch of unlocks and things but just be aware that you are just going to fly in and kill all the ships and then do it again and again until you win or lose. Again that's not really a con if you know what you're getting into.
I whole heartedly recommend the game to anyone looking for a flashy arcade shoot em up to play with friends on a couch.

I have hundreds of hours logged, but it won't show it because I'm using gzdoom to run doom on windows 8.1. I'm also using two mods: DoomMetalVol4.wad and brutal19.pk3 aka BrutalDoom.
To this day, almost 30 years since the release of this game, there's been only one FPS that is as good as this, and that's the entire half-life series.
This game isn't a rails shooter. It's not a trip through disney land. It's a "cozy" maze based shooter. You're in the middle of a non-linear level with limited ammo and horrors from hell, but it feels good.
This game makes you feel the entire world is burning up around you, but you have the power to fight back. Hence, "cozy".
Just an incredible game.
If this is your first time going through this on a modern machine.
Pick up gzdoom and the two mods I mentioned above and you're in luck. There's probably a newer version of brutal doom by the time you read this, so get the latest one, but even going through the game once in vanilla is probably fine, but you'll still want to go through the vanilla version in gzdoom because dosbox doesn't always play friendly with the latest OS.

This game is a blast! It's like a 3D shmup without a pattern and is something I would have pumped tons of quarters into if it existed before now.
It's pure mayhem and there's zero fluff. You drop in and start shooting until everything is destroyed, or until they destroy you, then it's on to the next level. They get more difficult as they go - there are more ships and a greater variety of them further on, and the bigger ones pack more of a punch and are harder to kill. If there's not many enemy ships left in the wave, just follow the tracers from the capital ships and you'll be right back into it!
The HUD is minimal, just a  reticle and weapon selection, and the controls are simple and easy to use. You can strafe and roll in any direction while shooting constantly. The AI is decent and will track your movements with their weapons, no matter how slick you think you're being. The backgrounds are pretty and the ships designs are cool too.
The sound effects are a bit tinny to my ears but they are well done and you can tell the direction of incoming fire by sound location as well as the shiny lasers. So many shiny lasers! They are everywhere and remind me of bullet hell games. The capital ships don't seem to damage you though, just the other fighters.
If this were in an arcade, I would have already spent more than $5 bucks on it so it's a good buy in my book, plus it's pure no-frills fun, no BS, and I'm enjoying the hell out of it!
It's a good game if you like dinos and killing. Best dino game I'v ever played so I would recommend this game.

This is my thrird review for this game, the first was after 7 hours of pay time, and the second was after 25 hours. While writing this review I have had around 55 hours on the game.
Alot has changed since the launch of this game in terms of bug fixing and server issues. Most of the bugs i initially encountered have now been patched, so overall the game is very playable and has less issues than most other games.
The developer was also quick to patch issues relating to hacking and glitching, which I encountered once where a player took all the items from my inventory, but this was an isolated incident and is no longer an issue. Games with much larger teams and budgets such as GTA V have far more issues in terms of hackers than this, so don't let reports of hacking stop you from buying the game.
The game has also improved in terms of servers, it is quick to find a game and most lobbies have good ping compared to when the game first launched. It is now possible to remove the full party from a lobby and bring them with you, which is better than having to re create the party if you leave a game.
Since players have become better at the game it is now much more balanced. It is easier to escape Jason when you have more playtime, since you know how his abilites work and how to avoid them, such as running in a circle during morph. This means earlier issues with the balance of the game have been improved naturaly, so it is more easy to escape while still being challenging.
The three maps are different, and have different methods of escape which helps to make each match different although it does get repetitive at times, random loot spawns help to make the games different also.
I would like to see some sort of in game report feature to more easily report cheaters or people who work with Jason, since this is very annoying and the devs can't ban people which they dont know about.
The banning policy should be more clear, since it does not say anywhere working with Jason is bannable, this needs to be made clear before purchase and during start up to remind people, since I imagine being banned from a £30 for doing nothing you thought was wrong would be very annoying. Also a "three strikes" system could be implemeted, first a warning, then a day ban, then a week ban, then a permenant ban would be much more fair.
Content - Content is lacking for the game, I woild like to see more Jasons, Maps and councillors added for free along with maybe paid DLC in the future if it were a signinfigant change. Since currently the only update since launch was the retro stuff, which is cool but dosent go far enough to address the content lacking.
F13 is a game well worth buying and is very fun, but it should be noted content can become lacking eventually, so if you are on the fence maybe hold off until more stuff comes out, otherwise if you like the genre and are fine with the three maps, its a very good and well made game.

This game is truly completely different than all the other Supergiant games.
I’ve played for a while now, and I believe the following points are important to know about Pyre.
1. The game is extremely story centered. You have to read a lot. If you don't like reading dialogues or anything at all in games then I think this game is not for you. The game depends on you reading everything. The story is interesting though. Sometimes there are really funny moments. All in all it’s not boring to read it.
2. You have to make many decisions, and yes they do impact the story to a certain extend. Some have more impact than others though.
3. So, expect for the fights, this game is like a Visual Novel. The most time is spent reading.
The story is interesting and I want to know what happens next. Also the characters. Those are so diverse and likeable; it’s nice and refreshing. The art is just gorgeous and the music is too, just like in any previous Supergiant games.
I personally really like reading a good story so I'd definitely recommend this game to anyone who does too.
--- I've written a little bit more about story & characters below (light spoilers) ---
Story
I‘ve read a lot of Visual Novel’s (not sexual one’s, mind you) and I also read a lot of books. I think the story is interesting but not as engaging as it should and must be as a Visual Novel’s. There is a whole backstory written in a book about the Rite’s that you are completing, which you can read. It’s mostly told out of the perspective of a person, but it still gets boring fast. Sometimes after completing a rite, I gained up to 8 pages of this book at once. It’s not fun reading 8 pages at once. I do believe there is a better way of implementing the backstory into a game. I really wanted to read it all, but it began feeling like a task all too soon. Of course, this could have been me being lazy.
Characters
I love the diverse and likeable characters that Pyre presents to you. In fact, I like them so much, that sometimes I ask myself: Why can’t we speak more with them? Instead of having so much text written in a book, why not be able to deepen your friendship with your companions? I did ‘care’ about them a little bit, even with the relatively short and rare interactions that are available. But being on a journey with them, being a team, completing the rite’s together… I think it would have been good for the game if there was a possibility to speak and interact more with your companions. But that’s really just my opinion.
Obligatory German: ‘I’m sorry for my bad English’ and thanks for reading! :)

Definitely will update when I've finished, but first impressions are that this is a great game, with the same quality we're all used to from Supergiant.
It's a lot different from their previous games, but that certainly doesn't make it bad. After all, Transistor was different from Bastion, but it's still one of my all time favourite games.
The playable characters are all endearing so far, especially Rukey and Bae, and I look forward to spending more time with them. The voice acting is all wonderful as well. It's done in a constructed language mostly based on Latin which sounds gorgeous.
It's definitely a lot more text heavy than their previous games, so if that bothers you, I'd approach with caution. The devs mentioned drawing inspiration from Fire Emblem, and I can see that in how they tell the story, and the general flow of the game: They'll present you with a cutscene, developing the characters nicely. After that is a battle, perhaps with a few lines of text thrown in around the beginning, middle, and end. Next is another cutscene, and then an optional look in their wagon to talk to one of the characters. I personally don't have a problem with this, but I'm sure there are plenty of people who would be turned off by this.
The battle system is also an aspect which I thoroughly enjoy, but understand why it might turn people off. When you get down to it, it's a sport. You have to pass the ball from teammate to teammate and get it to your opponent's goal. Some people, if I understand correctly, are complaining about only being able to control one character at a time, but I honestly don't think there's any other way around it. It's not like it can take a similar route to The World Ends With You without being incredibly difficult and clunky. The settled upon system does take a bit of getting used to, learning how to pass and position your teammates effectively, but I personally found it incredibly satisfying once I got the hang of it.
Finally, I just want to end on the note that Darren Korb's soundtrack is amazing, just like in Bastion and Transistor. It fits the world perfectly, and is honestly one of the main reasons I was excited for the new game. If you don't buy the game, I highly recommend you go to
and purchase the soundtrack, as well as those for Bastion and Transistor if you haven't already. Darren and the rest of the team at Supergiant put a lot of love and hard work into their games, and they have definitely earned my support.

First of all disregard time played, I have been playing this game from the moment it entered the Closed Beta.
Game Modes
Well where to begin. At this point in time Survarium has several PvP modes available for you to play.
First up is Scavenge, in this mode 2 teams of 8 players start must sniff around the map for batteries,
these spawn in random but fairly predictable locations around the map, some will be out in plain sight,
and some close to or within the anomaly( I will get to this later) on the map. These must be picked up
and delivered to a charging station located close to your spawn and indicated on the map, while carrying
you are 100% vulnerable, unable to spring or perform any functions aside from moving, jumping and being
able to drop the battery. There are a total of 10 of them all around the map and you need to have more
on your team's side to win. Mind you while this sounds simple it is much more complicated than that,
as batteries can be STOLEN by the enemy and vice versa, a common and rather sour strategy is to collect
a "safe" amount of batteries, usually 6 or +2 of whatever the enemy has, and when the countdown reaches
low like 10 - 20 seconds depending on the map, people just rush the enemy charger and unplug all batteries.
Next mode is Charging Stations, in this mode instead of locating the batteries several charging stations are
placed within the environment, these randomly but once again fairly predictably spawn a single battery which
must be taken to your charging station, once the first battery is spawned they begin spawning subsequently roughly
once every 30 seconds.
Third and the most recently added mode is Research, I personally do not like this mode and avoid it, so go find
info on it somewhere else.
Last but not least is your traditional Team Deathmatch, no batteries, just pure old fashioned bloodshed with 150
spawn tickets for each team and 15 minutes of time, whichever runs out first.
Features
Survarium can be played in several different ways, much like the majority of modern day shooters you have access
to a rather impressive arsenal of weapons and gear, and decent customization to both. At this stage the guns cannot
be messed with, ie silencers scopes etc, but that will be added at some point in time. The outfitting customization
however is most impressive, different types of clothing Feet/Legs/Chest/Hands/Face/Head/Back, of these Chest and Head
can have changeable cloth types and camo types as well up to 2 player placed decals. You can basically blend into almost
anything in the game if you know how to do it right, and if not moving you can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to see, and locate.
While most people think "Ohhh f**king campers everywhere" allow me to assure you that it is not the case as the guns being
so goddam lethal if you know where to shoot a sniper is rarely stationary, moving place to place as the sound alone will
attract every enemy within half the map's radius. That pretty much covers the basic stuff. And then there are things like
Traps, Explosives, Anomalies and Artifacts, oh and soon Mutants. At this point in time the only trap is the Bear Trap
which, if stepped on, will 9/10 times break your legs and cripple you, as well as take a third of your hp, oh and make you
bleed too, if carefully placed, 2 or 3 traps can be triggered at the same time for an amplified effect, 2 traps will put
you into critical condition and make you vulnerable to one hits from most guns, 3 traps will kill you instantly, at lower
levels in the game that ammount is less with 2 traps being a killer and a single one being a crippler. Combine these with
Smoke Grenades (damn the effect in this game is really GOOD) and you have yourself one helluva an advantage knowing where
the traps are. Grenades at this point is the only explosive, BUT, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥is it good, you can run and hide from them
but if cooked to perfection only an activated Onyx artifact has a small chance of saving you, you will still be bleeding
from every single body part there is and will need medical attention. The Anomalies in this game are present on most
but not every map, Cologne Bridge for example does not have Anomalies and therefore does not have Artifacts. Anomalies
are either Gaseous, Radioactive, Toxic and Electric in nature, each one will affect you differently and at different speeds
depending on your outfitting, with some requiring only a small amount of protection to enter, you will use antitoxins
90% of the time when you are interracting with one, these help you live through the anomaly without dying in seconds.
Once inside one you will gradually take anomaly damage, this is indicated by the visual change on the screen, everything
will begin to shift in colors and focus ranges as well as tube like vision effects, basically like some good ACID. Once
this reaches a certain point you will die in a blink of an eye regardless of HP. So WHY would one seek entry in such a
treacherous place? 2 reasons, one being the fact that anomalies are cleverly placed, they are usually blocking off the
fastest/safest path to the enemy base or otherwise cut off access to certain locations, and then there are Artifacts.
These little bad boys are a real gamechanger, there is a total of 6 different types of artifacts with different passive
and active effects to complement a variety of playstyles. From damage reducting Onyx or movement enhancing Spring to
my personal favourite the Sponge, which soaks up anomaly damage passive, and can be thrown in a form of a toxic gas
grenade. Best part of it, the passive AND active effects can all stack, both with one another and with themselves.
Aside from that there your obvious med kits and bandages and items called "Rations", these occupy one equipment slot
and are consumed at the start of the round, giving the user a solid boost to a certain factor of the game, depending
on what you ate. They are however rather costly, especially for newbies, so I suggest you stay away until you have a
mil silver floating around unused.
Setting
Survarium is set in a world where mother nature has had enough of your♥♥♥♥♥♥ and decided to give us humans the boot up
the♥♥♥♥♥and kicked us out of cities and homes while casually murdering the majority of human population. Once she'd had
enough people began to emerge and blah blah blah blah and you know, now we wanna kill each other because there is nothing to
do and the world is a complete sausage-fest. The environment around you is overgrown and ravaged by nature, grass is up to
your nuts, some trees reach to the skies, and buildings are now just a gloom, pale and lifeless memory of what once was
our home, and when no guns are firing the sound of clarity fills the air. From distant birds to the sound of wind crossing
the halls of a School. In short, the atmosphere is nothing short of breathtaking, the sounds just bleeds into the atmosphere
making you feel like you are really there. All that, generously painted with Vostok's very own engine, designed specifically
for this purpose.
These are the biggest points of the game, everything mentioned above is the "Good". Now we move onto the "Bad".
Like many other online shooters the game suffers from ping. At this point in time there are no Oceanic servers, which
makes it painful to enjoy the game, but with proper configs I was able to achieve playable ping and could kick♥♥♥♥♥at
least half the time. The game is VERY ping dependent, so if you are not close to the currently available servers I suggest
to not play until there domestic servers near you, as high ping will CERTAINLY ruin your experience.
Then there is a very big question of Pay To Win. Some would say that the game is completely free, other people will say
that it's P2W. I think it is neither. On one hand you have the choice to play for free, you will have access to everything
there is in game, except for purchaseable camos/decals

You know, after enjoying Transistor and Bastion so thoroughly, for some reason, I didn't think Pyre would really be on the same level as those two games. The gameplay, at first glance, whilst interesting, didn't seem too engaging.
...But the more and more I play Pyre, the more I think I'm wrong. This game - whilst it has a slow story->gameplay->story pace not all may enjoy - is actually shaping up to be one of my favourite games of all time. Allow me to explain why. (And if you don't like long-winded reviews, you'd better find another one haha).
Pyre is an inspiring, lovingly-crafted, and clever game of quality I've only experienced in few games. When it comes to a mixture of creativity, quality, and a genuine love for the product they're producing, Supergiant has proved to me they're one of the best companies out there in that regard. Whilst I'm not one to read every inch of lore, I love being immersed in a certain setting, getting a feel for characters, and really feeling 'part of the game'. Pyre absolutely excels in that regard.
The gameplay itself appears simple at first, but there are many layers of complexity to it which I think would make it a really excellent multiplayer game. I won't fully go into details, but it's basically like playing top-down basketball made a lot more exciting with excellent graphics, sound design, and with a selection of many characters spicing up your different 3v3 matches with their own abilities. There are honestly tons of ways you can play, with characters such as the slow and powerful Jodariel offering an aggressive/defensive playstyle, or the super speedy Rukey allowing you to quickly rush down the celestial ball. Matches can get tense: seriously tense, if you find yourself getting thrashed by the AI (thankfully that's only happened to me once).
I wouldn't go as far as to say the gameplay is flawless (though it is very very good). Even at max difficulty, whilst I'm sure things are getting harder, I find it rather easy to repeatedly 'rush down' the celestial ball with fast characters. It would be nice to see a level of difficulty above the 'hardest' one that already stands for crowds looking for a true challenge. That said, if you lose a match, as far as I know, you don't just 'restart'. That loss goes down in history forever, so it's pretty intense. You /can/ restart a match if you lose, but... I'd sort of recommend against that, really.
Also, I'd love to see online multiplayer in this game, but unfortunately, I don't think it'll be possible to impliment it. It offers local multiplayer, though, and an 'arena mode' if you just want to hunker down into some gameplay and ignore the story.
Gameplay aside, another very big strength of this game is its characters. As you meet them (and yes, you meet more than the initial trio as you go along), you slowly begin to learn more and more about them. All of their dialogue is carefully written, and if you like seeing a lot of dialogue from a seemingly huge lineup (a bit like Fire Emblem), then this is a game for you. I also love how there's loads of little 'hidden interactions', and the game sometimes gives you 'multiple-choice options' that I'm sure will accomodate
The best thing about this game overall, though, for me at least, is the creativity of its design. I don't know if I'm the only one, and it's sort of unrelated, but I'll be going into university to do a Game Design & Writing course. I've always thought that, being a writer, I'll always be the 'useless' one of a game creating team when it comes past the design/ideas stage. This game, however, has encouraged & inspired me to think otherwise. The writing in this is truly superb, well-thought out, and it's funny how much a few little words on a screen can make you think and inquire about a character that... well... doesn't actually exist. And there are so, SO many multiple choices and ways you can go about this game, I can't even begin to imagine how many lines of dialogue were actually written for Pyre.
Oh, and this game costs not even half of what I'd be willing to pay for it. If you're cautious of your money, whilst I haven't completed a full playthrough yet, I am very, VERY sure this is worth your money.
So, waffling aside, what would I rate this game? Personally, it gets a 9.8/10 (which may as well be 10/10) from me, and I'm rare to give games I even consider 'good' anything higher than an 8.
I'd only recommend against buying this if you're someone who doesn't like story-driven games, or someone who gets annoyed when they're pulled out of gameplay and just can't bring themselves to care about characters at all. If you're one of those people, whilst I think you're missing out, I'd definietely say your money is better spent elsewhere.

Telltale Games one of their first finest work!
It might not be Telltale Games first developed title but, I was pleasantly surprised by this "Back to the Future: The Game" episodic series. It follows the adventures of the good ol' Doc Emmett Brown and his good friend, Marty McFly. It's not truly mandatory to have seen the movies BUT, it really helps to have background information of the movies. To put it short, this adventure game has a new story set after BttF Part 3 movie (it could be seen as a BttF Part 4). It ends with a possibility for more content so whether or not it becomes another episodic season or a new movie, but this season/series ended in 2011 so not sure if a sequel is likely... we shall see...
The episodic format takes you about 3 to 4 hours for each episode to complete. If you skip conversations and if you use or not, the hint system, the game can be shorter or longer.
PROS:
+Funny, goofy... just like the movies!
+Familiar setting with the visuals, voice cast, music.
+Interesting story. It could almost be interpreted as Back to the Future: Part 4.
+Hints mechanic to help you if you are being stuck.
+Stong voice acting skills of the actors.
+Christopher Lloyd voice acting his movie character, Doc Brown. Micheal J. Fox appeared for the final episode!
CONS:
-Filler between episodes: Seems to drag between later episodes.
-Technical issues: Each time I started a new episode, the game kept crashing until a game restart and then another restart once the settings were changed.
-Puzzles are somewhat easy but the HUD elements makes it hard at times to see where you have to click and is bothersome.
OVERALL:
A good adventure game. Not the best of Telltale Games and you cannot compare this to their "The Walking Dead" masterpiece series but I quite enjoyed this Back to the Future: The Game series.
RECOMMENDATION:
If you liked BttF movies and you like point & click adventure, goofy-funny games, you should really enjoy this BttF: The Game. You may want to wait for a sale though... as I did!
Just remember... it is not mandatory to have seen the movies BUT it really helps that you do! I watched the three movies just before starting this game and let me tell you that I would have been lost since it was so long ago! At least, read the synopsis of the movies before playing this game or you may feel lost here and there!
RATING:
7.0 / 10

TL;DR: A good game from Supergiant Games, definitely recommend playing it. But beware, there is much to read and if you don't like the core gameplay (the rites) then this game will disappoint you.
Gorgeous and breathtaking art aside, this games core mechanic, the Rites, is a really fun kind of soccer, almost reminiscent of Mario Strikers: Charged, but also vastly different in style. The different characters have different abilities with weaknesses and strengths, making it crucial to choose the right team against the opponents you are facing.
Main goal is to push a ball in the enemies fire (the pyre) and extinguish it, either by tossing yourself with the ball in there (easier, but with drawbacks for the next round) or just tossing the ball (more difficult, because easily interruptable, but no drawbacks).
The enemy however, having the same abilities as you, won't make it easy on you and every Rite plays different.
There is more, the story is also quite intriguing, slowly opening up to the player as he goes his way. The characters all have their own quirks and almost all of them are likable in their own way. However, the game gains another component after aprox. 4 hours of playtime, opening it up more, but also falling into repetition gameplay-wise. Midgame you experience the same procedure again and again, always interrupted by different story bits, but still, it is a loop and the story does not really move at this point.
Unfortunately I am quite sure the many "choices" you can make throughout the game (don't want to spoil anything) will not amount to as many endings as it wnats you to believe, because the sheer number of possible outcomes cannot be programmed into this little game.
All in all, the beautiful art, the unique gameplay and the possibilities unfolding as I play make this game pretty good. This certainly gets a high recommendation, everyone should try this, but also beware, there is much text and a lot of repeting gameplay mechanics midgame, making it a game that is NOT for everyone. Not Supergiants best game, especially story-wise, but very enjoyable nonetheless (for me at least).

Survarium is a really good game... on paper.
I can immediately find too many flaws in this game, though there are a few aspects I love about it.
Let's start with the good side.
The game is a nice break from all of the fast-paced, tight shooters that so many people love, for some odd reason. The sniping side of things is amazing when you aren't on the recieving end (more on that later), and the game feels leagues better than CoD, due to the fact that the enemies have no nameplates, and that I don't feel so enclosed on the maps. The fact that this game supports all types of weapons is amazing, simply due to the fact that there are many ways to play the game. The way the character moves is great for the most part (again, more on that later), and I enjoy being able to run farther than my grandma. Graphics aren't the best, but they certainly look good, and when you get a kill, it is extremely satisfying.
And now, the bad part.
The game is a snort-fest of death and spawn-campers, and the sniping factor on the recieving end annoys me to the point of breaking my screen. Keep in mind that this wouldn't be so bad if I could actually do something other than be target practice. And the tutorial basically tells you nothing except how to die. Here are just a few questions I had on how to play the game:
How do I stop bleeding?
What classes are there?
Is there a medic in this game? If so, why can't I use it?
How does the health system work? Note: I figured this out at about my fiftieth death. I lost my death count at twenty.
Can I modify my weapons?
Is there a way to swith loadouts and weapons in-game?
The matchmaking is♥♥♥♥♥♥poor, i.e. I would find a match, and I would lose my head to a die-hard sniper, and I would kill him once to his ten kills on me alone. Rince, repeat.  The crouching is like me getting on my knees, and the jumping is just lazy. I find the lack of weapon choice very disturbing (varieties of weapons, like a semi-auto sniper, or more than one to start with at the least, and this is especially bad in snipers), and the leveling system is confusing.
Overall, I really want to like the game, but I just can't. It is a great idea, and I wish it would have been executed better.

0.3h on steam release, ~200h on open beta non-steam client... proof in razr cortex:
Survarium has lots of potential but suffers from bad decisions along the way, bad/dirty monetization plan for a f2p, mishandling of the community, and false marketing as a 'MMOFPS' despite being currently a 8v8 instanced generic session FPS, and freeplay projected to have only up to 40 players interacting in instanced seperate session accross a closed map.
pros:
- sound design is top notch. their sound guy put a lot of effort and passion into it and it shows.
- map design in some of the maps is really good and gives a very unique soviet/post-apocalypitic "Direvna" feel to the game.
- well implemented (tho not perfectly balanced yet) RPG elements on gear and character trees.
- server-side hit detection.
cons:
- poorly implemented monetization plan that results in community frustration and no real incentive to invest your money in.
premium weapons come in few forms: premiums that don't have a freemium version but are weaker than gear rank competition or just simply sidegrades, premiums that have a freemium on the same gear rank but are much weaker because you're unable to add weapon mods to them like normal weapons, premiums that have a freemium on the same gear rank but that freemium is a RARE drop only item, premiums that have a freemium 2 gear ranks higher (which means the premium can be used earlier, against weaker freemium or premium gear, and have an advantage [proven through raw stats or dps calculations, having an advantage despite the freemiums it comepetes with have maxed out weapon mods]).
no way to obtain gold currency without paying anymore.
extremely expensive economy that is based on GAMBLING making combining items, or modding your gear the way you want pretty HARD to IMPOSSIBLE without spending real cash.
every turn you take in this game you're reminded how you're a 2nd class citizen in this world. it's literally shoved in your   face like planetside2's UPGRADE NOW era.
anything cosmetic atm just doesn't look good enough or appealing enough. UI has no way of examining before purchasing.
- outdated graphics in combination with poor optimization making the recommended specs feel like the minimum specs.
- mechanically input feels laggy, unresponsive, even with maxed out mobility character skill points and without a lot of weight load.
jumping sometimes occurs with a small delay. sprinting issues and jumping issues are claimed to be non issues because of momentum. if anything momentum is lacking in strafing where one can ADAD spam and abuse lag to his advantage without any penalty.
running towards objects or simply strafing around objects sometimes forces a climb you didn't really intend to make. even on high things that normally in other games would be climable only by jumping on them.
- some maps are extremely unbalanced towards one of the teams, and encourage spawn camping.
- weapon balance is not in a good state.
up to rank 12~ SMGs are making any other weapon type not viable. weapon effective ranges got shrinked due to map sizes and the SMG got a rather high effective range with 10-20 meters of difference from ARs only, while having a LOT easier recoil, way better hipfire, and generally being lighter (can make you faster).
from than on, there are snipers who 1 shot you from across the map, no matter where (it could be a foot shot or a hand shot). there are LMGs that are pinpoint accurate, pack a real punch, and their downsides are almost not felt due to character skill trees, gear mods, etc.
shotguns are pretty much not viable due to SMGs and ARs being way better and easier to use.
- lacks character roles or complexity in recoil or movement penalties. pvp modes are copied from other games in the genre, but are poorly implemented and buggy. turns it into a flat arena shooter.
- dev team and moderators are mishandling the community and are doing a really poor job at communicating. they tend to not be inline with one another, with the facts, or with what's going on. they tend to be biased towards "beta testers" who don't really criticize anything and are apologists, and quickly dismiss or ban any legit testers who come with feedback or criticism. there's also an issue where devs have shown bias towards the russian community and posted info only on russian forums (and no, more than a few devs know and can express themselves in english).
- game is mislabeled and falsely advertised as a MMOFPS. currently a 8v8 arena shooter. in the near future an instanced PVE mode with up to 40 players. which is not MMO, no matter what other games also use the word for. MMO stands for Massive interactions in a game envrionment (not just a chat room or lobby).

Honestly, I wanted to love this game. I'd give it a lower score than what I have based on how disappointed I am, but that's based on my own hype for the game that got rudely awoken by Ubisoft's laziness and greed. However, I will try to be fair and just grade it on what works and what doesn't.
1. P2P connections and shoddy base servers. You connect to whoever is hosting the match, and if that connection sucks, you're gonna suck. Base servers go down from time to time as well. There was a 7-hour outage today for example, and then it got fixed for an hour, and now it's down again. Not reliable in the slightest, and certainly not fair since the game has to be online to even play Singleplayer.
2. Bot logic is cowardly and cheap. Bots will sometimes abandon their duel with you to go swarm some lone player nearby. If not swarming some poor guy, the bots will often just spam their unblockable attacks or throw you around until you fall off a cliff. The bots have perfect timing on counters and comboes, and flawlessly execute them without shame or falter. You will have to spam the guarranteed-hits comboes and other free-damage type moves in order to beat them with actual combat. There's no catching them by surprise at all, so you can't do any damage without stunning them first, and even then, they can usually counter the stun. Then they spam their unblockable combo until they're out of stamina and back off. Eventually, everyone can be beaten somehow, but it's extremely tedious and sucks the fun out of the fight. Although, if you don't beat your opponent fast enough, and a teammate loses their duel, you better believe that the extra opponent is coming to swarm you. They will not hesitate to bounce you between attacks from three different people until you're dead. Revenge mode can prolong this fight a little longer so maybe a teammate can join the fight or you can get better positioned, but it's often not enough. Once the bots start swarming, you're basically screwed.
3. Matchmaking desperately needs more polish. The filter for "player skill" is extremely broad, and the gear values aren't calculated at all. This means you can have a fight between someone with Heroic armor and weapons maxed out to the highest level, against someone who picked up the game yesterday with 2 pieces of common armor and the rest being default. Very broken for the gamemodes that don't disable gear stats.
4. Steep learning curve. This is actually a good thing in disguise, but poorly handled. There is so much to learn with each hero to master them, but the game does not detail each special move or combo enough. Often found Youtubers to be a better teacher than the game's tutorials and practice modes. Needs more in-depth strategy training.
5, Unrewardling loot and impossible goals. Each hero can prestige somewhere around 40 times, I think. For this monumentous feat, you unlock a new pattern to customize your hero. The pattern is completely unremarkable and you will probably not use it. Gear stats are tied to specific gear, and while you can pay to switch the cosmetic appearance of your upgraded gear, you must first find the gear from scavenging or a lucky random drop. I feel like this limits the customization of each hero since usually you only find terrible weapons and armor with a random appearance. Scavenger crates do offer a way to get more specific loot, but it is still entirely random and you will often waste all your currency on crates that don't give you what you want, and selling crap-gear does not help you buy more crates. Oh, but you can buy more currency with real money, though! Business practice just screams: "Didn't get what you wanted in the first three crates? Try buying more!".
Final score : 7/10
The combat is fun and unlike any other game I've seen, but it is plagued by bad connectivity, unforgiving AI, broken matchmaking, shallow tutorials, and greedy business practice. Another fantastic premise ruined by the uncaring modern development standards of Ubisoft. The game is beautiful, immersive, skillful and brutal, but also sketchy, shallow, unreliable and underwhelming. I don't think any edition of the game is worth the asking price unless you're a diehard medieval fan. If your interest in this game contains "maybe" anywhere along the way, do yourself a favor and skip it.
And while I'm here, skip the Deluxe edition and the Gold edition too. Even if you're a die-hard fan. The best thing about these packs is the free Champion status, which you can get pretty easily anyway. Maybe the next round of DLC will make the Season Pass more worthwhile, but for now, it's entirely forgettable.
EDIT: 4/20/17
Many updates have come and gone, each adding some sort of cosmetic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t at a huge price. The currency system has been slightly buffed, so you now get 50% more money for completing orders. However, the game still frequently loses connection to the rewards server, meaning you do not get paid at all for any matches you complete if the server is down. This may be a cherry-picked example, but I played for two hours last night and one hour tonight... About 20 matches total? I think I only got paid for about 6 of them. And! My NAT type is frequently green, indicating a connection queue time. It has since degraded to yellow, meaning "not worst, but not good". In terms of balance, the most spammy class got buffed to have more value out of his spammy moves (Lawbringer) and Valkyrie got more damage overall since she had to stunlock enemies just to get any real damage done. The problem is now, she can still stunlock enemies with real damage output, and certain comboes can take away half your health if you don't counter the first hit.
I find myself utterly disappointed and actually ashamed I bought this game despite the warnings. I didn't think it was possible, but I dare say that this game actually took a TERRIBLE launch reception and made it WORSE.
I degrade my overall score of the game to 6/10. Graphics still beautiful, game itself runs pretty smooth, but the net connections, servers, business, balance, and reliability are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game had real potential and Ubisoft shoved it aside while leaping for a dollar on the ground.

Simply put, what we have here is a great concept poorly executed with terrible pacing and wonky controls, a game with flashes of brilliance that gets boring and tedious extremely fast, yet looks fun if heavily edited on Youtube. Some would even call it PewDiebait.
The game starts off promising: you're a "ghost hunter" camping out in the woods looking for something  not entirely natural. You grab your cameras, you grab your gun, and you set out to explore your surroundings and set up some surveillance. The atmosphere can actually be pretty good at times, and you'll probably experience a jump scare or two at some point, but then unfortunately, the game falls apart.
The cameras you set up? They occasionally provide you with a super-spooptacular glimpse of the creature, but you realize pretty quickly that your only goal is to kill the monster - and cameras don't help with that. Instead, you step outside your RV, wander a few feet away, wait for the sound of footsteps, turn, and fire.
Again, and again, and again. If you do this enough you kill the creature and you win. If you don't do this enough, you lose. You might think I'm exaggerating the simplicity of the game, but I'm not. This is literally what the game boils down to,  once you see through the uselessness of cameras, pigs, and exploring. Considering that's all this game has to offer, considering its extremely short length and redundancy, the wonky controls, fugly graphics and tedious mechanics, you're better off picking up something else for the $5 asking price.

The concept of a greek mythology-inspired game may sound run-of-the-mill, but Apotheon is anything but. The game is a metroidvania type of action-platformer, but uses very little rpg elements, which simplifies the mechanics for players new to the genre.
Your character does not level up, rather he gains extra health/protection and powers by upgrading his armor and weapons, and even honing his skill with select weapons such as the xiphos (sword) or spear.
You move with the standard WASD, but use the mouse to aim, attack and block; this can be confusing for players who haven't experienced this type of controls, and this ends up muddling the combat. Often, the player will be stabbing blindly at the air, simply because the cursor isn't at the proper elevation. Likewise, this can affect the player's speed when moving if the cursor isn't in the direction the player is headed.
The combat is not turn based, and most enemies can be dealt with only a few strikes of a sword or spear. However, enemies can pile up quickly and this is bothersome as running away is seldom a viable option considering the difficulties linked to platforming. The player is armed with only a modest jump and a stunted ledge grab to go through the levels.
The visual style is deceptively modest, taking on the the style of ancient greek pottery of colour-on-black. The characters move mostly fluidly, bar some repeated motions during dialogues, and the background is almsot always filled with  ancient greek forests, cities and the like.
Overall, Apotheon is a game that will frustrate the player in order to push them to do their best. The sometimes frustrating combat mechanics or platforming physics are easily overshadowed by the amazing visuals, immersive story and engaging gameplay.

This game provides me with some of the best memories I've ever had in gaming, but also some of the most frustrating (desyncs, ill get more into that later). Guild II is a very deep and interesting game. There's so many ways to play this game, you can be almost anything you want to be, a patron, scholar, craftsman or rogue. That's just the "class", you can actually be pretty much anything. A farmer, a banker, a banker, a priest, a stonemason, carpenter, gravedigger, thief, highwayman, politician... Too many to write in this review. Also the way you start with one character and get married, have children and progress through the generations is amazing. Let alone the fact that you're starting a family and working your business, you're also competing with other players/bots for position and power, being attacked, robbed, called to war and so much more. The interaction between players is so fun and hilarious at times. There's sooo many RPG elements and strategy elements in this game.  To me, this game is one of the best play-with-your-friends games of all time. I absolutely adore this game. The way you can work together against bots or compete together. The way you interact with eachother and the crime system is just fantastic.
Now to the problem I have with this game. Well, there's a few, but the BIG ONE, is that playing with your friends is almost impossible. I've tried time and time again but it constantly desyncs our game. We have downloaded patch after patch, tried fix after fix, all with no success. It's also not like you play, it desyncs and then you just leave, remake and load - It actually ruins the game, you have to start again. This absolutely destroys the game for me. I don't mind the singleplayer, it's good, but the multiplayer is AMAZING, thats what I WANT to play, but can't. It frustrates me that this was never fixed, because if it was, I would probably rate this as one of my favourite games of all time!
Now to some smaller problems. The graphics are dated, the character voice lines are hilariously bad, the AI can be kinda dumb, the balance is really bad between the professions and there's quite a few exploits and bugs in the game that were never fixed. The pacing can seem a bit off at times, the fact that you can just be "unlucky" and die of plague because there's no cure at that time is kinda lame. The fact that the market is like always out of resources and sometimes forces you to go to neighbouring towns can be annoying too. I'm sure there's many more I'm forgetting, but honestly these are nothing compared to the desync issue for me. Here's the thing though, if you only intend to play this game by yourself, wow you're in for a treat!
Graphics (For its style): 7
Sound: 8
Story: 9 (You make your OWN stories! The stories that come out of this game are amazing!)
Gameplay: 9
Game balance (how viable are different builds, is stuff overpowered or too weak): 5
Replay value (depth, amount of content, variety in gameplay): 10
Overall Rating:
This is really hard to review because this will change depending on how much you care about the multiplayer, but to me, that's what makes the game absolutely amazing. It has a good base, but the things you can do with friends makes it so much better!
That being said:
- If the desync problem and some bugs & exploits were fixed: 9/10 - Absolutely amazing game and HIGHLY recommend!
But since they're not, I have to say as a singleplayer experience: 7/10 - Solid, enjoyable game.

Based on trying this game for a short period of time, I think this is not a "game" at this point. Maybe more a "dinosaur sim"?
There is no interaction between dinosaurs other than the carnivore dinosaurs eating the the dinosaurs. If you are a herbavore, the game is boring - chomping on trees, hiding, and sneaking to drink water. There is no sense of goal or accomplishment.
If you player as a carnivore dinosaur, you do have some interaction with other dinosaurs - you fight them. But the fighting is boring and is mostly 1 v 1. Fighting consists of maneuvering your dinosaur to chomp on your opponents neck. Why not play a game that is focused on making fighting interesting (if that's what you are looking for).
To make this game interesting they need to introduce some sort of overarching goals and further encourage dinosaur vs. dinosaur interaction.
It seems like this game is more focused on the "sim" part of being a dinosaur (e.g. many types of dinosaur, special attack modes, different dinosaur "cries"), and less focused on the game part (introducing goals and achievements, encouraging interaction).
As it is right now the only interaction is 1v1 deathmatch combat. And outside of that all there is is walking around a sparsely populated world, chomping on trees (if you are a herbavore), drinking water, and resting.
Ideas:
1) everyone starts as a herbavore and 1 carnivore. When you become a carnivore you get points for how many kills you get. You get a certain amount of time and then another player becomes the carnivore (or whoever kills the carnivore).
2) scenario - a bunch of hebavores vs a small # of carnivores. Play out then switch sides.
The open world concept, based on what I saw doesn't work. Not enough interaction.

First off, I love supergiant games and their work - however, I'm not a fan of their latest game.
Their previous two games wonderfully wove story and gameplay together, which I think is absolutely the best (and only) good way to tell a story in a video game. Pyre, on the other hand, is constantly taking you from game to story and back again. The story is interesting so far but I'm personally not interested in clicking through pages of one liner dialogue. It's just a really inefficient storytelling technique as a book is tenfold faster while a movie is more engaging.
I guess it's best described as a "digital picture book" where you can't skip pages and each page takes a minimum of 1s to render. Imagine taking your favorite short story, splitting each sentence into difference pages, adding a few rarely changing portraits to each page, and then forcing yourself to read each page slowly, one by one.
The actual gameplay itself is quite fun, although somewhat shallow. If you removed the story/dialogue, there would be very little to do here.
Not recommended unless you are a fan of this type of game. Personally, I am just not the target audience I suppose.

It is so very different from the two prior released titles which in this case is not a bad thing. The game is less action RPG and more of a weird hybrid of a Visual Novel melded with some RPG elements and a sort of sports game. This works really well as, if you are a fan of Supergiants work, you will know full well that the atmosphere and aesthetic that their games ooze lends itself perfectly to something such as this.
The environments are beautiful, the characters are well designed and the detailed polish is all here. A signature of Supergiant to the T.
Gameplay wise as stated it is more akin to a visual novel majoritively so far. There's a lot of reading so if you're into that you'll get a lot out of the game. There are various decisions to be made along your path as well and as stated the various RPG elemnts which are impacted by said decisions. These effect how the sports-esc section can be influenced. Effectively you have a 3v3 game of American football (To specify) wherein you must carry the orb to the enemies fire pit and deposit it (Or alternately lob it in) sounds simple no?
That's the trick. Underlying this are various other mechanics such as character abilities, differing character types and the aforementioned RPG elements which all play into how you wish to partake in this segment of the game. Assumably as time goes on these differentiate further as is seen in the trailer to allow you to tailor your team to what you personally prefer.
So far I have been having a good time with the game and hope that if you are interested in Pyre that you may pick it up and try it for yourself. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

Despite all apparences, the game doesn't hate you.  It just treats you realistically.  You can die if your not careful, and you can die even if you are careful.
You are a soldier.  Not some overmuscled guy or a one man army.  You are part of a group.  A squad.  A part of something bigger.  You get the feeling when you start the game, that you are not important.  Because, you are just a guy.

There is not sure thing in this game.
The attention to detail is amazing.  I can't carry everything I could ever want or need on a mission.  I need to think my options through.  What do I need?  What am I doing?  Where am I going?
Treat the game as a realistic thing, and it will reward you with respect and an understanding of war.

Sniper Elite V2 is a not a particularly great game in any aspect but is fairly amusing, good-looking and adequately challenging most of the time. I would reccomend it, but only if it is on sale and you are a fan of long-distance combat and can accept the lack of any good kind of story.
The game features fairly standard cover-based shooting and snipering where your bullet is influenced by wind and drop-off. Aiming is a bit inaccurate when you are not using the sniper, but when  you are using it, in spite of whatever influences your bullet, in my case it became quite easy to just guess where to shoot. And when long-distance sniping is the core mechanic of the game, it makes for the game in general to be quite easy, apart from a few bumps in the difficulty curve.
Extraordinarily difficult bits occured when you encountered groups of Russians and Germans fighting eachother, or when you come across a tank. What I did like about it was that you can not just shoot the tank's gas can and cause it to explode, you have to hit the fuel cap instead. That is at the very least a bit more realistic and challenging and is therefore quite fun. Extremely frustrating however was one mission where you are tasked to kill a number of enemy snipers in a big open environment, who kill you with ease and are extremely hard to spot. But leaving aside a few exceptions, the game is no too hard.
Graphics are an area where this game shines, although the level of detail is not distributed quite equally. The player character, as well as the NPC's, look very good but the game world is left out a bit at times. In spite of that, the lighting and bright colors make the world pleasant to look at.
A few more nice things that this game features is an X-ray style vision of your target when a bullet flies through them, showing exactly what damage you did. What was also well done in my opinion was the feeling the city gave me. With idle conversations in German around me and the aforementioned nice visuals in the city it did manage to convey the atmosphere of the war-torn city.
What bothers me most about it is that there is nothing special about it, except for the X-ray thing. The gun mechanics and atmosphere are nice, but it is all you get and that is not enough for some people. The story, for instance, is quite boring. The game is set in Berlin in the last few weeks of World War II and you play as an American sniper sent to kill a few high-ranking German scientists as well as some of the Russians that are invading the city at that time. The biggest problem with the story, apart from the fact that nothing truly interesting or imaginative happens, is that it is only brought across by a voice during the pre-mission menu. This is no aspect of the game that is relevant.
I would reccomend this game anyway, because of that it can be something nice if it is on sale and you are looking for nothing else besides amusing gunplay.

I have updated this review after I tried the release 1.0 version. My verdict is largely the same.
The game has definitely improved since my impressions from Early Access, and can, if the developers keep improving it here after release 1.0, in time have enough gameplay to make it fun (not quite there yet). At the moment it has some flaws that makes the game unbearable to play for me.
No in-game pause:
One big flaw is the fact that this the inability to pause in-game.
This is a game about survival where you have to manage a lot of things that constantly degrade and break down and the more people you have and the bigger your shelter gets, the more this will require your attention. Sure, it is no problem at the start, but it quickly becomes a problem. Many of the things require attention fast and especially when a lot of things are happening at once does this problem really show itself. Only way to pause is by going to the options menu where you can't see nor interact with anthing. It is unnecessarily stressing and just makes you frustrated in stead of adding anything to the game.
I cannot for the life of me understand why the game doesn't even pause when you are rearranging the furniture in your shelter. Placing an object one pixel left or right can mean the difference between being able to fit one more object beside it. Either pause while I fiddle with this or give me the option to have objects snap to nearly objects. Rearranging your bunker will quickly take 12-in game hours.
Automation:
This brings us to another big flaw in the game: Automation that doesn't really work.
Release version edit: This has not changed enough. Your people still stand around untill something is 60% bad (60% dehydrated / 60% crapping my pants / etc.). One thing that has changed to the better is, that you can now repair items, while they are being used, so when you repair an item has much less impact on the game -- it has essentially been reduced to a breakdown timer you have to rewind.
Yes, you can automate your people, but this is a badly implemented solution since it means full automation or no automation. Your people (when not on automation) will stand still next to a full container of water and die of thirst if you don't select them and click the water. This is mobile game level of gameplay (= bad).
What this means is that you either let your people do whatever they please (not a very good idea) or you spend most of the game clicking on people and then a bed, shower, toilet, food, water, etc. just to keep them alive and happy. Automation also means they will stand around and do nothing at all until things are nearly broken before even considering fixing anything. They will not maintain equipment which can be a bit annoying because you have to manually repair everything if you need things at peak condition. Even when on automation, they will just stand still in a bunker that is running out of air while alarms are blaring and suffocate. Move 5 metres and live? No, I'll just stand here and die, thank you.
A fix to this would be to make automation much more fine-grained. If I, for example, could tell everyone to sleep if they are tired (20%/40% or more) and there is a free bed, then I would not have to keep doing boring things. Make auto-sleep/drink/poop/etc. an upgrade, if you really think micromanaging is a good thing when you start a new game. The release version has the automation fixed for everything at 60%.
Interface:
Last thing that makes me not like playing the game is the interface.
You will most likely play zoomed out since that shows you your entire shelter and let's you see and react to everything, that is going on inside it. Zoomed in (default view mode) is like playing with your face smooshed against the screen. So, it is a good thing that you can zoom out.
Problem is, that if you click the expand button on the selected character, it effectively covers up all of the entrance area of the shelter while zoomed out. The expand button shows their needs, so unless you have every single character on auto (which is a bad idea, as I described above) then you will need this info all the time, Since the game does not let you unselect people, you will have to unexpand the info area, then do whatever you need to do and expand it again after. In a game where time keeps running and you are stressed, this goes from being sligtly inconvenient to rageinducingly annoying.
The inability to unselect also becomes tiring really really fast once two or more characters are stading close to each other. Select is left mouse button, move is also left mouse button. Want to select that character A standing next to character B, who is in the middle of doing something? Oops, selected B. Ok, try again. Oops, just told B to move to where you clicked. Ok, remove that move job from B's job queue. Try again. Oops, once again told B to move.
There is an option to cycle through characters in the bunker with Q and E, but if you have more than the starting 4 it really is a clunky way to do it.
Unless people are outside, where there is danger, you almost never use the move command. It is almost exclusively used to move people inside. And even that is not something you need to do very often since they move inside automatically after completing tasks outside. Unless you moved them outside manually and left them there doing nothing, So why left mouse button is overloaded with the move command is anyone's guess. I would call it bad interface design.
Conclusion:
If none of the above things seem like big problems to you, then I think you might enjoy the game. It's a really good idea made by a team that seems to want to make a good game, which is also why I kickstarted the game way back when. For me the flaws outweight the pleasure of playing the game.
TL;DR:
Game has promise, but unless some serious flaws get fixed/design choices are changed (pause, automation, and interface are at the top of the list), I would not recommend this game. If these things get fixed and the gameplay get's fleshed out a bit I think this could be a good game.
