This game is beautiful. It's clearly old and hasn't aged quite well in some aspects, but it remains as one of the best rpgs you can get on the market.
Welcome to Star Wars, set after the Mandalorian Wars that nearly wiped out all the Jedi. You are an exile from the jedi order, and don't think you get any time to rest, as you're attacked and captured by the Sith, who are hell bent on destroying all remaining jedi. Now it's up to you to escape and reunite the remaining Jedi, OR destroy them and the Sith and be the strongest in the galaxy.
This game can be summed up as Fallout Star Wars DLC. You can repair bots, hack doors, overload terminals, fight with light sabers, choke people with the force, use blasters, almost everything you can imagine.
Game looks a bit ugly, as it aged not all that well, and it has some gameplay design choices that will infuriate you (you will learn dark rituals just so you can curse the developers for forced solo battles using other characters). You'll create your character with gender, pick from different faces, your class, distribute stats and powers, learn new force moves and depending on your build, you'll have a variety of means to deal with situations (a personal advice is to get force persuade as soon as possible. Have a lot of persuasion, it'll save your skin).
Say good bye to boring clitche quests, as this game often has you investigating murders (or murdering someone special yourself, like a war general, for profit), repairing droids to get information from them, de-throning queens, and your various actions can give you light or dark side points (such as performing a task for free or threatning someone to get a better reward), and those actions will impact how your teammates react to you, giving you more or less influence. Influence by the way, reflects how much a teammate trusts you, and that will say if they'll be willing to tell you their secrets and trust you in battle.
A beautiful soundtrack follows you, alongside a carefully crafted world and story (aliens have their own language like in the movies), and often times they'll react differently to your choices. You'll constantly question if what you're doing is the right thing and how the others might react if you do this or that.
The A.I can be a problem though, as your friends may struggle with walking around obstacles very often. Said trick can be abused though, and can often times make hard bosses freeze in place or not have enough time to attack you (force storm, run, force storm, run).
At the long run, Kotor 2 The Sith Lords is a magnificent gem that has aged like a fine wine and i definently reccomend it

Honestly, I wanted to love this game. I'd give it a lower score than what I have based on how disappointed I am, but that's based on my own hype for the game that got rudely awoken by Ubisoft's laziness and greed. However, I will try to be fair and just grade it on what works and what doesn't.
1. P2P connections and shoddy base servers. You connect to whoever is hosting the match, and if that connection sucks, you're gonna suck. Base servers go down from time to time as well. There was a 7-hour outage today for example, and then it got fixed for an hour, and now it's down again. Not reliable in the slightest, and certainly not fair since the game has to be online to even play Singleplayer.
2. Bot logic is cowardly and cheap. Bots will sometimes abandon their duel with you to go swarm some lone player nearby. If not swarming some poor guy, the bots will often just spam their unblockable attacks or throw you around until you fall off a cliff. The bots have perfect timing on counters and comboes, and flawlessly execute them without shame or falter. You will have to spam the guarranteed-hits comboes and other free-damage type moves in order to beat them with actual combat. There's no catching them by surprise at all, so you can't do any damage without stunning them first, and even then, they can usually counter the stun. Then they spam their unblockable combo until they're out of stamina and back off. Eventually, everyone can be beaten somehow, but it's extremely tedious and sucks the fun out of the fight. Although, if you don't beat your opponent fast enough, and a teammate loses their duel, you better believe that the extra opponent is coming to swarm you. They will not hesitate to bounce you between attacks from three different people until you're dead. Revenge mode can prolong this fight a little longer so maybe a teammate can join the fight or you can get better positioned, but it's often not enough. Once the bots start swarming, you're basically screwed.
3. Matchmaking desperately needs more polish. The filter for "player skill" is extremely broad, and the gear values aren't calculated at all. This means you can have a fight between someone with Heroic armor and weapons maxed out to the highest level, against someone who picked up the game yesterday with 2 pieces of common armor and the rest being default. Very broken for the gamemodes that don't disable gear stats.
4. Steep learning curve. This is actually a good thing in disguise, but poorly handled. There is so much to learn with each hero to master them, but the game does not detail each special move or combo enough. Often found Youtubers to be a better teacher than the game's tutorials and practice modes. Needs more in-depth strategy training.
5, Unrewardling loot and impossible goals. Each hero can prestige somewhere around 40 times, I think. For this monumentous feat, you unlock a new pattern to customize your hero. The pattern is completely unremarkable and you will probably not use it. Gear stats are tied to specific gear, and while you can pay to switch the cosmetic appearance of your upgraded gear, you must first find the gear from scavenging or a lucky random drop. I feel like this limits the customization of each hero since usually you only find terrible weapons and armor with a random appearance. Scavenger crates do offer a way to get more specific loot, but it is still entirely random and you will often waste all your currency on crates that don't give you what you want, and selling crap-gear does not help you buy more crates. Oh, but you can buy more currency with real money, though! Business practice just screams: "Didn't get what you wanted in the first three crates? Try buying more!".
Final score : 7/10
The combat is fun and unlike any other game I've seen, but it is plagued by bad connectivity, unforgiving AI, broken matchmaking, shallow tutorials, and greedy business practice. Another fantastic premise ruined by the uncaring modern development standards of Ubisoft. The game is beautiful, immersive, skillful and brutal, but also sketchy, shallow, unreliable and underwhelming. I don't think any edition of the game is worth the asking price unless you're a diehard medieval fan. If your interest in this game contains "maybe" anywhere along the way, do yourself a favor and skip it.
And while I'm here, skip the Deluxe edition and the Gold edition too. Even if you're a die-hard fan. The best thing about these packs is the free Champion status, which you can get pretty easily anyway. Maybe the next round of DLC will make the Season Pass more worthwhile, but for now, it's entirely forgettable.
EDIT: 4/20/17
Many updates have come and gone, each adding some sort of cosmetic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t at a huge price. The currency system has been slightly buffed, so you now get 50% more money for completing orders. However, the game still frequently loses connection to the rewards server, meaning you do not get paid at all for any matches you complete if the server is down. This may be a cherry-picked example, but I played for two hours last night and one hour tonight... About 20 matches total? I think I only got paid for about 6 of them. And! My NAT type is frequently green, indicating a connection queue time. It has since degraded to yellow, meaning "not worst, but not good". In terms of balance, the most spammy class got buffed to have more value out of his spammy moves (Lawbringer) and Valkyrie got more damage overall since she had to stunlock enemies just to get any real damage done. The problem is now, she can still stunlock enemies with real damage output, and certain comboes can take away half your health if you don't counter the first hit.
I find myself utterly disappointed and actually ashamed I bought this game despite the warnings. I didn't think it was possible, but I dare say that this game actually took a TERRIBLE launch reception and made it WORSE.
I degrade my overall score of the game to 6/10. Graphics still beautiful, game itself runs pretty smooth, but the net connections, servers, business, balance, and reliability are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game had real potential and Ubisoft shoved it aside while leaping for a dollar on the ground.
Sorry for the long review, I just find it very difficult to summarize how EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING this game has turned out to be. I would even turn away hardcore melee/medieval fans now. It looks good on paper, but this is one big trashcan of an experience.
If you're considering For Honor... I say this: Regardless of your interest, skill, wealth, and patience, turn away and don't look back. This game is a ham-fisted failure.

I'm a long time Mythology nerd who's looking into an archaeology major and reads about ancient history for fun. I logged into steam, saw this game on sale, and resigned myself to buying it.
It was amazing.
Media accurately depicting the Greek Gods is hard to find, and doubly so for video games. "Someone is god of the wrong thing" is a square on my mythology movie bingo card. But Apotheon completely nails everything. This game wasn't written by people who read through a couple wikipedia pages and called it day; literally everything about the Gods is correct, from their attitudes to their ironic demise, and even their allegences. One of the most telling moments was having Dionysus on the side of humanity; someone who'd only done cursory research wouldn't know that he'd lived among mortals for years before joining the gods.
And don't even get me started on the art. This game is one of the most beautiful things I've ever played. Everything is stylized perfectly down to the creases in a character's chiton, and the color changes in the different realms are beautiful and perfectly fit the tone of the area. The architecture is accurate, as are the items and decorations. The NPC dialogue and major themes of the story even parallel important values of Ancient Greek life.
Basically: the devs for this game researched the hell out of Ancient Greece, and I kind of want to kiss every one of them for it. 10/10.

Holy mother of power fantasies, this game is amazing.
The story is based on ancient Greek mythology, though it is not the game's strongest point. The combat is very satisfying and generally fantastic. It reminds me very much of the combat system in Dark Souls, but instead, it's in 2D.
The player takes the role of Nikandreos, who wakes up in the middle of a siege on his home village by bandits. After killing these bandits, you learn that the gods have forsaken humanity and no longer wish for them to exist. Upon going into the temple, Hera appears in front of Nikandreos and tells him that they could form a partnership. She has had enough of Zeus cheating on her with other deities and even mortals, while Nikandreos has an interest in humanity not being wiped out. Hera teleports Nikandreos to the gates of Olympus, where he is tasked with gathering the strenght of all the major gods around and prepare to overthrow Zeus, the king of gods, himself.
As you can see from the pictures and the trailers, the game has a unique artstyle in that it looks like ancient Greek pots. The soundtrack supports this artstyle and setting very well and the sound effects are very good.
One thing to note with this game is that the bossfights are very cool and unique. This does not go for minibosses sadly, as they're mainly just something bigger than everything else and otherwise behave as all others.
Overall, I had a blast.

Classic FPS, very accessible and easy to pick up and play for newcommers to the fps genre yet challenging for veterans. There are 5 difficulty levels which dramatically effect the way the game plays. Whether you're looking for some hardcore action with unforgivable enemies or you want to breeze through with a chaingun tearing the demons to pieces, you should play doom.
The levels are huge and very easy to get lost in, there are tonnes of secrets to look out for too and loads of ammo/health kits to keep you energized, you can either explore these huge demon filled labyrinths looking for secrets or breeze through the level trying to beat your best time. The art design is great, the computer/monitor sprites are rather detailed for it's time and the enemy designs are very detailed too, particularly the hulking demon enemies you will fight later on in the game. There are also several obtainable weapons and you can carry 1 of each weapon, no stupid 2 weapon limit, once you find a weapon, it's yours... until you die but you can jsut reload a save if you want to keep them, there are some really cool weapons like the minigun and the BFG which differ from your conventional FPS weapon arsenal.
The only issue is that you may occasionally find yourself in a dark room, now this is expected in a game like doom, however the flashing lights can be a bit uneasy on the eyes, it would have been better if the flashing was slowed down a touch, i don't reccommend this game to anybody with epilepsy but to everybody else, if you're remotely interested in the roots of the FPS genre or you want to have some kick♥♥♥♥♥old school FPS action, you need to get this game now!
Do note that considering it's age, Doom is missing vital features of more modern FPS such as the ability to aim up and down so it may confuse players who are used to more modern shooters but don't worry as the game will auto aim at enemies in line with your gun no matter what height they are.

The game is lacking some basic animation as well. Unlike the Asteroids game we know and love, the asteroids do not break apart or even appear to explode. They literally just disappear when hit. Not even a few pixel dots scatter.
So overall I found it disappointing to say the least. An otherwise great and probably well-selling game fell short due to some lazy programming. I would say to the creators to pick it back up and just focus on user experience. Everything else is there.

The setting is so beautifully expressed through the fantastic graphics Apotheon has to offer. Everything blends together well while keeping the foreground action obvious. Never do you get confused or lose your character. The art direction is exceptional.
The controls are soooooooo tight—they would have to be to make the crux of the gameplay so manageable and easygoing. You're rewarded for going out of your way to explore little nooks, finding more and new weapons and armors to better define
playstyle. You may not like swords for their short range, so you decide to use spears, although you might not like spears for their stabbing attack animations, so you start using maces for their arch and shield-breaking capabilities.... You decide how you want to play Apotheon... It gives you the freedom to go wild. I believe that might be where people make the comparison with Dark Souls: How you can be plotted right into a battlefield with no hand-holding, having to learn on your own. The soundtrack, produced by Marios Aristopoulos, is phenominal. From the moment you begin your epic, to your final battle, Marios compliments the beautiful scenery with a range of ambient to intense music (all strings, by the way) to create the perfect atmosphere!
Enemies are difficult as

That being said. I consider to have played enough to try and write something unbiased about this game.
Pros :
The game is fun as hell especially with voice coms or a pre determined group of friends. I have not had fun like that in years murdering my friends :)
Gun Media has been working their butts off to make this work. You could tell they were extremely excited when the friday license was offered to them. They seriously absolutely love the game they created. You can feel that love in game if you pay attention to the environment. You could also tell they are extremely hurt by the reaction from the community about the server issues.
The jump scares. Before Stalk the game would end up being boring and you started to get immune to the anxiety you would feel while being chased. The stalk ability changed that and i was able to extract some very manly tears on my murder spree.
The kills are some of my favorite aspect of this game. It feels very Jason like and voice coms only improve this aspect.
The feeling of dread, especially after some Counselors have died and you realize you will eventually be next.
Cons :
The price - Ultimately you need to decide for yourself if the game is worth it to you, there are plenty of streamers where you can build your opinion about the game.
Griefers- I dont know why but this game is attracting a lot of Jerks, im not talking about the ones that abandon you to die. No, people that aim personal attacks at your Ethnicity or gender. I have been in 3 games where people straight up sexually harrassed a female gamer, directed personal attacks at them ( using the C word) or made racial remarks because the guy had an heavy accent.
The server issues - Yes this one sucks and is also why most bad reviews have been written. I personally dont get why you would write a review if you cant even log on but hey to each their own. I could explain what makes this game a great experience with a group of friends or on a rainy day against five AIs but this type of game is best reviewed with a story from gameplay.
I'm Oliver Tumblesnatch, an honest ironsmith based near the center of the city. My journey starts with paying a man 1500 gold to marry his daughter, I'm sure she was fine with it. I work all day in the forge while my wife stays home with our two infant sons. This goes on for years and I'm always struggling to break even between buying sparsely available materials and selling shoddy products on the market, as I'm never wealthy enough to make any improvements to my business, or increase my own social standing in the city. Meanwhile, another family dynasty, led by one Birinius Adilger, is making a killing off of thuggery and thievery, and yet remains a prestigious figure in the society. Putting my own frustrations aside, I continue to walk the straight and narrow for years, working in the forge, selling in the market, praying in the church, and repeating.
One day, on my way to the forge, I post a slanderous poem about the aforementioned uncouth character Birinius (the author's name graciously omitted) on the town bulletin. Sometimes after finishing some metal tools I'd take a look to see the laughter of those reading the poem in the road and saying, "I can't believe Adilger would say something like that!" or "Why that does sound like Birinius Adilger doesn't it." Despite not ever being confronted for this little jape, it would be the initiation of the family rivalry between the Tumblesnatch and Adilger dynasties.
It was when my sons came of age to work for the family that my days of honest living came to an abrupt end. The supplies of iron had stopped coming into the town market, so I no longer had any materials with which to forge, and on top of this I had never been able to afford sending my sons to school, so they wouldn't be of much use when it came to expanding the family business. It was this fateful combination of most unfortunate circumstances that led me to sell my forge, the family's only means of making money in the market. But what we lost in monetary value we made up for in practical utilities. Using the money I got from the forge I bought a dagger for myself, my wife, and my two sons. My money which came from sales in the market was replaced with money taken from the purses of victims, the tax collector, the mayor's wife, and a handful of average civilians straying too far from the road, and I made more than I ever had working at the forge.
Unbeknownst to me, Mr. Adilger had witnessed one of these crimes, and I was notified that I was to appear in court the following morning. I can't remember what it was exactly the charges filed against me, but I can remember immediately going to the court and scheduling a trial against Birinius for the morning after my own, assuming I wasn't in the dungeon or under the axe. The trial came and by some stroke of good fortune or divine intervention, I was ruled not guilty by an agreement of all but one of the jurors.
Later that day while sitting in the town square accompanied by my wife and children, a gang of Adilger's thugs led by Birinius himself charged us. A brawl broke out briefly fought with daggers and fists, and quickly broken up by the armored town guards who killed two of Birinius' hired blades and brought a quick end to the scuffle. Here a great victory was established for the Tumblesnatch Rat Pack, as few were the townspeople who were unaware of the day's events. The next day the pivotal trial was to take place. Birinius and myself both arrived forty-five minutes early, with a band of jurors trickling in leading up to the commence. The words exchanged were vicious and energized, but ultimately unnecessary, Birinius could do little to dissuade the jury. The verdict was set, exile from city boundaries for ten years.
It was a new city as I stepped out of the court room, I felt like the king despite the technicality of being a "Citizen Without Full Legal Rights." We continued the game for about four years time, with the occasional run in (or run through) in the woods or the fields outside of the city walls, but after our starting characters had died of old age we never did continue playing as the second generation.

Alright, this will upset some fan boys. Do not freak out, please. To be honest, I wanted to like this game, loving Supergiant for Bastion and a bit for Transistor, but Pyre does not work for me.
It is a bad competitive game, if you are into competitive games. If you are mainly into RPG’s, or similar, you may find it interesting or challenging, I think. For a competitive game it just feels cheap and weak like so many similar games. In short: an RPG developer tries a competitive game and fails, with weak UI and weird decisions. It happened before. It is actually more of a 3-v-3 Rocket League (with an orb), as others wrote, but with a weird design choice that you can only control one character at the time, while having 3 on the board. So to speak.
To me, who is playing all kind of competitive games, it looks as if competitive gameplay is not their thing. It's boring, frankly speaking, and does not feel balanced and well tested. After having seen the game at conferences, I wondered already if the final game will work. My impression at the confs was that the audiences didn’t get it or were bored. I did hope that they would polish it, or change a few things, so people that are coming straight from Bastion and Transistor do no get too disappointed. I hope it sells okay at least, so it was worth the try (for which kudos to Supergiant).
There is a story, but it does not work like in the past games. It feels on top of some competitive gameplay, which happens sometimes in this genre, which they should have avoided, in order to be perhaps more innovative, I think.
Pro
- art style is nice, not overall, but often enough
- sound and music is great, as always
Contra
- combat animations are weak and weird sometimes
- weak UI for this game type, like more for RPG than competitive players (complicated)
- too many unnecessary text boxes, too many “click to proceed” moments
- overall, it is probably a cheap hero competitive game
- if you ask me: nothing special, from a competitive gameplay perspective
- also linear and a bit inconsequential story gameplay
- felt like a Rocket League clone sometimes, but this could be the orb/goal thing ;)
There are plenty of better competitive games out there. Wait for sales, if you need it.

When I first wrote a review for this game, it was while it first released, and I mostly talked about it it's inexcusably shoddy launch. I know that a lot of games have poor launches, but that's not an excuse. Just because some other companies can't get it right, doesn't mean that others are exempt. A few problems are fine, but being unable to play the game for several days? Major bugs and glitches and crashes? There's no excuse for it. But now that the game is, for the most part, playable, I will write an actual review of it.
To begin, let's talk about it and Dead by Daylight and get that comparison out of the way, as it is something a lot of people want to know. First, this game does it's killer far more justice than Dead by Daylight, where playing Killer is a nightmare sometimes.  I still find playing Jason to be tedious, however, as Counselors can evade Jason sometimes by just running around a building and leaping in and out of windows. Characters with higher stamina and speed with med spray can do this for even longer durations. Even with the shift, it can still be tricky to catch them. Still, it's easier to find your victims and catch them off-guard, which helps with chasing.
There are more things to do, more ways to escape, which makes it less repetitive than Dead by Daylight's generators and gates. And, you are able to fight back and you're not just limited to running away. Finally, all of the Counselors have their own strengths and weaknesses, and it actually matters who you chose. It's not like Dead by Daylight where literally all Survivors can eventually do everything that all the others can do.
But that's where the praise ends.
My biggest gripe with this game is that it is way too easy for a Counselor to accomplish nothing. For me, a lot of games go like this:
Spawn as Deborah. Go into Cabin to look for stuff. Find nothing useful. Go to next cabin. Find medspray and a bat. No parts. Go to next cabin. Cabin has already been searched by other Counselors. Jason shows up. Jason shifts on top of me. Die.
This happens to me almost every other round. Either Jason just happens to find me or someone getting chased brings him to me, only for them to die and then Jason come after me next. You spend five minutes trying to do something useful to your team. Even if I die after putting something in the car, the boat, or the phone, at least I did something. I know this isn't technically the game's fault, it could just be poor luck on my part, but still, the fact that this game makes it that easy for you to accomplish literally nothing is a little off putting.
Jason's ability to shift and then grab and auto kill you plays into this. To be clear, I really have no problem with Jason's ability to grab and then execute, even after shifting. The problem is, the ability to do this directly negates the Counselor's combat and the ability to execute on command makes attempting to break free virtually pointless. This makes the stats Compsure, Luck, and Strength worthless, as fighting Jason is suicidal as his grabs can interrupt your attacks and sometimes, due to poor detection, your hits won't even register. This makes it so the best way to survive is to avoid Jason entirely, so Stealth is a priority, which is why most people play Eric, AJ, Tiffany, and Deborah.
Another issue is that Jason can trap all objectives of the Counselors, placing his bear traps at the door of the cars, in front of the phone box, on the dock of the boat, and that basically covers all four escape routes. Traps can be disarmed via a pocketknife, but those can be hard to come across. Plus, no one wants to sacrifice one to disarm a trap, as the pocketknife is the only way to reliably escape Jason's grasp. This basically forces Counselors to deliberately walk on Jason's traps to get rid of them. This alerts Jason and he then goes right over and murders the person and everyone nearby. This wouldn't be so much of a problem if Jason's grab wasn't so easy to pull off and Composure was such a pointless stat.
Bugs and glitches are rampant in the game. The hair of character models glitch out sometimes. Jason can be sent to orbit after hitting him while he grabs someone from the car. Achievements don't work. I one time got stuck under a bed after Jason killed someone in the bed next to me. Jason can be rendered powerless if people quit while he is killing them. The car one time randomly stood upright on it's back somehow after just going in reverse, making it inacessible. Hits against Jason don't register. Some perks don't work properly.
There is no option to play as Jason and Jason only. This is not so much a problem for myself, as I really don't care who I play as (and I usually prefer the Counselors anyway). But it is when you consider that 98% of the people who bought this game are major fans of the series who probably bought for the sole reason of getting to be Jason Voorhees and murdering everyone they see as their favorite horror film slasher. When they don't get Jason, they quit the match, leaving five or four players against Jason, which is almost impossible (if not entirely) to win against. So, if you are thinking of buying this game and playing a lot of rounds as Jason, you might want to reconsider, as you will play Jason typically 10% of the time, while playing as Counselor the other 90%. This can be bad for some players as it can be extremely difficult to get your strategy down as Jason when you don't get to play as him very often. Each time I finally get to play as him, I have to remember how to play as him as I'm usually surprised I even got him. I've heard some people going thirty plus games without ever being Jason.
The last complaint is the price. Currently, the game has one mode with three maps. That's it. There is no Single Player mode yet, which is odd considering the game was delayed so that it would be included. Dead By Daylight is half the price of this game. Now I know what you're thinking, "But in order to get everything, you have to buy DLC! And that makes it way more expensive!" True, but even if you don't buy any DLC, you still get more. You can still play all the maps, you can get offerings to play the DLC Killers once in awhile, and you can still get their perks via the Shrine of Secrets. In the private Kill Your Friends mode, there is an option to enable access to DLC Killers as well. Even if you buy no DLC, you still get more than what you get in Friday the 13th as of this moment. I know that more content for Friday the 13th will surely come, but it's hard to justify a price, when most of it is for features that won't come until well after release.
To be sure, this game is not bad, but it is definitely one you need friends for. You need coordination to do well in this game, and, even with voice chat enabled, I find a lot of lobbies with people who either don't talk or don't speak English, which severely handicaps the Survivors when you don't know what their doing or what items they have. It is very easy for your fellow Survivors to die with important items on them and then you have no idea where that item is, effectively cutting off a route of escape. Dead by Daylight's generators may be repetitve, but at least they can't be misplaced by hapless teammates.
This game has a lot of potential, and it is fun when it works properly. But it has a lot of problems and a lot of times you will die without getting to do anything and then you're stuck spectating everyone else just so you can get more points so you can get more CP so you can get more stuff for your Counselors and Jason. It's not a good sign when more than half of your play time can potentially be sitting and watching other people play. At least in Dead by Daylight you can just leave without missing out on more XP (or Bloodpoints, as they're called in that game).
Overall, it's not worth the price, it's buggy, it's easy to accomplish nothing, and if you're looking to play as Jason a lot, you won't.

I have updated this review after I tried the release 1.0 version. My verdict is largely the same.
The game has definitely improved since my impressions from Early Access, and can, if the developers keep improving it here after release 1.0, in time have enough gameplay to make it fun (not quite there yet). At the moment it has some flaws that makes the game unbearable to play for me.
No in-game pause:
One big flaw is the fact that this the inability to pause in-game.
This is a game about survival where you have to manage a lot of things that constantly degrade and break down and the more people you have and the bigger your shelter gets, the more this will require your attention. Sure, it is no problem at the start, but it quickly becomes a problem. Many of the things require attention fast and especially when a lot of things are happening at once does this problem really show itself. Only way to pause is by going to the options menu where you can't see nor interact with anthing. It is unnecessarily stressing and just makes you frustrated in stead of adding anything to the game.
I cannot for the life of me understand why the game doesn't even pause when you are rearranging the furniture in your shelter. Placing an object one pixel left or right can mean the difference between being able to fit one more object beside it. Either pause while I fiddle with this or give me the option to have objects snap to nearly objects. Rearranging your bunker will quickly take 12-in game hours.
Automation:
This brings us to another big flaw in the game: Automation that doesn't really work.
Release version edit: This has not changed enough. Your people still stand around untill something is 60% bad (60% dehydrated / 60% crapping my pants / etc.). One thing that has changed to the better is, that you can now repair items, while they are being used, so when you repair an item has much less impact on the game -- it has essentially been reduced to a breakdown timer you have to rewind.
Yes, you can automate your people, but this is a badly implemented solution since it means full automation or no automation. Your people (when not on automation) will stand still next to a full container of water and die of thirst if you don't select them and click the water. This is mobile game level of gameplay (= bad).
What this means is that you either let your people do whatever they please (not a very good idea) or you spend most of the game clicking on people and then a bed, shower, toilet, food, water, etc. just to keep them alive and happy. Automation also means they will stand around and do nothing at all until things are nearly broken before even considering fixing anything. They will not maintain equipment which can be a bit annoying because you have to manually repair everything if you need things at peak condition. Even when on automation, they will just stand still in a bunker that is running out of air while alarms are blaring and suffocate. Move 5 metres and live? No, I'll just stand here and die, thank you.
A fix to this would be to make automation much more fine-grained. If I, for example, could tell everyone to sleep if they are tired (20%/40% or more) and there is a free bed, then I would not have to keep doing boring things. Make auto-sleep/drink/poop/etc. an upgrade, if you really think micromanaging is a good thing when you start a new game. The release version has the automation fixed for everything at 60%.
Interface:
Last thing that makes me not like playing the game is the interface.
You will most likely play zoomed out since that shows you your entire shelter and let's you see and react to everything, that is going on inside it. Zoomed in (default view mode) is like playing with your face smooshed against the screen. So, it is a good thing that you can zoom out.
Problem is, that if you click the expand button on the selected character, it effectively covers up all of the entrance area of the shelter while zoomed out. The expand button shows their needs, so unless you have every single character on auto (which is a bad idea, as I described above) then you will need this info all the time, Since the game does not let you unselect people, you will have to unexpand the info area, then do whatever you need to do and expand it again after. In a game where time keeps running and you are stressed, this goes from being sligtly inconvenient to rageinducingly annoying.
The inability to unselect also becomes tiring really really fast once two or more characters are stading close to each other. Select is left mouse button, move is also left mouse button. Want to select that character A standing next to character B, who is in the middle of doing something? Oops, selected B. Ok, try again. Oops, just told B to move to where you clicked. Ok, remove that move job from B's job queue. Try again. Oops, once again told B to move.
There is an option to cycle through characters in the bunker with Q and E, but if you have more than the starting 4 it really is a clunky way to do it.
Unless people are outside, where there is danger, you almost never use the move command. It is almost exclusively used to move people inside. And even that is not something you need to do very often since they move inside automatically after completing tasks outside. Unless you moved them outside manually and left them there doing nothing, So why left mouse button is overloaded with the move command is anyone's guess. I would call it bad interface design.
Conclusion:
If none of the above things seem like big problems to you, then I think you might enjoy the game. It's a really good idea made by a team that seems to want to make a good game, which is also why I kickstarted the game way back when. For me the flaws outweight the pleasure of playing the game.
TL;DR:
Game has promise, but unless some serious flaws get fixed/design choices are changed (pause, automation, and interface are at the top of the list), I would not recommend this game. If these things get fixed and the gameplay get's fleshed out a bit I think this could be a good game.
Hook is a pretty short game; almost extremely short. It took about an hour to complete, but at a price of only a dollar; it was well worth it. It is an interesting puzzle game, I recommend it.

There's a lot of things about this game that some may or may not like. I will give an honest review. I can honestly say that I think the "downvotes" that are being given out aren't warranted.
First, this game is still in DEVELOPMENT. There's a lot of things that are still being made. Right now, the game has the PvP gamemode that is open to beta testers. They are currently making Freeplay Mode, a Clan Battle Mode, and The Storm.
Here are some links you can read up on the stuff being made
Factions/Clans -
Freeplay -
The Storm -

On The Storm they've already done a lot of testing (closed) on it and recieved feedback. So the mode is still undergoing development changes and the such in response to the feedback
Now lets start the review.
First, If you're downloading this game expecting a DayZ, H1Z1, or other post apoc survival/roaming game; DONT. At the game's current state, it's a PvP game. The stuff that would make it a post apoc suvival game are still in closed alpha/pre alpha development. So this review will be coming from a PvP game standpoint.
Now, if you're familiar with the game Heroes and Generals (staged battles), the game is similar to the infantry combat pacing (this game is infatry only). It's not as arcadey/fast as CoD, but not as slow/tactical paced as Insurgency or RO. It's taken a nice middle ground between them.
Quick Tutorial
Two types of gear. Physical and Isolation. Both with varying degrees of weight and amounts. Physical protects you against bullets and the such. Isolation protects you against anomalies. Anomalies are just like STALKER. Artifacts are just like STALKER.
Pros
+ Looks. The game looks amazing. Everything from the maps, to the characters and equipment
+ Atmopshere. It feels great. If you've played STALKER before, it's got a very similar atmopshere
+ Factions. Factions have depth and stories behind them. They will also be used in upcoming Story modes.
+ Teamplay. There's many modes where you don't play as a team, you will get screwed over. On some modes you need to have people defending. Other modes you need people to bring back objectives and you need others to escort them. IF your team is treating this like CoD and just running around DM (unless you are playing DM), then you will lost most of the time.
+Map Design. Most of the maps have a interesting and cool design. Both layout and asthetic wise.
+Not pay2win. Most people say its pay2win because premium members get more currency, but there is no gear in the game that is better than what you can purchase in the store. I have so many battles where I've gone up against a fully upgraded soldiers/players and kicked their♥♥♥♥♥with grey/none upgraded gear.
+Anomalies. This adds a whole new depth to some maps. Being in full isolation gear and getting a battery in the middle of an anomaly, or going through an anomaly to flank; it's an amazing feeling.
+Artifacts. Gives you a reason to risk your life in an anomaly. They can often turn the tides of battles if used correctly.
+Character Trees. There's a lot of progression skill trees to choose from. Sadly there's only 2 open to use right now, but there are three undergoing revamps.
Neight
+/- Matchmaking. Reason this is a neither is because its dependent (like all games) on population. If you've got a low population, the MM won't be able to put the perfect match together because it would rather you play, then sit there for ~hours. Now this part of the review (and most of the negative reviews for this game that involve MM) are from a pre steam release. This means most of the players in this game were in EU or the CIS region. Now that steam has been released, I'm hoping for a much larger population which means much btter matchmaking
+/- PvP Only. Reason this is neither is because they're working on the other gameplay modes.
Cons
-Optimzation can be spotty at times, but it's beta so we can't expect it to be perfect.
- Balance is questionable at times. I sometimes have felt some guns were much better than others
- Isolation vs Physical Balance. Right now I'd advise everyone coming into this game is focus on a Physical load out first, then make a secondary Isolation one (if you want it). Reason being is that not all maps have Anomalies placed in regions where it would be tactically beneficial to go through them. One map doesn't even have Anomalies while another is really useless.
-Artifacts vs Items. When you trait for isolation (so you can get artifacts) you sacrifice pockets which can carry items (like medkits). Now you can do a hybrid or change some stuff around to get pockets. However items are much much better than artifacts most of the time. There is one artifact (onyx) which is really good, and another (speed) that CAN (situational) good. The only other artifact you can get is a regen one which is questoinable in terms of its usage. So right now it feels like Physical+items is so much better than Isolation+artifacts in many of the maps.
-Missions. I still feel some missions are a bit too...intrusive. Instead of missions complimenting your games and rewarding you for them, I find they often change the way I play a game. Sometimes this means it could hamper our ability to win.
Overall, I give the game a 7.5/10 with its current state (as a PVP Game). Once freeplay and such are released I expect this to go much higher. There are some obvious issues (that all games have) that deal with balance, but I think that will get better ovetime.
I high suggest that any players who like PvP shooter games (CoD, Heroes and Generals, RO, etc) to give this game a try. It adds some new changes to the genre.

Hook is a fantastic little puzzle game which gives your brain a little workout for around one hour or so, depending on how fast you get the hang of the game.
It starts of easy enough: You push a button and the line that is connected to the button gets hooked in (get it?)
This pretty simple principle is taken to another level by the new mechanics that get added as you progress through the game. Now you have to work with switches that change the direction, with wireless connectors and the evermore interlocking puzzle pieces that you want to take apart to get to the next puzzle.
While doing so you will listen to some peaceful background music that just adds this certain little something to this great puzzle game.
For only 1€ this game is certainly worth every cent if you are a fan of little simple puzzle games since you won't play this game only once.

I've seen so many negative reviews pop up in the past couple of days I felt like I, too, should chime in from a newbie's perspective.
This game is in alpha, and it is not even remotely polished. In fact, it has some scathing problems. Chief among them is the horrible "main menu"/server list. Every time I launch the title or (more likely) crash I'm stuck at "my nemesis." The goddamn thing takes anywhere from 5-10 minutes to load up. Unacceptable indeed. Once I get on a server, it's even less reliable. Sometimes I'm dropped in to a forced spectator mode, sometimes I'm started in the wild, sometimes in a safe zone. Keep in mind I have played on the *same* server each time. It's painful.
I have yet to run in to any of the bugs I've heard so much about aside for some clipping issues. No hackers, either. -Well, save maybe one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who was up a lamp post and ganking noobs as we left the safe zone, but that's not really a hack. That's just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ exploiting a clipping error.
Problems aside, I *still* think the game is great. I love the tense atmosphere it creates, not knowing when and how you might die. I love feeling like I actually DO have to scavenge and watch my♥♥♥♥♥to stay alive. I love the paranoia it creates, and the necessity to build trust in others that stems from it. It *is*, despite its bugs, *exactly* the game I was hoping it would be. I just wish the servers were larger, but oh well. I still have fun in spite of how many times I've been killed all to hell in the last couple of days.
SO, if you choose to play it, I recommend you form your own opinion and ignore the negativity of others. To make sure you don't make the same mistakes we do:
~Travel with friends, if you can.
~Watch your noise level. No, really. Illumination isn't nearly as important in this game's "stealth" as the sound of your movements.
~One ranged weapon, one melee weapon. No more. Keep the rest in your global storage for when you inevitably respawn.
~When in doubt, avoid. This goes for players and Nethers alike, at least outside the safe zone.
Have fun?

Breach & Clear is a tactical strategy game that puts you under the command of a squad of soldiers from various forces from around the world, such as the SAS or Army Rangers. (Note that there is a Frozen Synapse DLC, which adds a squad, a new location and few missions from what i know, but i don't own it so i can't say much about it.)
TL:DR - Skip to Conclusion
REVIEW:
There are 3 modes, a Terrorist Hunt (where you hunt down and kill all enemies in the area), Bomb Defusal (pretty straight forward), and Escape Plan (you're surrounded by enemies and you have get your men out of there and to the marked exit). There are a total of around 6 locations from around the world, and there are 5 missions for each location, for each mode. It works in "phases", or turns, where you can plan your squad's actions, from where they move and face, to throwing a flashbang in a room while the rest of the team storms in. Early in the game in the first three or so locations, the game is relatively easy, and having two men with suppressors enter a room first to not alert everyone, then bring in the other two when the sh-t hits the fan. There is, on occasion, situations in the Escape Plan mode where a soldier or two will be put in situations surrounded by 3+ enemies making it impossible to escape with them, it's fixable by exiting to the menu, and restarting the mission, but it can be a hassle sometimes. Missions tend to get repetitive.
At the time of writing this, I have only reached the fourth location and it's become tougher than the first three, so it can provide a decent challenge, at least on higher difficulties, as i only play on normal. The game includes different roles for your squad members (The names of each role escapes me, i apologise) which can help in different situations, and  you can level them up using XP from completed missions, and you can give them bonus stats to the Accuracy, or the amount of Health they have. Oh, and there's a perma-death option which grants bonus XP. The game also offers customisation, allowing you to change your squad's clothing, camo, armour, and weapons. You can do this with the in-game money you earn from completing missions. The weapons all have available attachments which you can customise to give bonuses, like Accuracy +9001, for example. Despite this, there's a balance, where body armour which gives Health +35 will be balanced by making your movement speed go down. When breaching into rooms you have options for different entry points and different methods of breaching; Kicking the door, shotgun, breaching charge, and lock pick. Each offers an advantage and disadvantage, but i'd recommend just kicking the door open instead.
The graphics, animation, and game design are pretty well done for what it is, considering it was also originally made for iOS, with Android somewhere down the line. The game offers two viewing angles while planning, a Top-down view, and an Isometric view, personally i like the top-down view better when planning because its easier to see where you moving your men. After you've finished planning and started the phase, you can view an over-the-shoulder cam of either of your soldiers, which is pretty neat, although sometimes when behind cover you wont see anything. It's there that you'll also notice how the graphics aren't as great as the would be when you're planning in t-d or iso view. There are some neat effects, and slow motion queues, which i can't say look amazing but it's tolerable. Additionally, the animations arent too great, especially when breaching and using a lock pick, as the soldier will be picking at the air or the middle of the door, as well as having their gun floating in front of them whilst doing so.
CONCLUSION:
Gameplay:
+Multiple game modes
+Different locations
+Stealthable missions (for some)
+/- Mission difficulty
-Escape Plan mode
-Repetitive missions
Visuals:
+Decent textures
+Effects
+Different camera angles
-Animations
Overall it's a good game, with decent visuals, good gameplay, more than one game mode, etc. Coming from a more casual standpoint, for a tactical, strategy based game, it's definitely worth a buy, and if you can get it on sale even better. If you're a more "hardcore strategist" or prefer more robust strategy games, then it may not be worth it to you.

Normally I wouldn't try any game that has PvP aspects and premises, but I thought I would give this a shot as I do enjoy open-world games and first-person shooters. I did not spend much time in the game (about half an hour or so), and I understand that this game is still in Alpha stage. Please take my opinion with a grain of salt.
That being said, my time with Nether was less-than enjoyable. I don't have a top-of-the-line PC, but my PC can handle most games well-enough on high settings and perfectly on medium. Even on the lowest graphical setting the game was still jerking around with a horribly-low framerate. Playing this game actually made my head hurt slightly, and combat was a major pain. Fortunately I joined a server where all of the people I encountered were also in the same area and we worked together to kill most things that came our way, unlike the bullet to the head from afar that I was expecting with games like these. Perhaps I just got lucky, but I still ended up dying since I couldn't find a way to heal myself or get any armor/weapons.
And when you die, that character is gone: permadeath. That didn't bother me since I hardly achieved any success besides reaching Lv. 2. What DID annoy me was that I was given the tutorial objective to turn in a package...and I couldn't do it. I reached the designated area, did what the on-screen prompt told me to do, and jack-all happened, save for me getting swamped by more enemies. From what I could tell the "safe-zone" wasn't safe or it had been compromised, so that was super-swell to know that I had hopped in at the most inopportune time to where I COULDN'T complete the tutorial objective because of some instance. So yeah, I practically died at the tutorial stage. That is frustrating.
And maybe I just suck at the video games! I don't want to think I do, but that could always be the case. From what was happening, however, it seemed that I was just set up for failure right from the beginning. Didn't help that I couldn't open ANY of the in-game store menues to craft any items or trade junk, even though I had acquired junk from monsters that didn't start dropping until I was Lv. 2 oddly enough.
So, my review in short: Not worth it right now. Maybe somewhere down the line with more tweaks and more polishing this could be cool. I'd like some PvE servers so people like me can choose whether or not they want to deal with the extra threat of human players, but let's focus on the mechanical problems of the game first.

Customer support finally came through. They solved my problem easily,. It took awhile,. but better late than never. For anyone having the input not supported issue, here's the solution:
1) Open the start menu, in the search bar type "regedit" and hit enter.
2) In the registry editor go to: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Mighty Rabbit
Studios\Breach & Clear
3) Modify the following values (*make sure to switch from Hexadecimal to
Decimal*):
- Set *fullscreen* to 0
- Set *Screenmanager Resolution Height* to 768
- Set *Screenmanager Resolution Width *to 1024
- Set *Screenmanager Is Fullscreen mode* to 0
This will allow you to set the game to run as a small window - you can then
change the settings in-game to whatever you prefer.

Thanks,
Breach & Clear

I don't really these 'reviews' that much, but I really felt like doing an exception for this masterpiece.
To start with I have to mention the graphics of this game. Even though it's only a 2D platform game the graphics themselves are absolutely perfect. Done in a style of ancient greek paintings and mozaiques it unbelieveably matches the whole atmosphere of the game and is a pleasure to watch. Also each and every place you visit has a different atmosphere, from welcoming Agora of the Olympus, to hostile swamps under Artemis' realm, it really spices the game up and makes you feel you are still about to discover more and more unique locations, it never makes you bored.
Another jewel of this game is the outstanding soundtrack composed by greek composer Marios Aristopoulos <3 . For each part of the Olympus (at which you operate in this game), or other destinations there is a different theme music which fits the nature of the place perfectly. When playing in the Hades' realm of the Underworld I was actually pretty scared solely because of the song playing in there.
The story itself is very interesting as well and I really liked the differences between each of the numerous bosses appearing throughout the game as well as the unique ways of defeating them, every single one of them had a different approach and developers of this game really took everything they could and used every opportunity the 2D platform RPG game offered.
For me as a lover of greek mythology this game earned it's place in my heart and I would really like to thank the developers for creating this game (not game a masterpiece within games!) and it pleases me that even in these times, some people are still passionate enough to make a game about the awesome greek mythology!
I highly recommend Apotheon to everyone, this piece of art will just suck you in and won't let you out until you finish it and maybe not even then.
That's it, thanks to the ones reading it this far and I hope that one day the 'gods in making games' at Alientrap will bring us something even more awesome than this, even though trumphing Apotheon will be an extremely hard task. :))

When I first wrote a review for this game, it was while it first released, and I mostly talked about it it's inexcusably shoddy launch. I know that a lot of games have poor launches, but that's not an excuse. Just because some other companies can't get it right, doesn't mean that others are exempt. A few problems are fine, but being unable to play the game for several days? Major bugs and glitches and crashes? There's no excuse for it. But now that the game is, for the most part, playable, I will write an actual review of it.
To begin, let's talk about it and Dead by Daylight and get that comparison out of the way, as it is something a lot of people want to know. First, this game does it's killer far more justice than Dead by Daylight, where playing Killer is a nightmare sometimes.  I still find playing Jason to be tedious, however, as Counselors can evade Jason sometimes by just running around a building and leaping in and out of windows. Characters with higher stamina and speed with med spray can do this for even longer durations. Even with the shift, it can still be tricky to catch them. Still, it's easier to find your victims and catch them off-guard, which helps with chasing.
There are more things to do, more ways to escape, which makes it less repetitive than Dead by Daylight's generators and gates. And, you are able to fight back and you're not just limited to running away. Finally, all of the Counselors have their own strengths and weaknesses, and it actually matters who you chose. It's not like Dead by Daylight where literally all Survivors can eventually do everything that all the others can do.
But that's where the praise ends.
My biggest gripe with this game is that it is way too easy for a Counselor to accomplish nothing. For me, a lot of games go like this:
Spawn as Deborah. Go into Cabin to look for stuff. Find nothing useful. Go to next cabin. Find medspray and a bat. No parts. Go to next cabin. Cabin has already been searched by other Counselors. Jason shows up. Jason shifts on top of me. Die.
This happens to me almost every other round. Either Jason just happens to find me or someone getting chased brings him to me, only for them to die and then Jason come after me next. You spend five minutes trying to do something useful to your team. Even if I die after putting something in the car, the boat, or the phone, at least I did something. I know this isn't technically the game's fault, it could just be poor luck on my part, but still, the fact that this game makes it that easy for you to accomplish literally nothing is a little off putting.
Jason's ability to shift and then grab and auto kill you plays into this. To be clear, I really have no problem with Jason's ability to grab and then execute, even after shifting. The problem is, the ability to do this directly negates the Counselor's combat and the ability to execute on command makes attempting to break free virtually pointless. This makes the stats Compsure, Luck, and Strength worthless, as fighting Jason is suicidal as his grabs can interrupt your attacks and sometimes, due to poor detection, your hits won't even register. This makes it so the best way to survive is to avoid Jason entirely, so Stealth is a priority, which is why most people play Eric, AJ, Tiffany, and Deborah.
Another issue is that Jason can trap all objectives of the Counselors, placing his bear traps at the door of the cars, in front of the phone box, on the dock of the boat, and that basically covers all four escape routes. Traps can be disarmed via a pocketknife, but those can be hard to come across. Plus, no one wants to sacrifice one to disarm a trap, as the pocketknife is the only way to reliably escape Jason's grasp. This basically forces Counselors to deliberately walk on Jason's traps to get rid of them. This alerts Jason and he then goes right over and murders the person and everyone nearby. This wouldn't be so much of a problem if Jason's grab wasn't so easy to pull off and Composure was such a pointless stat.
Bugs and glitches are rampant in the game. The hair of character models glitch out sometimes. Jason can be sent to orbit after hitting him while he grabs someone from the car. Achievements don't work. I one time got stuck under a bed after Jason killed someone in the bed next to me. Jason can be rendered powerless if people quit while he is killing them. The car one time randomly stood upright on it's back somehow after just going in reverse, making it inacessible. Hits against Jason don't register. Some perks don't work properly.
There is no option to play as Jason and Jason only. This is not so much a problem for myself, as I really don't care who I play as (and I usually prefer the Counselors anyway). But it is when you consider that 98% of the people who bought this game are major fans of the series who probably bought for the sole reason of getting to be Jason Voorhees and murdering everyone they see as their favorite horror film slasher. When they don't get Jason, they quit the match, leaving five or four players against Jason, which is almost impossible (if not entirely) to win against. So, if you are thinking of buying this game and playing a lot of rounds as Jason, you might want to reconsider, as you will play Jason typically 10% of the time, while playing as Counselor the other 90%. This can be bad for some players as it can be extremely difficult to get your strategy down as Jason when you don't get to play as him very often. Each time I finally get to play as him, I have to remember how to play as him as I'm usually surprised I even got him. I've heard some people going thirty plus games without ever being Jason.
The last complaint is the price. Currently, the game has one mode with three maps. That's it. There is no Single Player mode yet, which is odd considering the game was delayed so that it would be included. Dead By Daylight is half the price of this game. Now I know what you're thinking, "But in order to get everything, you have to buy DLC! And that makes it way more expensive!" True, but even if you don't buy any DLC, you still get more. You can still play all the maps, you can get offerings to play the DLC Killers once in awhile, and you can still get their perks via the Shrine of Secrets. In the private Kill Your Friends mode, there is an option to enable access to DLC Killers as well. Even if you buy no DLC, you still get more than what you get in Friday the 13th as of this moment. I know that more content for Friday the 13th will surely come, but it's hard to justify a price, when most of it is for features that won't come until well after release.
To be sure, this game is not bad, but it is definitely one you need friends for. You need coordination to do well in this game, and, even with voice chat enabled, I find a lot of lobbies with people who either don't talk or don't speak English, which severely handicaps the Survivors when you don't know what their doing or what items they have. It is very easy for your fellow Survivors to die with important items on them and then you have no idea where that item is, effectively cutting off a route of escape. Dead by Daylight's generators may be repetitve, but at least they can't be misplaced by hapless teammates.
This game has a lot of potential, and it is fun when it works properly. But it has a lot of problems and a lot of times you will die without getting to do anything and then you're stuck spectating everyone else just so you can get more points so you can get more CP so you can get more stuff for your Counselors and Jason. It's not a good sign when more than half of your play time can potentially be sitting and watching other people play. At least in Dead by Daylight you can just leave without missing out on more XP (or Bloodpoints, as they're called in that game).
Overall, it's not worth the price, it's buggy, it's easy to accomplish nothing, and if you're looking to play as Jason a lot, you won't.

Side scroller action/adventure set in the world of anceint urn decorations.  Huge credit for the unique art style.  The gameplay is unusual, too, in that it's more than run, jump, strik, and parry.  There are various types of strikes to try to get around how an opponent is holding their shield.  It's a welcome addition of depth not present in so many competing titles (where seems most sidescrollers are made in tribute to the 8 and 16 bit eras).  Apotheon kind of does its own thing and I applaud that.  The music is good, the voice acting sounds professional, the graphics really add to the immersion, and the story is well executed and fun to watch unfold.  That said, the difficulty is a little uneven (usually trending toward too easy by rewarding button mashing with strong weapons), the story is a bit straightforward (Gods of Olympus are destroying the mortal world and the player must asend to their plane to prevent it) and there are a few specific glitches that could stall progression at certain points.  All in all, though, it's an unusual and enjoyable game, one I'll likely remember for years, and one I'd certainly recommend.

This review concerns the whole series of Back to the Future.
TL,DR; I had a blast with the series and recommend it, more easily so if you liked the movies.
+ Telltale game engine
+ Back to the Future theme
+ Voice actor A.J. Locascio very closely resembles Fox's voice from the movies
+ Overall good voice acting
+ Believable characters
+ Hours of nostalgia
0 Puzzles of medium challenge
- (the old) Too short, about 2 hours for each of the 5 episodes
First off, the game uses the
tool known from adventures like the three new Sam & Max serieses, The Walking Dead, the current Tales from the Borderlands and a number of lesser known games, e.g. Puzzle Agent.
Except for maybe the awful Bone series the tool generally provides easily navigable good-looking scenery. It manages too closely resemble the respective flair and art style of the basic IPs.
Same with this adventure, I was seamlessly brought back to the 1985 setting, then gleefully thrown about. The voice acting did it's part with A.J. Locascio closely imitating Micheal J. Fox's pitch and tremble from the movies.
Characters are believably written and we get to learn more about the McFlys, Browns and Tannens.
The puzzles are not too hard and most of the time logical and with clear intent. This though adds to the episodes being somewhat short. I think I spent around 2 hours per episode making the series roughly a 10 hour experience - an experience of awesome.
Thank you, Telltale, for once more providing a high-class adventure and letting me dive back into the atmosphere of Back to the Future including feelings of hope for and fear of the technology of the future.
Also, the future is now! 2015 is only days away. I hear self-tightening shoes have been done and the hoverboard works if only just. Now, where is the self-drying jacket and the convincing shark hologram?
Five episodes of Back to the Future adventure and reminiscence. Recommended.

Alright, this will upset some fan boys. Do not freak out, please. To be honest, I wanted to like this game, loving Supergiant for Bastion and a bit for Transistor, but Pyre does not work for me.
It is a bad competitive game, if you are into competitive games. If you are mainly into RPG’s, or similar, you may find it interesting or challenging, I think. For a competitive game it just feels cheap and weak like so many similar games. In short: an RPG developer tries a competitive game and fails, with weak UI and weird decisions. It happened before. It is actually more of a 3-v-3 Rocket League (with an orb), as others wrote, but with a weird design choice that you can only control one character at the time, while having 3 on the board. So to speak.
To me, who is playing all kind of competitive games, it looks as if competitive gameplay is not their thing. It's boring, frankly speaking, and does not feel balanced and well tested. After having seen the game at conferences, I wondered already if the final game will work. My impression at the confs was that the audiences didn’t get it or were bored. I did hope that they would polish it, or change a few things, so people that are coming straight from Bastion and Transistor do no get too disappointed. I hope it sells okay at least, so it was worth the try (for which kudos to Supergiant).
There is a story, but it does not work like in the past games. It feels on top of some competitive gameplay, which happens sometimes in this genre, which they should have avoided, in order to be perhaps more innovative, I think.
Pro
- art style is nice, not overall, but often enough
- sound and music is great, as always
Contra
- combat animations are weak and weird sometimes
- weak UI for this game type, like more for RPG than competitive players (complicated)
- too many unnecessary text boxes, too many “click to proceed” moments
- overall, it is probably a cheap hero competitive game
- if you ask me: nothing special, from a competitive gameplay perspective
- also linear and a bit inconsequential story gameplay
- felt like a Rocket League clone sometimes, but this could be the orb/goal thing ;)
There are plenty of better competitive games out there. Wait for sales, if you need it.

Pretty great idea, and breath-taking models. They do appear to be straying away from the modern bird-like models however, and they are now starting to look more like they do in Jurassic Park (Although that isn't exactly a bad thing). Game seems to run fine for me, and its a fun experience. Although the game does currently have MANY major flaws.
1: Servers
Massive Multiplayer games like these need good servers, and when you seem to crash out of you're game every 30-40 minutes it just ruins the fun you and your friends are having. Not to mention that many of ther servers are flat out dead, and with only about 30 to choose from, you will more often then not find yourself in one with only 10 people because the main servers are full with around 50-70 players capped.
2: Map
The map FEELS small. I have yet to find how small it really is, but I always spawn next to the wall (Which is just a drop off into nothing). This coupled with the very dense hills you traverse through, make it so you can never see any mountains in front of you, so the map just appears to end almost everywhere. This makes the game feel VERY small. Although the Misty Vally map is a perfect polar opposite of this, with plateaus and deep valleys, filled with fog and well mist, make the map feel open and spacious. I hope to see later maps go follow this example, or better yet, just try to make the current maps feel more open.
3: Chat
When you choose a dinosaur, your chat box is now exclusive to that type of dinosaur, and you can't see the other chat. This is bad in its own ways, but mainly it makes the game feel very empty. I can see where they are coming from with this, making it so you and other species can't communicate with one another and give away position. I think that instead of locking my species, they could lock it by Carnivore and Herbivore. This way, the game is still keeping the the division between species well enough that herds can't be exposed by others in the group, and the chat can be more easily used between these groups.
Thats about all I can think of off the top of my head, I didn't talk about anything like the camera, or ping issues (Beside Servers) because those will al be fixed in due time. I would just hope to see more "design" being placed into gameplay and immersion instead of pumping out new dinosaurs every other week.
Have these be fixed, and the final product be as smooth as I hope it becomes I would give it a 7 or 8/10. I just ♥♥♥♥ing love dinosaurs.
Although as the game is currently I would give it a 5/10.

Incredible story about some profound topics.
If you're afraid this might be too scary, you have 3 options: 1. Use the Wuss MOD to deactivate common enemies, so you will only have to outrun 3 scripted "runner" enemies (and those sequences become very easy), or 2. Watch a playthrough on YouTube to sort of "memorize" how to get around the monsters, or 3. Read the guide on the monsters, as each type of monsters has specific exploitable weaknesses (like "cannot hear" or "cannot see"), with which you should be able to outsmart them.
Graphics are top notch, environments are beautifully designed, story is captivating and convincingly delivered.
There's also quite a lot of optional content in the form of diaries, journals, recordings etc., just like in e.g. Bioshock games, which adds to the depth of the story.
Note: even with active monsters, this is probably going to take between 6 and 9 hours of play time. I bought it at 40% off and feel like it was definitely worth it.

I studied Latin and Greek hexameter poetry at university so I normally hate games set in ancient Greek mythology, but I liked this - they clearly give a damn about making it authentic and have bothered to look up some black figure pot art!
Their grasp of ancient Greek theology is a bit squiffy in places: a definite tendency to turn the gods that we find sympathetic nowadays into goodies, and the inscrutable, all-powerful type ones into baddies. The controls are really really floaty which put me off playing on hard. Easy was loads of fun though. The level design is absolutely world-class and they always used the engine in creative ways, whether it was racing in a hunt against Artemis in stag form or frantically trying to chuck invading dead people off Charon's barge. The music and voice acting are excellent throughout. Lots of pertinent quotes from Homer scattered about and every NPC is a name-drop... I just wish they could have been a bit more restrained with the overall plot, which is sadly pretty similar to God of War. The fact Zeus doesn't clobber humanity in a fit of divine grumpiness is sort of the point of him.

This is the first game in the DOOM series. The reason it is called "the ultimate doom" is because alle the episodes are included. Doom consists of four episodes, three episodes that makes up the main storyline, pluss an extra fourth episode.
The Doom series is a must have for a PC-gamer born in or before the 90's. This is buy far one of the best first person shooters out there, and is therfore highly recomended. For me, and probably for a lot of other people, this game is packed with action and nostalgia.
If you are running windows 7/8 you will need to run this game in compability mode for windows "XP (service pack 3)". To do this, go to: Steam>SteamApps>common>Ultimate Doom>base. In this folder you should see the dosbox.exe. Rightclikk it and go to properties. Clikk compability in the top tab. Check "Run this program in compability mode for" And choose: Windows XP (service pack 3) in the dropdown menu.
For further inprovement you can change the configurationfiles for Dosbox and Doom. The configurationfiels are called: dosbox.conf, ultimate.conf and ultimatem.conf. Open the files with notepad to make your changes. If you are changing annything in this files make sure you set the same values in all three files. If you screew up with theese files, just uninstall and reinstall the game and they should be back to their default setting. In the dosbox.conf file all the different values are explained.

Apotheon is a 2d sidescrolling platformer taking place in Greek mythology. You play the role of Nikandros, a human whose civilization was forsaken by the gods. Seeing your city in ruins, you make an alliance with an opportunistic Hera, who guides you through your quest of assassination and dethroning.
The graphics for this game are themed entirely around ancient Greek paintings such as those found on pottery or tapestries and it has a really neat look as a result. The soundtrack is also set along the same theme and various obelisks detailing actual Greek scripture can be found in each level. The weaponry mirrors that which one would find in ancient Greece and just about any other obvious reference you could make is accounted for.
If I had to pick one beef in this game, it would have to be the controls. The control scheme in this game is very similar to terraria in that you have to both face your character towards enemies or items as well as “aim” him. Combat can be kind of tricky at first and combined with knockback effects, downright awkward. I found myself struggling just to land hits against an AI that instantaneously switches to the exact counter to my current weapon. Thankfully the game has potions and other items which can be used to easily resolve combat, although with the added detriment of a cheapened accomplishment when one uses a potion of invulnerability to cheese a boss battle. Additionally the quests can be both tiresome and predictable (come to an area, 3 sub-quests, rinse and repeat).
In the end I didn’t think that Apotheon was a great game, but it wasn’t a terrible game either. If you can grab it for under $10 you’ll probably get your money’s worth on this one.
