It's amusing why I'm writting this, since it's DOOM for ♥♥♥♥ sake, but I'll get to it. Anyway for those that have experienced this game all those years ago and haven't touched it since, I advise to pick it up, play, to relieve the nostalgia, then hop onto the mod scene for a kick in the nuts surprise. Anyway, it is one of the first FPS games that started the genre and got me interested in it. (Though to be fair Duke Nukem 3D was the real spark for me for shooters, and Quake was what got me into competitive MP portion of the genre).
The vanilla experience is extremely dated, no proper aiming, clunky controls by today's standard, heavy reliance on auto aim and naturaly the primitive graphics. Even with all that I played the vanilla recently (though I ended up modding it via zdoom for better control scheme) and still was fun as ever. Secrets were ♥♥♥♥ well hidden (for those that I couldn't remember), shooting still felt great. Amusing how a primitive shooter like Doom can have such great shooting feeling. Enemies will flinch depending on guns, rockets will gib and blast stuff apart and BFG will clear rooms. The level design was fantastic, mazelike key hunting formula that made a lot of old games great, and put a large majority of modern games to shame when it comes to inteligent level design. While I had an absolute blast with Doom, and not just due to nostalgia, I encountered the large amount of fantastic mods.
At first I take this with a grain of salt. Mods for games are peculiar, usually extremely specific, niche or such. Here or there there will be some that truly stand out. In Doom's case, good God are there a lot of great mods. I'm not going to rattle them off but I will mention one particular mod that enhances the experience to modern standars, and puts to shame almost every known FPS developer today. I'm talking about Brutal Doom mod. If you liked doom, any iteration of it, go look this up. It takes the entire old game/s and tuns it to 11 with gore, weapons, effects, sound and feeling. To me this mod made Doom game so much more in standard with current games. Doom already was a pinacle, had nothing to prove since it stood among the first and best, but with mods like this it really makes me ask: what the ♥♥♥♥ are current FPS devs doing.
The original game is timleess, and while I admit there is some nostalgia there, there are still a lot of technical aspects (gameplay wise) that hold strong even 20 years after. With mods (like Brutal Doom), all bets are off, this is balls to the walls amazing value in a game that offers everything a shooter should have. Shooting is fun, satisfying, strategic, skill based, and no matter how much they throw at you you will want more to paint the walls with (that is quite literal in Brutal Doom's case).
If you feel that game requires fancy graphics to be good, you are in the wrong game genre. This game right here does everything justice in terms of shooting, level exploration, wit, and just not giving a ♥♥♥♥. Go to hell, and make them sorry they ever heard of you.

I bought this game because I like X-COM a lot and thought this might have been a good alternative before a new "real" PC TBS game came out and for once there were more than US units and British SAS, including one of my personal favorite : the German Kommando Spezialkräfte or KSK for short.
So I "created" my unit, I use the word very loosely as there are not a lot of physical customization available for your soldiers, still better than what BF4 of COD do though, I entered the game and blazed through 3 environment, about 15 missions, with barely a scratch on my men, starting to think "Ok this is starting to stink badly...", only to finally start getting some pretty serious opposition in the next environments to the point where I finally had to start thinking how not to get my me killed... even though calling the enemies "mentally challenged" would make the COD AIs look like rocket scientists.
So the game does offer a fair deal of challenge in later stages.
But what about "The Gear" ? Yes with upper cases because that's what gives an 8 year old playing COD wetdreams. One word defines my whole experience on that : "disappointment". To explain it better the customizations options for clothing and apparel is giving a decent choice but : the plate carriers and chest rigs all look the same and the arsenal  comes straight from your average US armory. Why is it a problem ? Well, because the armory is an AR-15 based orgy (seriously, you got more than 20 variation on the M4/M16) and a couple things more "original" live a 1st version TAR-21 and SCARs seen thousands of time before... where are the real guns like, I don't know, Aks, HK416/417, FAMAS, G3 or even the base gun all KSK use : the G36K (and I found that many people think only the C exist)... I have more variaty in my own armory.
Also : where the hell are the side arms ?
Also one might think given the realistish approach the gun stats may have reflected their actual use in real life, but in fact is a linear progression where the next gun is better only by virtue of being unlocked later.

This is not acceptable at all for a 15$ game !
In the end I had some hopes for this game but fact is this game does not just fail to deliver, it is simply a money grabbing operation on TBS amateurs such as myself and all the Kikoolols thinking they could become SAS by snapping their fingers (thanks Modern Warfare...).
To sum it up : you want a real TBS game, just type X-COM in the search bar and save yourself.

Honestly one of the best side-scrollers I've gotten the chance to play. The art style caught my eye immediately, reminding me of the Muses' scenes from Disney's Hercules. About a third of the way into the game, the realization that there are hidden shopkeepers, side-quests for items and buffs, and hidden chests scattered all over the game added some depth and diversion from an otherwise straight-forward, linear experience.
As a fan of the God of War series, it's interesting to see a similar story implemented in a very different style of art and gameplay. Side-quests involving Dionysus, Aphrodite and Hephaestus were a welcome addition. The magic weapons you find along the way are great, a favorite being a discus that works much like a boomarang. After receiving items from each God and Goddess, you snowball into a powerhouse, which makes the rest of the game a breeze, but ends up making enemies more annoying than challenging.
Like any game, there's room for improvement, particularly with items getting stuck into corners and left unreachable to the player, but this was a nice way to spend a weekend. Nicely done Alientrap!

If this game was in open alpha, I would surely have given it thumbs up. It features a plausible game mechanics, dated but nice  graphics; the missions are fast-paced and action-loaded. However, as with many games that try to avoid micro-management, the developers seemed to forget at times that the game is intended to be played by a human being. There is a ton of interface constraints which I cannot help but call stupid, like being able to throw grenades only at the beginning of the turn, excluding any movement for that soldier, or being unable to command soldiers to wait for a specific number of seconds to ensure simultaneous action. Another issue is balance. To name just one example, the UAV is like a legit cheat which shows all position and movements of all enemies throughout the mission, even inside buildings, which renders the recon class absolutely pointless.
But the most glaring disadvantage is the lack of tactical possibilities. I mean, in a tactical strategy, where are the smoke grenades? Where are those nifty hi-tech gadgets like motion scanners? They would be a lot more fun to use than the aforementioned UAV. The scarcity of the tools offered to the player quickly makes the missions monotonous - Breach & Clear, Rinse & Repeat - making the game suitable to kill off half an hour from time to time, but not more.
These are all correctable flaws, and it's a pity that the developers released Breach & Clear too quickly, without testing not only stability but also playability. The should have invested more effort into their product.

One entire year and a bit later Update.
This game has come a LONG way. When I first bought it, the maps were bland, the game was buggy to hell, the dinosaurs did not look good at all, everything about it was bland, boring and looking back, a waste of money. However, after the year's progress and the 1000 hours of experience I've had I can make a thorough review.
-Mechanics-
While still in the works, the game has built some brilliant mechanics.
-Nesting is good to have, with new baby models of each dinosaur possibley on the way I look forward to how much further the nesting can go.
-Bleed, bone break and weight classification brough into play has a major change in the game, this made combat so much more than face-tanking. With certain dinosaurs built for crushing, bleeding or simply small game hunting, it makes things so much more realistic, atleast on the select few Realism servers available by the community.
-Scent, currently a work in progress is going to make things so much more difficult and scary, small dinosaurs will need to rely on being quiet, sneaky and able to stay out of sight and scent. This will be a huge game changer.
-The Dinosaur models and maps-
-Dinosaur models have been getting a much needed overhaul, the new and bneautiful Triceratops, Diabloceratops, Dryosaurus, Maiasaura and Allosaurus models are absaloutely magnificent. This shows a massive drive in the developers for improvment.
-The maps, shaders and vegitation has improved drastically, with a new redwoods map, which I am looking forward to the results of, and improvments to the current maps seemingly underway.
-New dinosaur skins and textures give off beautiful and realistic feels. Along with the new blinking on the dinosaur eyes and new calls.
-Theres a new interface or GUI, with sound effects that usually scare me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥...
-Game modes and workshop-
-With sandbox and Survival now ingame together, it is amazing to see how many people enjoy both. However personally I think survival on a realism server is much much better.
-The race to apex has gotten harder with the new layout made for it, having to go through many different animals.
-Depending on the server depends on how hard or easy it is, server owners can edit the points required for everything, this can break or make a server in my own opinion.
-With the new workshop the community has created mods that fix certain things wrong with dinosaurs to make them more realistic, make new maps, import or mess with the dinosaurs, you name it they're probably going to do it.
-My own personal thank you-
If I had not bought this game I'd have never met the people I have by my side today, people say the community is bad, but in my opinion, i've never been happier. Like-minded people almost. So I thank the developers for making the game. It led me to making the friends I have today.

Graphic wise it is very good, the mechanics are I feel mostly solid and the gameplay is challenging enough for someone like me who greatly enjoys the adrenaline thrill of the game. That one well placed hit or block that lands the win can have overwhelming adrenaline.
I beat the single player campaign, which is a decent story, in about 8 hours in normal mode. Making it more frustrating when you get to the end, and have to run through 30 minutes of super easy content to get back where you were. Of course the meat of this game is the Multiplayer, and it is on those merits that I can not recommend the game in it's current state.
The peer to peer networking this game uses is garbage. You will often get messages when queing that you can't join a session because it is full, I have an incredibly fast internet speed and great pc and sometimes the load times can be quite long if the "host" is lacking. Quite often players leave matches, and whenever that happens the game tends to rewind a few seconds.... sometimes negating good kills... or leading to kills that shouldn't have happened...
My BIGGEST issue with the game is that this is supposed to be a pretty dedicated multiplayer game...
while, if you are in a party and then get the dreaded "There are no longer enough players in the session." You get kicked back to the main menu and have to reform the entire party. This is more annoying then anything else. I also don't understand when the game is going to replace players with bots or determine there are not enough players and kick everyone back to the main menu... why not.... have all those people who can't get into games because they are "Full" join the match eh?
If you are patient enough to deal with the networking issues this is a great game but one I can't recommend until those issues are addressed.
One thing I would like to see added someday is a tournament mode which makes sense in a game like this.

This game is as scary as people say it is THIS GAME IS AMAZING now I will list my pros and cons
Pros
-The graphics are great for the time this game came out and the graphics are still good to this day
-The atmosphere HOLY CRAP is PHENOMENAL it's probably the best thing about this game and makes it the horror game it is
-The monsters are decent looking but still are horrifying and it scares me to deal with them and the fact that looking at them drains Daniels very VERY fragile sanity doesn't help make them less scary
-The music is great and really helps with the games atmosphere making it scary as all hell
-The mechanics really help build tension and show off this game's "Survival Horror" aspect especially the Lantern Oil and Sanity mechanics those are really good and as I said really help show the "Survival Horror" aspect of the game
-The enviornments are really well done yes the whole castle astetic does get a bit dull after a while but that still doesn't mean the enviornments aren't really well done
Cons
-The sanity mechanic can be very annoying at times especially in a very dark place like the prison and especially if you have no Lantern Oil
-The Terror Meter as people call it is a sound that plays when an enemy spots you and gives chase the sound is a loud siren like sound that while adding to the tension is ear pierceing especially if you are wearing headphones
Verdict
-Great Graphics and Ok Animations
-Terrifying Atmosphere and Decently scary monsters
-Great setting that after awhile feels a bit dull
-Great and tense mechanics that add to the "Survival Horror" aspect
-Sanity can be a tad annoying at times and so can "The Terror Meter"
**Score 9.4/10**

This is my first review on Steam. I feel obliged to write one because this really is a great game that deserves support from the community.
If you're like me, then this is the game you've been waiting for. It's a family-sized vault survival game, similar to FTL in micromanagement and Fallout Shelter iOS app in gameplay. You go out and search for supplies, encountering friendly and dangerous NPCs along the way, all to scavenge stuff to help your family back at the fallout shelter survive. when you have encounters outside the vault, the setting changes to that encounter, which may result in combat, or not, depending on you. I think this is really cool.
You expand the shelter as you go, building and upgrading new useful things, whilst mainly worrying about food and water. Expansion of the shelter is one of the coolest features, as you get to decide in what order your family's survival priorites are.
This game is not for babyshit survivalists. This will adequately simulate the hopelessness, desperation, and satisfaction of fallout shelter life. You will get radiation poisoning. You will get food poisoning. You will experience dehydration, starvation, desperation, and elation as you find that little bit of food or water or whatever that will keep your family going for a few more days.
A few features of the game do need a little tweaking at the moment, but that's fine because THE DEVS ARE LISTENING! I know this for a fact because I've personally seen it. The alpha has been released for the best possible reason - to improve an already great game.
Overall, for 15 bucks, this is a great buy. Even in early access, the game is very playable, with no gamebreaking bugs of any kind that I've found. If you enjoy basically anything post-apocalyptic, the novel The Road, or, specifically, the Fallout Shelter iOS app, this game is for you.

This is the first game I've played in as long as I can remember where I kept playing after I finished the main story just to collect all the items, do all the sidequests, and explore the world. Having the entire game look like the artwork on an ancient greek urn was an inspired decision and it really payed off. Just walking through the different areas and looking at all the statues and characters and enviroments is a lot of fun, and that's a big part of what made me want to keep playing.
The combat takes some getting used to but can also be a lot of fun. I think a big part of what makes it difficult at first is that a lot of weapons have a long wind up time before the strike, whereas in most platformers the strike happens almost instantenously. I can see why some people don't like this but to me it made it feel like the attacks have real force behind them which makes landing a blow a lot more satisfying. The other unusual part of combat is that you aim your attacks with the mouse. This probably adds more depth for players who want to really dig into the system and develop their skills, but to me it often felt overcomplicated. However, if you play with a controller your attacks will automatically go in the direction your charcter is facing, so that was a good solution for me. You can still aim your attacks with the right stick if you need to.
The story is interesting if you are interested in Ancient Greek literature and mythology. They did a good job portraying all the gods and had some interesting takes on their characters. A touch I really liked is the signposts around the game with quotes from Homer and other Greek authors about the parts of Greek mythology you're currently playing through. One problem I have with the story (and this is a pet peeve of mine that happens in a lot of stories like this) is that the characters all speak in that weird, formal, pseudo-Shakespearian register. It doesn't make sense to do this just because this is set in an old time period. These characters are not English people from 400 years ago, they're based on Greek people from 2,000 years ago. It would have been cool if the writing was more like Stanley Lombardo's translation of Homer, which uses mostly modern language but still sounds appropriately epic.
Despite a few drawbacks though, I highly recommend this game. Its a fun and engaging platformer with a good story and a unique and beautiful artstyle.

DOOM is a great game, and it's an awesome experience for any FPS player. It's not one of those games that has you going straight from point A to point B. You have to explore the maps to find keys that you to proceed to the next map. There is a wide mariety of maps, this version of DOOM has a total of 36 maps if you also count the secret maps. Some maps can be a maze, however, and it can ruin the pace of the game. The game also has a lot of secrets and even a few secret levels. DOOM also has a good variety of enemies, some can be annoying though, such as the Lost Souls, the pinky Demons with partial invisibility, and the Cacodemons. The bosses are probably the most badass bosses in gaming, a giant robot demon with a rocket launcher for a hand, and a robot spider demon with a chaingun. I won't count the bruiser brothers, because they're just two Barons of Hell. The game also offers some kick♥♥♥♥♥music, which adds good pace to the game, although some songs can be a bit boring, but most of them are awesome. It has some really neat powerups such as +100% health, invinsibility, increased damage, +200% armor, partial invisibility, a sphere that brings your health and armor to the max (200%), and a radiation suit. You start with 2 weapons, your fists, and a pistol. The other weapons, which you earn as you progress through the game are a shotgun, a chaingun, a rocket launcher, a plasma gun, and the almighty BFG 9000, this weapon is a beast and can kill multiple enemies with one hit, and it's also an easy way to quickly end a boss fight, but it is very overpowered, and might ruin the fun unless you're a psychopath, which you probably are if you can't stay away from DOOM. The gameplay is quite simple, find what you need to continue to the next map and shoot whatever is alive. No living thing here is your friend. The controls can be awkward for players, you use the up and down arrow keys to move forwards and backwards, and the left and right arrow keys to turn left and right, left control shoots, alt strafes, shift sprints, and space flicks switches and pushes buttons, they aren't rebindable. But you can still use GZDoom, which has rebindable keys mouse looking, and it allows you to move left and right. And GZDoom also quickly starts the game, which is something we should really thank the dudes who made GZDoom for because the game takes about a minute to finally get to the main menu.
TL;DR: Doom is awesome, some things can be a bit meh, GZDoom can fix some flaws. My individual rating the aspects I talked about are:
Gameplay: 10/10
Enemies: 8/10
Map design: 8/10
Music: 9/10
Weapons: 8/10
Controls: 6/10 (GZDoom fixes that)
Time to load the game: 0/10 (GZDoom makes is a 10/10)
Simplicity: 10/10
Bosses: 8/10
Powerups: 10/10
Maps: 7/10
Overall score: 7.6/10

Not sure why people rip so hard on this. Yes it's buggy. Yes, it's expensive too. But seriously, c'mon! Strategy games these days are unique and sophisticated and have all sorts of things to do in them, but they have an intense feeling of being dragged forward in time, led ahead by the nose. Even Supreme Ruler devolves into tank combat pretty fast.
And don't get me started on the whole "every good game that goes into political nitty-gritty is an Election Game" problem the strategy community has right now, in my opinion at least. There are sooo many great election simulators, but very few about actually BEING the head of state after that part, because it's complicated to put in that many life systems after all.
If you play abandonware (or were around when those titles first came out!), some games I like you may recognize are Balance of Power, Shadow President, Alter Ego, and Creatures. They're all buggy or limited in their own ways, but the important thing is that they don't try to game-ify away the feeling of a cold straight-played life simulator, which is nice sometimes.
Yes, it's hard to win in this game. Yes, it's a grindfest on par with phone games at certain moments in the gameplay. Yes, you'll get frustrated after doing everything right for half an hour that you can't seem to meet the criteria for ending/winning the current game. And bugs, who cares. This game has a TV NEWS SIMULATOR in it, for freakin sakes! You can flirt with diplomatic contacts, one-on-one, and watch the relationship develop over time with text and gifts from the person you're following around! WHO CARES IF YOU CAN'T WIN!
*coughs a little* Ahem, sorry. Got a little carried away there. I'm not an idiot of course, and it's easy to see why less than 1% of the people who buy this game might actually enjoy it. But if you enjoyed the likes of Space Station 13, Starship Corporation, FortressCraft, or even Escapists and you're looking for a light-on-strategy political simulator that's heavy on toys and doodads to click on and play with, you might like this one as long as you're not as focused on progression and winning as you are on exploring features and options.
For example, not many games of this type let you use nukes immediately, and most of them don't require you to wine and dine your military officials until they're on your side and willing to give you the launch authorization codes. I'm not saying these features stay dazzling forever, you have to try harder than usual to "make your own fun" and come up with plots and things and ideas to do, but that's my playstyle anyway. And no, it's not worth the money at all, really. It's something to get if you've got the disposable income handy, don't really "get" buyer's remorse, and want to play with a big heap of clickable buttons that let you do fun things in a modern world simulation as long as you're not pushing it too far.
Power & Revolution is a toy, not a game. Think of it more as buying a license to a software engine, but instead of it being productivity tools it's an "Earth Politics Game AI Engine" that you can interact with, built by a small team who can't fix all the bugs. And now with the God'n Spy addition, you can manually edit the game variables, making it even more that way. So, I call this a toy: An object that has moving parts, instead of a game where it's designed to help you get sucked or drawn into the experience. But if you think you might like to try the former, it's pretty dang sophisticated, at least to me. In fact I'm surprised it has as few bugs as it does, considering that the engine seems to be updating the world piece-by-piece "for real" instead of ignoring large swaths of variables until the user gets interested in a country and then "guessing" what probably happened inside of that country. (Which is what I've seen some strategy simulators try to do in order to increase framerates.)
Oh and if it runs slow? Well duh, it's supposed to. People don't seem to be used to games that have to do a lot of artificial brain calculations to work properly, but what that means is that your graphics card won't help you. Scream "unoptimized!" all you want, but I'm willing to give the benefit of the doubt that writing all of the calculations for the gameworld was hard enough without having to make the code unreadable by optimizing it too. "Real" AI engines used in commercial applications can be slow at times, too, and making them multithreaded (or use GPU acceleration, which is always proprietary even when it's not) is a pain in the butt.
If only this title could find an audience who enjoyed such things. How all the negative reviwers can't see the creativity and drive to create a unique piece of software is beyond me. P&R gets 3/5 from me just for being a special snowflake, and upgraded to 4 out of 5 stars for being such an interesting one at that. The one star removed is a combination of the bugs and the price, but I wouldn't dare take more than one star away from it because that would make it seem less amazing than it really is (to the right audience, if they ever exist and happen to notice that *this* exists).
Basically if this review didn't bore or annoy you to tears, you'll probably like it. XD

Played over 150 hours in closed alpha, tech test, closed and open betas. Took Orochi, Kensei, Valkyrie to rep 3s.
I refunded the game for the following reasons:
1) Usual "ubishit" execution. I don't really care about p2p versus servers as long as it works. Problem is that there are huge connectivity issues. In duels p2p is fine, but in 8 person dominion, someone always rage quits and it makes you reinstance, often kicking everyone out to the menu.
No proper matchmaking. If you want to try a new hero, you will queue into people with their "mains" at rep 10 with gear score 108. you have gearscore 0. The MM is based on account, not hero, which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
Often when you quit a lobby with a group, it kicks everyone from the group.
No penalties for rage quitting. If your opponent does, they are replaced by a full health bot and sometimes even a player (if he quits within the first 2 min of the match). If you're low health, that full health new opponent can kill you and win the match. Yeah...
There are many more. You can find discussions on /r/ForHonor and here:
which has a good article
2) It is my humble opinion that the game is fundamentally broken mechanically.
This is the main issue with class-based pvp games: BALANCE.
So this game was designed as a casual, console/controller based fighting game. The problem is that hardcore pvp fight players are attracted to this game, which is fine. However, they bring the mentality that you leverage efficiencies and probabilities and spam these situations to win.
In other words, you find the most broken/powerful/reliable combo or moveset your character has and you spam that until your opponent breaks down. The result is that 90% of each character's moveset/kit is neglected in favor of one or two moves.
Right now, it's Feinting to bait your opponent into parrying you, which you then parry. You then follow it up with a Guard Break and 1-2 hits. Keep in mind I said 1-2 hits, not full 3 hit chain combos (as the game wants you to do). This is because Defense in this game is SO strong that you can never reliably finish a 3 chain combo without yourself getting parried.
So the result is that people will leverage their characters' most broken and quickest interaction, then just do 1-2 light attacks then back off. Repeat process.
Combined with the fact that Defense/Parrying has no drawback, you get a ridiculous Turtle meta where no one ever attacks first and everyone does 1-3 broken mechanics.
Examples:
- Warlord: headbutt / cancel into guard break, followed by heavy. And turtle defense with shield
- Warden: Zone attack is ungodly fast (broken so you can start a light attack in another direction then quickly press heavy to do the zone attack in another direction. So the game incorrectly displays the attack direction). Vortex with shoulder bash vs shoulder bash cancel into guard break. A true 50/50 guess with no way to know which is coming.
- Peacekepper: Light attack spam. Her light attacks are faster than other characters combo chains. I could just spam light attacks + running attack and I beat very skilled Kenseis/Berserkers who I had no business beating.
- Parrying/Defense in general has no risk and is too forgiving. Hardly any stamina penalty and gives you a free guard break. High level matches are basically people spinning their stance around and then staring at each other cause attacking first has ZERO benefit in this game.
- Charge mechanics that players spam to try to push you off cliffs, but missing a charge has no drawback and you cannot charge off a cliff yourself. Makes zero sense.
-Revenge: People have 108 max gear score and can literally get revenge in only TWO blocks (you go supersaiyan and your attacks become uninterruptible and you get speed/health etc). To make things worse, revenge exists in 1v1.
In conclusion, For Honor is very similar to The Division, in that it looks great, is very addicting at first, but at high levels, it is broken mechanically because it doesn't prevent players from leveraging broken mechanics and riding those statistical certainties to victory. This is not the players' fault because they will always do anything/everything they can in-game to win. It's because the game is shallow at its core.

Where to start? This game has so many flaws I could write an entire essay about the gameplay, the community, the devs, and other things. So where is the best place to start? Clearly most reviews like to start off with the basic stuff such as the gameplay so let's start there. I do notice this is a Early Access game, but honestly, its been out for nearly four months and this is all we have so far.
The gameplay is horrific. Bugs are everywhere. Flying dead dinos along with annoying bugged hit boxes as well as texture loading problems. The graphics are alright, some stuff seems as if little attention was put into it such as some of the foliage. Also from time to time the textures will not load in which causes your enjoyment of the game to dwindle entirely. Honestly, I've seen two pixel games that are better then the Isle. The biggest weakness of this game is the fact that there is no purpose to it, you simply walk around as a dino and kill stuff, not very fun. People may have bought this game hoping that they could mate with other dinos and raise there babies, because that's what dinos do, and they also try to live. Instead, you are stuck with everything around you wanting to kill you, no matter if it is a tiny diablo or a freaking puerta. Like what the h***, herbivores hunting down and killing predators isn't normal? So you buy this game to enjoy being the top predator of the food chain, but instead you're lying dead in a pile of diablo s***. Because logic apparently. I could go on for days but instead let's move onto the dinos.
You'll be terribly disappointed to hear that the herbivores are the strongest dinos in the game, rex doesn't even make the top 3rd spot. So much for King of the Dinos, more like King of the Dryos. Since we are on the topic of rex let's move into more detail. Rex has a lot of issues, there are lots of hitbox bugs when trying to attack another rex which could get you killed in turn. Most of the time you think you have the upper hand but then the game decides you suck and let's the other player kill you somehow, even though you may have been behind it and bit it three times, it just tells you to go f*** yourself. It gets extremely frustrating because you know you have a good ping and it isn't the lag but instead it's the game itself that caused your demise. Onto the next cool dino, the allosaurus! It's basically sh**, the turning radius is about the same as a Shunt which isn't good. Rex two shots it, basically it is weak and it takes more then 6 bites to kill a rex. All in all it is not something you want to be playing right now. So up next is the Carno. The carno is fun, it's fast and agile, it is mostly for smaller prey though it can kill a puerta because that's how bada** it really is. But puerta is tough, so you may have to die four of five times before you kill the large motherf*****. Though carno isn't strong enough for a rex since the rex can turn 360 degrees with no problems and two shot the carno. For our last carnivore we have the austroraptor. It is small and quick, it isn't exactly good at killing anything, I've seen very skilled players kill larger dinos but mostly you can only kill dryos and gallis, that's about it, have fun. With all the carnivores done let us move onto the overpowered dinos who rule The Isle, the herbivores. First up we have our top predator, the Puerta! This fata** is the toughest thing you will ever see, these large dinos go on mad killing sprees killing up to 20 dinos in a single life. With so much health it can survive for a long time, but not defending itself, no instead these dinos are blood thirsty killers, sometimes they are friendly to other herbivores, sometimes not. These large beasts rule the world without a doubt. For our next extremely tough dino is the Stegosaurus. These things can kill a rex in two swipes of its tail that can bend like a snakes back. Don't question the devs because that's their logic. Honestly, you need about two to three rexes to take down one stego, it's not worth the trouble since most stegos hunt down carnivores to kill and feed from. They have been notoriously labeled, "Nazi's." As for our Shungtungasaurs they have recently been nerfed so they don't pose much of a threat except to every carnivore. These fatties don't do a whole lot, they just stomp and eat stuff, like the stegos they will chase after carnivores from time to time which gets really old seeing all these herbivores chasing carnivores. Next we have Theri, it is a cute bird that has nice long claws which it doesn't use all that much because it is usually dead before it does. They have a slow turning speed as well as a slower run from that of a galli. Mostly these things go after carnos and raptors. As I was saying about Gallis, these things are the fastest thing in the game (besides quetz that isn't out yet). They can kill a rex easily if they get behind it first, you just need patience and lots of kicks to the rex's butt. Once you have torn that rex a new a**hole you can move onto your next victim. For the Trike and Diablos they mostly do the same things, one is just the smaller then the other and does less damage. They can kill a rex relatively easy. The most deadly dino in this game by far is the Dryo, it kills with cuteness. It evades death by striking adorable cuteness in anyone's eyes. These things will f*** your life over if you end up killing them, before you know it herds of stegos will be running down the hill at you. So with the boring part of this review is done I so dearly wish to move on.
Now for the fun bits, the flippin community. It is toxic no doubt about it. Everyone yells at everyone over the dumbest things. Most of the time you find yourself in the constant face palm position that never seems to go away. One would assume most of these players are under the age of 15 so no much intelligence there, but don't get me wrong not all of them are pains in the a**, only most. Players tend to just whine and complain about things they don't like, for example someone taking there spot on this hill or quetz won't come out we will have to wait seven months. :
-	Strong narrative & interesting story;
-	Remarkable art direction;
-	Excellent sound design.
:
-	Amateurish voice acting of the main protagonist;
-	Tedious monster encounter in the later levels.
:

:
Highly recommended for any sci-fi or horror game fans, even if you’re not into the horror genre and just want to enjoy a good story. See the “Tips” section below for more details.
Upon finished SOMA, I can safely say that Frictional Games, the Swedish dev renowned for psychotic horror titles such as
and
series, has outdone themselves once again, I was amazed by how much thought was put into this game, as well as the emotional impact it creates. It’s a masterpiece in certain aspects yet falls short in others, the details are explained below in sections(*slight spoiler alert*):

:
Why SOMA isn’t your average horror game is that it puts more emphasis on the story rather than horror itself, a sci-fi fan can easily pick up the core concept of SOMA because it features similar elements from classic titles such as
,
,
and
series, yet by combining them with excellent narrative and presentation the devs still managed to create a unique feeling out of SOMA, during the gameplay I stopped more than once to think about the plot details, and watching the ending made me totally speechless for a while. The tradeoff, however, is a bit “story over gameplay” in this title and I can understand this might be frowned upon by some fans, but I applaud Frictional Games for willing to take risks in creating such a compelling experience.

:
You find yourself in an abandoned hi-tech base haunted by crazy monsters, while you have to find notes and solve puzzles to advance the story, well this is what we’ve done for 1000 times in other games. However this seamlessly fits in SOMA’s setting, as you navigate through the vintage style computer interface and read scientific reports throughout Pathos II, the story gradually unveils itself in a unique but cohesive way. My only gripe about the story is that the protagonist, despite being hinted multiple times about his ultimate fate, only to realize the situation in the last few seconds, this “dumbed down” feels forced and not clever writing.

Another feature that makes SOMA stand out is excellent in-game sound design, the ambient sound like machine beeping , distant monster groaning, suspicious noise like footsteps, as well as the water flowing sound in the sea walking levels are all amazingly done, which creates a unique, immersive and haunting feeling. The music, while I didn’t feel its existence for most part of the game, did reminds me of scores from
and
in later part, and it complements the atmosphere gloriously.
I found most of the NPC voice acting very well done and Catherine’s voice is especially brilliant, but I can’t say the same for the main protagonist’s voice: it’s unnaturally calm considering all the things happening around him, and for most part it feels like a student reading a textbook, while this more or less explains his not-so-smart mind it just takes away lots of immersion the game manages to create.

:
Slightly outdated but gets the job done fairly well, there’re some low-res textures here and there as well as color banding issues, but the game looks really beautiful during the seabed walking scenes and in the later interior levels due to the well used lighting. Early on I’ve heard lots of complaints about the game’s performance issues but in my play-through I experienced no stutter and bugs, so I guess the early issues have all been fixed.

:
As I previously mentioned, the whole Pathos II base is presented to the player with remarkable detail and authenticity, you can pick up a large variety of small objects as well as drag-open doors & drawers in a realistic way, although the physics in this game is more cosmetic and doesn’t play a vital part as in titles like Half-life 2, it adds a great amount of immersion to the gameplay.
However, the “real” gameplay is a mixed bag for me, despite walking on the seabed chased by monsters is nothing short of thrill and brilliance, and the fact that the devs tried to create a diversity of monster behaviors, the core mechanics (crouch, peek & hide) coupled with the chromatic aberration screen effect caused by panic/ monster attacks inevitably make the gameplay more like a chore than interesting interaction, especially in the later phase, like you’re in a pitch dark room but can’t use flashlight since that will immediately attract the monster, as well as some linear and uninspiring chase scene, this makes the last 1/3 part of the game more like an interactive movie and less like a video game, which is kinda disappointing.
: If you’re a fan of psychotic horror games and good story, this is a must buy for full price to support the indie developer. However if you’re less interested in the story and prefer more “hardcore” horror gameplay you may want to pick this up on sales, because the gameplay is kinda weak and game can be finished under 10 hours.

I was one of the Kickstarter backers and I was really excited about this game and have eagerly been watching the updates. I still am excited about this game but in it's current state I cannot reccomend it. There is a ton of promise but right now there are too many things that need to be fixed. Still, this is an alpha release so hopefully, with some community feedback, all of these problems will be addressed for the final release. I'll of course update this review as the game is updated.

- Beautiful astetics and pixel art
Cons:
- Tutorial does not teach the game. The learning curve is far too steep making the game frustrating and confusing to play
- Unintuitive controls. This is a mouse driven game... but the mouse does different things in different menus? Sometimes you need to right click, sometimes left click and it's seldom clear what is what...
- Bugs. There are bugs especially if you run the game full screen. The click boxes on the menu screen does not scale with resolution.
- Boring gameplay. It may be due to lack of features but the gameplay right now is rather boring and repetitive.
- Hidden Mechanics. It is very hard to determine the mechanics of the game so strategic playing is not possible. For instance, if you don't run the generator your water isn't filtered. That makes sense but there's no indication in the game that water and power are linked. I had to determine that through trial and error.
- Features are missing. Some things  promised in the Kickstarter (or shown in the Kickstarter) have not et been added and it's unknown if they will be added in the future.

It hurts. I quite enjoy minimalistic puzzle games, but I just can't recommend this one due to a large number of factors that just led to the game being unenjoyable for me (specifically visuals, audio, 'missing' features, and level design). My primary grievance was just the aesthetic of the game itself. While the whole neon theme of 'Glowing Sokoban' seemed neat in theory, in practice when coupled with the moving background it just hurt to look at after just a few consecutive levels. They did add options to disable the moving background, which I quickly toggled and left off, but this doesn't affect the title screen. Even with this off though the neon colors of the elements with a flat background hurt to look at if I played for too long in one sitting, and this detracted a lot from the game's experience.
The music also didn’t help at all. Although the game boasts '13 soundtracks', they are all fairly short loops that sound very similar and quickly became annoying. What made the music unbearable to me was the fact that a different track would be selected every time you beat a level or restarted, and it did so by very harshly cutting off the previous track and beginning the new one. On top of that, the background color scheme changes at the same time, which furthers the visual grievances I mentioned above. When I turned off the dynamic backgrounds, I also muted all the music of the game.
The game is also lacking in a few gameplay features that I would have expected. There is no level select option, each level just leads to the next. If you load up a save once you've beaten all the levels it just takes you to the end game screen from where you can only return to the main menu, so at any time you can only ever access the next level in an existing save or create a new save. The game had a reset level option (bound to 'r', as seemed natural), but there was no button to step back a single move (which I would have expected on 'backspace'). To make that issue worse, not every input would be registered, so when moving along a long path, I would often stop too early and ruin the level because some key presses were lost, and without a backspace option I was forced to then restart the level. When completing a level, it would sometimes take a few seconds to register the victory, and during that time if you moved a piece you could be forced into a state where you have to start completely over (this happened once to me). And while the game describes itself as "You need to place all the blue rings on the red squares at the least number of moves", the number of moves taken is completely irrelevant. It does track how many move you make, but there is no incentive to minimize that, unless you want to go back and one-up yourself (which you'll need to start a new playthough and beat all levels up to that point to even attempt).
The levels design also seemed lacking. The levels were of a huge variety of difficulties, and mildly difficult levels would be sometimes followed with several trivially easy ones. Among the 60 levels, a few were at least mildly challenging, and a single one had me stumped for around 20 minutes. Even the hard levels didn't feel satisfying to complete, the difficulty just felt like an annoyance. Many of the levels would also have portions that were pointless, like pieces that started in their goal position and never moved or unusable areas of the map. This led to levels that have numerous possible solutions, and many where the solution was visually obvious from the moment the level was presented. Take for example level 27:
The one square at the top is completely unusable, but so is the entire section to the right of the map. Not only is it pointless, but with the mechanics of the game, it is fundamentally unusable. Things like these lead most levels to have sections that just go unused and don't add to the game in any way.
With the dynamic background and audio disabled, it is a passable puzzle game, and the fundamental mechanics do work, despite the missing features that one would expect from a game such as this, so it is probably best to give this game a pass. Even though it is cheap, your money could be spent much better elsewhere.

I made a very risky purchase yesterday with this game. I had heard good things from YouTubers like Kailvin and CommisarBro, but bad things from the rest of the community. I decided to buy this game and I thought that if I didn't like it I could just get a refund. I ended up playing it for 5 hours straight. Now I think the game overral is good but there are a few things that need to be fixed and patched.
Pros :
- Play as any country, terrorist organization or political party
- In depth economic and political system
- Choose how to run your country
- Each country responds with realistic response to political reforms, so for example let's say you play as Iran, a country with Sharia law, enacting laws and reforms that are secular or laws that go against religion will make the poplution unhappy, while playing as a secular country like Germany or Britain, secular laws will make the population more happy
- The city battles are pretty cool too, as you can actually command units around the city to hold key buildings or major chokepoints
- Military action will have consequences around the world if you make the wrong decisions, like bombarding a city will rocket artillery
- The parody names can be pretty clever sometimes, like Jack Ohama.
- You can now play as revolutionaries, like play as pro democratic rebles in North Korea, and secular rebels in countries like Iran.
Cons :
- A pretty obvious one, the voice acting is awful
- AI can be dumb or buggy, for example, I was playing as democratic Qatar rebels and I stormed the city palace. I had around 10 units in there and 3 enemy units walked in and killed 7 of mine because they didn't know how to react until I did manual commands
- The game is poorly optimized. Now I'll admit I don't have the best PC in the world, but if I can run Battlefield 4 as decent framerate on average settings I should be able to run this game on ultra settings, but I can't
- The tutorial isn't very good so the learning curve is very steep, I spent a few hours alone trying to learn how to navigate through menus, learning how to move military units on the campaign map and how to handle economics
-  The revolutionaries mode needs some patching. It's a cool idea and it's fun to play, but it's very difficult to gain support from other countries, funding, and men to fight for your cause. I found myself trying to sway countries to help me most of the time rather than actually starting protests or fighting.
Overral the game is good, and if you like simulations and don't mind the hefty price tag, this is a must buy, but for everyone else I'd wait until the developer patches the game to fix the dumb battle AI and fixes the optimazation. That is, if he fixes it.

Gameplay posted here.
Power & Revolution is a politically oriented game that puts you as the Prime Minister/President/King of a country. This is deeply detailed, with controllable statistics such as crime rate and graduation rates to your military and your foreign policy. You control the country. You propose laws which can free the shackles of tyranny or use Obama's last months to lock him a spot as the eternal president.
P&R is developed by a third-party company by the name of Eversim. They produced games such as Commander-in-Chief, Masters of the World, and Rulers of Nations. They detail their games with extrordinary detail, and each game brings something new. GPS4 is the pinnical of their development, learning from their mistakes they made with GPS3.
Pros:
-More playability
-Updated, fixed of bugs
-Minute by minute basis
-City view, fight military or riots in here. Gain money from taking museams or banks.
-Expanded political system. Includes billionares, fundraising for party, etc.
-Better ways to find out who wants what. Polls can be taken to see if a bill will pass and what the people think.
-Less bugs
Cons:

-Expansion of last game, only changed interface
-Some bugs may break game function, but not as prevelent as last game
-Multiplayer not included, will come in future expansion
The game also features many new things. Natural disasters can occur such as disease and famine. Chemical and biological weapons can be used. Casualties can be seen to see how many have died in your conflict.
I personally recommend the game. GPS4 is worth the investment!

I wanted to like this game. I expected it to be a scary, good executed game like Slender, since they're both based on Creepypastas. Sadly, this game came nowhere near good.
Correct me if I'm wrong, but each day takes an hour. A real hour. In real life. If you want to go through a whole day, good luck. You can sleep during the day, but not during the night, as you need to hunt down Rake.
During the day, you set up cameras and traps. At night, you look at those cameras, with gameplay stolen straight form Five Night's at Freddy's. I'm not a fan of FNAF, and even if you are a fan of it, this game is still boring. You sit there for thrity minutes, doing absoltely nothing, but staring at nothing. At least in FNAF, there were other things you had to keep track of, and the animatronics were a constant threat.
Of course, if you choose to go outside to find Rake, things get a little more interesting. The dark amospher and creepy sound effects are well done. You will get scared at the sound of footsteps, thinking it's Rake, but it's a boar. It's fun and creepy. Until you actually see Rake. Since the graphics aren't the greatest, he doesn't look all that intimidating. And he follows the same attack pattern every time. You can easily take him down if you figure it out.
The nights would actually be okay if you could do something else. This game should've had more survival gameplay. You don't need to get food, or drink water, or pretty much do anything. All you have is a health bar. At night, all you can do is stare at cameras for a boring time, walk outside for a little fun, or walk around your claustrophobic mobile home. You can't cook any food to eat, drink water, or anything fun.
2/10 Slenderman is better, and it's free. If this game was free, it might've gone up to a 3/10

My story:
Life in our little town was relatively peaceful and slow going.  My wife and I started some small business and supply lines and slowly worked our way up the social ladder. We made our fair share of enemies along the way, due to no fault of our own other than our slowly growing success and monopolizing of the business estates in town.
Along the way we had our son "Ordo."  Ordo wasn't a particularly special boy.  His schooling was poor due to our lack of funds and title at the time, but he did his best and eventually grew old enough to be handed the reigns of a small bakery.
Ordo had a bit of a problem though...he was very clumsy.
At the age of 26, while courting his wife, he sprained his ankle on 2 separate occasions while strolling through the town with her, requiring medical intervention each time. Fortunately he never lost her favor (possible due to his wealthy family and her lower class...) and ultimately married her.
Then on the night of their wedding, while consumating their marriage and trying for a child, somehow Ordo managed to break a bone. The problem was that there wasn't any medical facility of a high enough level in town to heal his wound. So Ordo, after breaking a bone while boning, shortly after midnight in the middle of winter... had to make the grueling trudge to the big city on the other side of the map to try to see an experienced Dr.

He nearly made it... but unfortunately succumbed to his wounds just outside of the hospital.
Luckily enough those few hours of marriage resulted in a beautiful baby girl who grew up and went on to college becoming a schollar and a doctor. When she came of age, she built a great hospital in our small little town so no one would ever have to die boning again and no more children would be left fatherless.
9/10 would experience awkward deaths again.

If you love Dead by Daylight you will love this game. There are some pros and cons right now you should know about though.
-Survivors can't run forever which was one of the annoying and unrealistic thinks about DbD (although I know it isn't meant to be realistic).
-The map doesn't favor one or the other. I think the chasing portion was done pretty well and Jason is slow to run giving you plenty of time to find a way to defend yourself.
-The map is big and randomized every time ensuring every game is completely different.
-Jason is great to play with. I love smashing through doors, smashing windows, setting traps and executing survivors. His executions are very satisfying and there's plenty of ways to kill your prey. Smashing them into walls and doors, throwing them in and out of windows, crushing their windpipe, (which are both very easy to do making it unfair for councelors) and once progression is fixed there will be plenty more to see and do. I can't wait!
-Survivor reactions to other player deaths have made me jump multiple times and I think this is a great addition.
-Every Jason and survivor has upsides and downsides further making every game different.
-A few ways to escape: Call the cops and wait, repair the cars and/or boats available to drive away or survive for a full 20 minutes.
-Killing with Jason is way too easy. Just simply pick someone up, wait 3 seconds and instant death is available. It would be better for that to take a lot more time to charge up. That should be available at the halfway point or around the last 5 minutes.
-Some stun times are too short. With knives I think it's about where it should be. He takes it out and he can't run for a few seconds afterwards giving plenty of time. Guns wounds however are easier. Jason falls and you mash E to get back up which takes about 5-6 seconds. It should be a much bigger penalty for that.
-While combat isn't meant to be a survivor strongpoint and all stats are different I feel that it's virtually impossible to fight Jason off. When you hit him he doesn't flinch. Unless you have a gun (or unless he's picking someone up and you have a window) you're screwed. If there's going to be survivor combat they should be a tad better. Then again, I can't unlock the others yet as the progression is currently broken.
As it stands now I expected problems and I'm still having a blast. Just like Dead by Daylight, it isn't perfect and needs tweaks. If you're a diehard fan of Dead by Daylight or horror in general like me  I'd say the $40 is worth it. If not, stay away for now. The devs already worked on one immediate issue and care about the game and the game is already more stable than Dead by Daylight ever was. Thumbs up so far for me!
Day one problems are fixed and the game is great. Like with Dead by Daylight there are moments where things just don't seem to make sense but with how unpredictable this game is it topples Dead by Daylight with ease! Once you know what you're doing, the game plays pretty fair most of the time. While some don't agree, I only stand by my words further now that this game is indeed worth double the price of DbD. You will run into a select few jerks and morons like all online games but a quick mute does the trick!
As long as you have a team that is willing to work together you have a much better chance at escaping or by the very least surviving longer. You will run into complete d-bags that only hide, run away when they can clearly help or act like they're perfect and tell you that you suck or even possibly try and team kill you. It adds to the variety at least though.

Tired of playing dinosaurs games where you do everything except play as a dinosaur? then The Isle is here for you. one of the few dinosaur games in the world that allows you to play as a dino, The Isle allows you to take control of a large selection of prehistoric animals from the T-Rex, to Triceratops, all the way down Gallimimus. explore a world designed to kill you as you compete with other players who want to survive as much as you do.
One thing you should know is that this game is still in development so there is still much that has not been finished yet. the game will have a large selection of dinosaurs to choose from once they are all finished. there will even be Humans in this game, both modern day man using guns and tribal men native to the island. both will be able to capture and tame dinosaurs. but Humans have not been added yet so you will not be able to play as them right now. but when they are added, it'll be a fun experience to feel like you're playing The Lost World: Jurassic Park. but playing as the Humans will be optional so one day you could be Online and run into your friend who's playing as a dinosaur while you're a Human. awesome right? :D
The game is open world free roam like Skyrim and Fallout. go any where you want when ever you want. but just to let you know there is no map and so you have to read coordinates to find your way around or else you're going to get lost. from what I understand, the Humans will have maps and even a selection of several vehicles to travel around the island quickly. from trucks, helicopters, and even military weapons. traveling on foot will create less noise to attract dinosaurs but you'll be vulnerable and easily killed. so you need to think before you leave your camp into the jungle or else you'll be an easy target for those who are playing as dinosaurs.
There are no aliens, dragons, or any magical creatures in this game. this is just straight up dinosaurs on a dinosaur island. but there will be something called, "The Strains" that will be added in the future. I haven't seen much info on them, but from what I hear they are supposed to be mutated dinosaurs like the ones from Dino Crisis 3. so there will be fictional creatures in the future.
There will be something called a Progression System added sometime in the future that allows you to level up the dinosaur you're playing as. increase your health, attack, and stamina until you're top of the food chain as the apex.
Once all dinosaurs have been finished, no where on the map will be safe. the land will have T-Rexes and Raptors, the rivers will have Titanoboas and Deinosuchuses, the air will have Quetzalcoatlus and Pteranodons, and even the oceans will have Mosasaurs and Dunkleosteus. keep alert at all times or else you'll be someone's dinner.
But like I said, this game is still in development and so a few things I talked about are not available at the moment. but if you're looking for a video game where you play as a dinosaur in a world of dinosaurs, I suggest you give The Isle a try.

So you're a guy named Simon who is from Toronto. One day you get your brain case scanned because you suck at driving and suddenly you wake up the next moment in the middle of the ocean. So it's like blacking out from drinking and finding out you signed up for the navy. The next third of the games story proceeds to give you no context other then "monsters like your bum so try to find this lady and gtfo." Then suddenly the game is like "I'm gonna make you question your whole belief system and make you wonder about the human soul" while you take breaks between uncomfortable monster hugs and reaching for your Doritos. Sheltered is an old school (graphics wise) title about keeping your family and other refugees alive in an underground vault. The title has been bombarded with comparisons to "Fallout shelter", despite numerous fans pointing out that Sheltered was an idea on Kickstarter almost (if not more than) a year ago.
A big portion of the game is resource management, with players directing each bunker resident to fix this or upgrade that or interact with this object. At the start of the game you start with an oxygen filter, water filter, 1 water storage container, a geiger counter (to see how much radioactivity is in the bunker? just a guess), a radio/map for organizing scavenging/raiding parties and hazmat suits for leaving the bunker to repair the filters and set traps for wildlife as well as a generator and 2 storage containers for food and other resources.
Players can use the workbench (also provided at the start) to rearrange the various items around the bunker instantly as well as craft new items (which include everything from gasmasks to toilets;traps for wildlife;showers and beds to name a few) Interaction with the outside world is done in 'expeditions', where players get an overview of the outside world. from this they assign 'waypoints' that survivors travel between, searching for new locations (such as bodies of water, houses or hospitals) to search through as well as finding new survivors to trade with, attack or recruit to join your bunker.
that while I HIGHLY recommend this title, there are a few minor bugs/balance issues that need to be addressed. The largest one i've noticed being that residents seem to get food poisoning EXTREMELY often, Even if you're constantly cleaning. Once that is addressed, I would openly encourage anyone and everyone to try out this title.

This game is mediocre and it's the fault of the sub-genre more than the game itself. So YMMV if you love the sub-genre.
I've always thought this game was a bit over rated. It's not terrible, or even bad, but at the time it came out people kept going on about how it was absolutely terrifying and incredible great, and it's not either one.
My reasoning comes down to some basic issues with the mechanics of this specific sub-genre of games. These are horror games with puzzles, stealth and zero combat. The problem is fear comes from risk and the perception of risk. Since you literally can not fight any of the foes in this game they have to be non-threatening enough that you can just walk away from them. There just isn't much range of response for your character to make, or much decision for you as the player. And the game has to be designed around this lack of options. It can't corner you with an enemy, because you can't so much as shove one away. So anywhere you could get trapped there will be no enemies. Or there will be a conspicuously placed hiding place for when the scripted enemy walks in. A horror walking simulator doesn't really work. The scariest game I ever played was System Shock 2, because you had to go into creepy situations and not know if you could handle it even if you had an assault rifle. In Amnesia you always know you can...because ironically your character can't handle anything...so there has to be nothing much to handle.
Eventually you realize that 'scary' things in the game boil down to two categories:
Haunted House Shenanigans - Flickering lights, rumbles and shaking, misc spookiness that amount to nothing.
Monsters - Which you walk around and trot away from, or hide inside a wardrobe from twiddling your thumbs until they wander off.
I know this is unfair, because it came first, but it's like a bargain basement version of Alien Isolation. Because in that game there's more you can do, even if you're still mostly facing a threat that is ultimately undefeatable and can only be escaped from momentarily.

Quake 2 is my favorite shooter. I love (almost) everything about it. From the opening level to the final boss there is always something that I appreciate and love every time I play.
Progression is something that is important to me, a feeling of a changing world as your move through the game. Quake 2 is easily in a whole different world with this. Every "Unit" of the game is spearated into a hub world and connecting levels that you go through to complete a variety of objectives. As you continue through the hub world and complete the various objectives, the hub level changes. The best example is in the power plant Unit at the the half way point of the game. As you turn off the coolant for the reactor and turn on the pumps for the toxic waste the actual Reactor Factory you go through falls apart as you run quickly to the exit. It is honestly one of the most sastifying feelings knowing that you are literally changing the world as you go through it. The hub structure of the game does more than just provide a look into your progression, it also serves to make the world feel huge and expansive. From the mission briefing screen before you are put into the Unit until the exit button at the end of the unit it all feels like one huge level. Sure, there are loading screens throughout it but they are so small and come at predictable and understandable times that it makes everything feel seamless.
The combat is also satisfying. The AI (While somewhat silly in some places) is suprisingly complex for the time. For example, the Berserker enemy will activley dodge your grenades that you throw at him (sure it hits him sometimes but he tries to dodge) and other enemies like the Enforcers duck from your bullets. The enemies also give out unique sounds so you know exactly who you are facing against, and if you are about to face them. For example, the parasite (a dog/spider hybrid looking freak) makes a very weird tapping sound while you are near him (but doesn't see you) so you can easily activley know that you will not only be facing a Parasite shortly, but also that he is hiding. With 11 weapons there is always something that takes out certain enemies better than others. This game even introduced the now legendary Railgun.
The level design is top notch. Every Unit of the game (of which there are 10) have unique designs that let you know exactly where you are. Sure, they mostly are inside factory areas, however they all look different enough to let the player know exactly what point in the game they are at. For example, the Bunker unit (2nd) is a very storage facility type place with boxes everywhere and a very storage type feeling to it. Meanwhile the Power Plant unit (6th) uses very bright powerful colors to show that you are in a place that powers your target, Big Gun (one of the main objectives in the entire game) Secrets also litter the levels which give players goodies, some are harder to find then others but they are all imensly satisfying to find. There are even three levels that are hidden from the player, each varying in length but all have somthing unique about them, from low gravity to a very harsh timelimit to grab as much ammo as you can.
The only issues I can thing of are the boss fights. There are 3 total bossfights in the game and they are all awful. The bosses do not have enough health to provide much of a challenge. Amnesia was, without a doubt, a landmark game. It forever changed the face of horror games and the genre is still feeling its impact to this day. Frictional games truly understands the key elements to creating real horror: Not in having things jump out at the player with loud sting music blaring but with subtlety and mechanics that never allow the player to get too comfortable.
One of the key elements to creating a true horror experience is making the player feel vulnerable. Nothing is scary when you’re armed with a rocket launcher, a minigun, three different kinds of shotguns, and enough ammunition to start a revolution. Amnesia accomplishes this by removing weapons altogether. You as the player have no way to defend yourself apart from running and hiding. The monsters that hunt you are always a danger, from start to finish.
Another core tenet of good horror is that your imagination is always far worse than reality. Hence, you are strongly discouraged from looking at the monsters in the game. If you look directly at any of the creatures, your screen distorts and you begin to lose “sanity”, which will eventually result in the monster finding you. You’ll find yourself on more than one occasion staring at a wall and praying that the lumbering sound of its footsteps is moving away from you and not closer.
The Resident Evil style puzzles offer something of a respite from the more intense portions of the game, following the tried and true formula of “tension and release”.
Really, though, the harshest criticism that I can level against this game is that it was too influential for its own good. Games like Outlast and Alien: Isolation have taken this concept to new levels. Consequentially, I just don’t find it as scary as it once was. If you haven’t played it and you’re enjoy being scared, definitely give this a try.

Amnesia: The Dark Descent is a horror game in which you sneak about and hide from murderous monsters while exploring an old structure. You could apply that description to the majority of horror games, but I actually found this one to be entertaining and genuinely creepy. If you want to kill things, this game probably won't satisfy. I love blowing baddies away, but I find that running and hiding is quite exciting, too, and Amnesia: The Dark Descent does a good job illustrating that.
The enemies look freaky coming at you from the dark, though technically their design is a little goofy. To avoid the player from getting too accustomed to their appearance in-game, the dev had the clever idea of triggering fear in the player character if you look right at the enemies. If you see them, glance away and run or hide, so that you don't suffer ill effets.
It's a pretty short game, but I find that short works better for horror. I really wish that Alien Isolation was half its length, or at least a bit shorter than what it is. I really like that game, but when you drag out horror, it doesn't work as well, in my opinion. I will say that the plot was a bit weird, with a final encounter that was even weirder still. This was a case of a game where the plot wasn't the major driving factor for me, which is pretty impressive, since that's usually a massive part ofwhat keeps me invested in a game.

The game is fantastic, just like I expected. I personally don't have an iOS or Android device, so I wasn't able to play the game prior to its PC release.
This game simulates rapid close quarter engagements from a top down view. You as the player controls a squad of elite counter-terrorist forces. Using careful movement and tactics, your goal is to move throughout a building complex and eliminate all hostiles as fast as possible.
The different factions you can play as gives me a really nice immersive feel when I give my men orders. It's not just an aesthetic thing either, every faction has a different stat bonus. For example, the British SAS specializes in Evasion.
If you're looking for a good top-down tactical shooter (or disappointed with Black Ops II's Strike Force missions), this is most definitely for you. Do not jump into this game thinking you can force your men in rooms like supermen and expect them to go gun blazing, killing terrorists.
My only gripe with this game is that the game freezes up my computer during the after action reports, forcing me to use task manager to close the game. Devs, get this nuisance out of the way, periodically update it with new content, and you have yourself a AAA quality indie game.

Now this is the one everybody remembers.  If you played a PC game in 1995, you played Doom.  Everyone played Doom.  Companies had to institute rules and ban Doom from being played during business hours, because too many employees were playing deathmatches.  Doom was so popular that Microsoft developed a port of it to work on their new Windows 95, in hopes of getting more people to buy the operating system, this of course after Bill Gates toyed with the idea of buying out ID Software all together.
But even with its popularity, there was the mounds of controversy.  Some hated it for its high levels of blood and gore, others for its satanic symbols.  Groups tried to ban it, tried to get it out of the public eye, blamed it for school shootings and random acts of violence.  Many tried to connect it to violent behavior in young adults, citing the violence learned in the game being brought to reality.  But through all of this it stood tall, exactly what it was, simply a game.
Doom is one of those classics that everyone needs to experience   You don’t have to play the whole thing, or beat every level under par.  But every gamer, that wants to truly be a gamer, should spend a little time running around the halls of the UAC facility on the Mars moon.

This Game is a perfect Example for a good Idea badly realised.
You start with a single workshop and are bound to build an Empire.
But You should be very carefull, which Craft You choose, because there are many worksops very dependend on the Market for raw materials - and this Market only has wares someone produces, that means You or Your KI-Opponent. But the KI is so bad, that some wares are never produced at all and so your workshop soon goes out of materials and becomes bankrupt.
The KI for Automanagement is even worse (on Autoselling and -producing, the KI even sells the raw materials needed for crafting, so Your workers will be without work and You again will be bankrupt), so You have to do the mikromanagment on Your own - all the time. This may be nice at the beginning, when You have only one shop, but already in the midgame You will have about 5 to 7 shops, and neither of them will work, if You dont sell and buy and produce every Item by Yourself.
But even if You are ready to play a Game like that, even You like the mikromanagment, I Wouldnt recommend the Game. Because You need to do the Mikromanagment of Your family, too. Find a mate, educate your children and so on - and of course become elected in court, visit the doctor, eat, drink, sleep, all of it at the same time. And a lot of the features arent even explained or seem to have an effect. So none of my characters has ever eaten, because there are no negative effects, at least none I could see.
With all of this to do, im lacking the Game "Guid". A  Game where you had to raise money to fight Your opponent via intrigue, violence and trickery.
The foundation for a good Game is there - the economic processes are quite nice and it is fun to bring your first shop to maximum level. But by then the KI of Your opponents and the catastrophic and suicidal automanaging-processes destroy every fun.
If You wanna play "The Guild" wait for the Guild III or play "The Guild I" Not this. spare Your 10 bucks.
